author: Arezu Fayyazi
title: Afghan Women Are Restricted, But They Cannot Be Silenced. They Continue to Be Agents of Change in Afghanistan.
content:
Afghan women have been living under one of the most repressive systems in the world, as the Taliban continue to impose restrictive edicts – over 160 in total to date. These orders restrict their ability to work, attend school, move freely and even leave their homes without a male guardian. Yet despite the barriers the Taliban have imposed, Afghan women continue to be at the forefront of efforts to build peace and stability in Afghanistan.

Peace and security extends beyond just political conversations. They also include the “daily strategies Afghan women employ to defend human rights and generate conditions for peace.” According to a report by the Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace, and Security, 81% of Afghan women participate in efforts focused on women’s and girl’s education, 64% in economic empowerment, and another 54% in health & reproductive rights and services. Afghan women are also engaged in health and reproductive rights and services, by roughly 9%, compared to women from other regions of South Asia.

These figures demonstrate the perseverance, leadership, and problem solving of Afghan women. Afghanistan is facing a reproductive health crisis, with maternal mortality rapidly increasing since the Taliban took over in 2021. The loss of international funding and organizational support has also greatly affected the reproductive health programs. To help fill these gaps and address the mounting health issues facing women and girls, Afghan women have stepped in to provide critical support and services.

This sense of responsibility extends beyond just responding to immediate needs; it reflects the determination of Afghan women to protect and strengthen their communities despite the restrictions imposed on them. While many formal opportunities for education, employment, and political participation have been taken away after 2021, women have continued to find ways to serve their communities. For example, they have established online schools, supported women’s access to healthcare services, organized community-based initiatives, and advocated for women’s rights.

The significant role women continue to play in activities that promote peace and security demonstrate that resilience is not just their ability to endure oppression. It is also the ability to adapt, organize, and create solutions especially in an environment that has been designed to limit their every move and every opportunity.

Their resilience is particularly significant because many of these efforts occur in an environment where women are already facing risks to their lives. Their actions demonstrate their collective responsibility, where women have repeatedly stepped forward to address unmet needs themselves.

Their resilience also challenges the perception of Afghan women in the media solely as victims of the Taliban restrictions imposed on them. While challenges of these restrictions are severe, Afghan women have found ways to find space and operate within them. They are evidence that resilience can take many forms.

Their efforts demonstrate that, even under deeply restrictive circumstances, Afghan women continue to shape the social fabric of their communities and contribute to building a more stable and peaceful Afghanistan. This is also evident in how Afghan women see and define themselves. Among women working in the peace and security field, 65% of women describe themselves as activists while 37% of them describe themselves as human rights defenders. As one activist explained, “As an activist woman, I am not a victim of war, but an architect of social peace, and this is a voice that must be heard globally.”

Their work in education, healthcare, economic empowerment, and community development demonstrates that Afghan women are not simply recipients of aid or victims of conflict, they are powerful agents of change. Their persistence and leadership are an important source of strength for their communities and a reminder that peacebuilding in Afghanistan cannot succeed without the full participation of Afghan women at the table.

author: Elizabeth Weill-Greenberg
title: Activists Are Pushing Cities and Companies to Cancel Parking Contracts With ICE
content:
The Trump administration’s abduction and deportation machine is multifaceted. There are clear-cut components — agents, shackles, and jails — and less obvious, although no less essential, ones — cars and parking spaces.


In an effort to impede the attacks on immigrants, mayors of some of the country’s largest cities, including

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani

,

Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson

, and

Boston Mayor Michelle Wu

, have issued executive orders

banning Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)

 from using city-owned parking lots and properties.


But even in cities where mayors have banned ICE from using government-owned properties, ICE still has free reign to contract with private companies. After the federal agency

posted a notice

 seeking “Surge Parking” in 14 cities, including Boston, Wu

released a public letter

 to

local parking garage and lot owners

, warning them that if ICE were “to procure such resources, it would constitute an unprovoked and unwarranted escalation, creating potentially significant risks to public safety and halting economic activity across our entire region.”


“Today, I ask you to join us: Reject any proposition by ICE to facilitate an attack on the people of Boston,”

she wrote

. “In the face of escalating attacks on cities across the country, we have repeatedly seen that the strongest defense is solidarity.”


In the Boston suburb of Burlington, Massachusetts, Bearing Witness New England has been holding weekly protests outside ICE’s Boston Field Office, where people are

held for days

 in inhumane conditions. Activists say ICE has been keeping its vehicles in a nearby parking lot owned by local developer National Development.


According to a report by

NPR

 affiliate

WBUR

, the company sent a letter to local activists in February, stating that ICE vehicles were being “improperly parked” in its parking spaces, and that it had “reached an arrangement with ICE that they would no longer park their vehicles on our property.”


However, the company also said that the government agency, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), has

rights to use the garage

 and the company does not have authority over how the FAA parcels out parking spaces to other federal agencies, according to

WBUR

’s report.


Nathan Phillips, a Boston University professor who organizes with the Burlington-area coalition

Building Up Resilience Networks (B.U.R.N.)

, says ICE has continued to park in sections of lots National Development leases to the FAA that exceed what the lease allows.


Protests that target parking garages are “throwing sand in the gears” of ICE’s deportation and abduction machine, he says.


“So much of their operation depends on logistics of transport and travel,” Phillips told

Truthout

. “It’s human trafficking, and so if we can go after the trafficking, the means by which they’re doing this, that can have a really effective impact.”


The Appeal in Your Inbox


Subscribe to our newsletters for regular updates, analysis and context straight to your email.


          Sign Up


Fellow B.U.R.N. activist Josh Model says National Development’s recent actions contradict its public image as a

philanthropic company

 committed to improving communities.


“National Development Corporation, which, as a local developer, likes to promote that they’re cognizant of community needs and give to charity and all these nice things,” but they’re “letting ICE stage kidnappings” from their property, said Model.


While the government spending website,

usaspending.gov

, only lists 12 active contracts for parking spaces, as of September 28, the true number of parking lots that ICE uses is likely much higher, said Model. It’s difficult to untangle where ICE is parking, in part, because many of the contracts are not with ICE, but through another federal agency, the

General Services Administration

 (GSA), he said. The GSA manages government buildings and real estate, and owns or leases space in more than 8,300 buildings, according to an

explainer

 on the agency published by the Congressional Research Service.


In the case of National Development, ICE is using parking leased by the GSA for the FAA, according to Model.

PPA website

author: Valerie Anne
title: Lili Reinhart Wants To Adapt a Lesbian Vampire Novella — Let Her!
content:
feature image photo by Emma McIntyre / Staff via Getty Images

Bisexual baddie Lili Reinhart has been on a press tour for her new film, The Love Hypothesis, and I’ve been really enjoying her interviews. The film seems to be the CLASSIC fake dating trope come to life — in fact, the book it’s based on started as Star Wars fanfic! — and despite the movie being seemingly extremely heterosexual, on this tour, she has been quick to remind interviewers and fans that she’s queer. She has also said she hopes in her next project is gay. (Fingers crossed!)

In one video interview she says, “I’m instantly way more interested in doing a movie if my character is a little gay,” she continued. “Because I’m a little gay.” She also reads a comment about being one of “the five pillars of bisexuality with preference to women” and she called it an honor.

In that same interview, she also mentioned that she’s trying to get a film adaptation of a lesbian vampire novella made but that Hollywood seems “too afraid” to make it. She also wonders aloud who WOULDN’T want to make it, a sentiment I agree with. The general assumption people have been making is that it would be an adaptation of the 1872 novella Carmilla, which the popular webseries starring Natasha Negovanlis and Elise Bauman was based on, and I think that would be fun if true. I personally think there can’t be too many adaptations of that novella. The gayer the better. In fact, I just read Hungerstone by Kat Dunn, which is one of a few retellings of that novella and offers a very different take than the webseries.

I, for one, am delighted that Lili keeps making her press tour about a heterosexual love story as queer as she can, and I’m glad she’s using it to pitch her idea. I really hope someone with the means is paying attention and can pick it up and let her run with it.

In my opinion, there’s no such thing as too many lesbian vampire adaptations in general. When is someone going to make a Bury Our Bones in the Midnight Soil miniseries? A movie version of A Long Time Dead, anyone? Let’s get all the lesbian vampires out here while we’re at it. Tis the season!

author: Eileen Flanagan
title: How to combat fear at the polls this November
content:
This article

How to combat fear at the polls this November

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


The ophthalmologist said he was going to touch my eyeball, then tilted my exam chair back in the darkness. I felt my body brace as movie torture scenes flashed through my mind. I noticed that I wasn’t breathing, so I practiced inhaling through my nose, and exhaling as steadily as I could for the rest of the exam.


Noticing our bodies and breathing intentionally may sound simple, but they are two of the practices that can keep us grounded when we are navigating scary or upsetting situations. As we approach a midterm election marred by threats of violence, I am practicing these skills as often as possible, not to suppress my feelings, but to be aware of how they are affecting me, so I can make conscious choices. 


Why staying grounded matters


The forces of authoritarianism want us to feel knocked off center by the many ways they are trying to keep people from voting. Trump administration officials continue to suggest that ICE, FBI or other federal agents could be sent to polling places. It’s important that election volunteers and voters stay grounded to avoid playing into their hands. One danger is that fearful voters will just stay home, whether or not the administration carries out their threats. Another danger is that we resist any government interference in ways that increase the chaos, which Trump would use to bolster his narrative that the left is the real threat.


Many national and local groups are hosting trainings to prepare people to protect our vote calmly and nonviolently. A widely used tool is the “

Election Defense Scenarios

” guide, which sketches out 18 possible threats and what people can do about them. Author

Daniel Hunter

 writes, “One of the clearest lessons from every scenario in this guide — and from democratic movements around the world — is this: Illegal and unjust orders only work if people comply with them.” He notes that a more subtle theme of the guide is handling fear. For example, those volunteering at the polls should make sure we do not become “vectors of fear” by spreading unfounded rumors.


Sign up for the latest updates.


Support Us


I learned the danger of rumors in 2020. Weeks before the presidential election, my friend Ingrid Lakey heard that the neo-fascist Proud Boys were coming to a park near her home in Philadelphia. Despite growing up as

George Lakey

’s daughter, and years of training for nonviolent direct action with Earth Quaker Action Team, or EQAT, Ingrid did not feel prepared to de-escalate armed militants if they wanted to stir up trouble. Neither did I, though given the times, we both wanted to increase our ability to handle scary situations. With two other friends from EQAT, we decided to show up, not to intervene, but to see what we could learn. 


We met early for a few minutes of silent Quaker worship and named our intention to observe what happened, including inside ourselves. We walked to the park early and watched hundreds of people arrive, none wearing MAGA hats. When the crowd’s energy became frenzied, we asked people nearby what was happening and were told there was a Proud Boy with a bat. Later we heard it was a hockey stick, or maybe a gun. 


The four EQAT members helped each other to assess what was actually happening rather than get caught up in the fearful energy. In the end, the Proud Boys never actually showed up, but the rumor of their presence led a small crowd to chase a man into his car. Within a few days, a video of his window being smashed got millions of views on conservative social media.


If a similar video emerges this election season, there is no doubt that Trump and the media that support him would use it to claim that leftists are the true threat to the vote, distracting from his many efforts to stop people from voting. Even if armed agents do show up near polling places, managing our fear will help us choose responses that will aid us both in court and in the court of public opinion. 


If Election Day turns out to be relatively uneventful — if our fear was the point, and the armed men never show — preparing ourselves for the worst-case scenarios will build nonviolence skills and relationships between organizations. Both will be important in the work ahead, no matter who wins the midterms.    


We have more experience than we realize


The good news is that many more Americans have learned the value of …

title: Flávio Bolsonaro e o risco de um presidente com esqueletos no armário
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Xeque na Democracia, enviada toda segunda-feira, 12h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui.


O Brasil que sai do primeiro turno está flertando com uma crise institucional permanente. Flávio Bolsonaro teve 2,2 milhões de votos a mais que Lula, ficando em 47% dos votos versus 45,1% do atual presidente.

Se eleito, Flávio teria uma bancada de 28 nomes no Senado e 121 na Câmara dos Deputados apenas do PL, seu partido, um desempenho histórico. 


Mas

Flávio Bolsonaro é um candidato com muitos esqueletos no armário. Está enredado em vários escândalos e corrupção

 dos quais, hoje, conseguimos ter apenas um vislumbre, mas que vão se aprofundar nos próximos meses. E

isso levará necessariamente a um governo maculado por revelações do seu primeiro ao seu último dia. 


A jornalista Flávia de Oliveira

chamou

 a atenção para o fato de que,

por conta da ação de


André Mendonça


de manter sigilo do caso Master, Flávio é o único candidato investigado por corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e evasão de divisas – e o eleitor não foi informado disso a tempo. 


Mesmo que você esteja acompanhando as notícias, é possível que tenha perdido as revelações mais recentes.  


Pois vamos a elas. 


Primeiro, as rachadinhas, esquema de desvio de verba pública dos mandatos de Jair Bolsonaro e seus filhos através de saques em dinheiro vivo de funcionários, que depois repassavam à família, das quais Flávio sempre foi figura central.

 O resultado foi demonstrado há alguns anos pelos jornalistas Juliana Dal Piva e Thiago Herdy: 51 imóveis dos Bolsonaro foram pagos parcialmente em dinheiro vivo. O processo judicial das rachadinhas foi extinto pelo STJ, que questionou a quebra de sigilo fiscal, mas as evidências existem e podem gerar novas investigações.  


Segundo, vamos ao caso Master. Ainda hoje sabe-se apenas parcialmente sobre a relação entre Flávio e Daniel Vorcaro. Além do financiamento generoso do filme


Dark Horse


e dos muitos diálogos resgatados do celular de Vorcaro

, não sabemos qual o valor real dos depósitos, que tipo de dinheiro criminoso foi usado para o pagamento pela empresa Entre Investimentos, que

lavava

 inclusive dinheiro para o crime organizado, e nem para que fim o dinheiro foi usado nos EUA.

Não se sabe, ainda, que outros favores e apoios foram prestados pelo banqueiro para Flávio – com quem ele tinha uma relação de amizade

,

segundo demonstram os diálogos completos publicados pela revista


piauí

: são 50 mensagens de Flávio, 46 de Vorcaro e 14 ligações – oito delas atendidas.

 Sempre se tratando como “irmãos”, Flávio chegou a oferecer a Vorcaro uma reunião com Eduardo Bolsonaro em Dubai em novembro do ano passado: “Tá precisando de algo lá? Peço pra ele te encontrar”. Além disso, jantares, cafés da manhã e muitas ligações organizadas entre os dois. 


A mesma revista

revelou

, ainda, que Flávio e Vorcaro viajaram para Fort Lauderdale, na Flórida, no feriado prolongado de 1º de maio de 2025, tendo passado 3 dias ao mesmo tempo no balneário, apenas dias depois do primeiro depósito de Vorcaro para o filme Dark Horse. É provável que tenham passado e celebrado juntos em uma das famosas festas de Vorcaro nestes três dias. Ainda não sabemos até onde foi essa relação. 


Terceiro, a ligação próxima com o “Careca de INSS”. Como


revelou


o ICL, Flávio tem uma empresa de capacetes que está registrada no mesmo lugar de empresas do operador financeiro do esquema que desviava verba dos aposentados e causou prejuízo de R$ 2 bilhões aos cofres públicos.

 Além de usar o mesmo escritório, a empresa de Flávio usava a mesma contabilidade de Antonio Carlos Camilo Antunes, mais conhecido como “Careca do INSS”, atualmente preso.


Quarto, os indícios de corrupção na gestão de hospitais públicos no Rio de Janeiro, inclusive durante a pandemia de Covid.

 Em uma reportagem

bastante detalhada

  aqui na

Agência Pública

, mostramos como Flávio comandava as decisões administrativas e indicações para a gestão dos hospitais federais durante a epidemia. Há diversos indícios de superfaturamento e má conduta em diversos destes hospitais, segundo investigações do TCU e outros órgãos. Esta história está só no começo.  


Quinto, a figura do advogado Willer Tomáz começa a aparecer como uma sombra sobre o passado de Flávio. O advogado já foi descrito como amigo de Flávio pelo próprio

, viajou com ele para um safári na África do Sul e …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Brasil: Ganó Bolsonaro y disputará el balotaje con Lula
content:
La derrota de Lula en los comicios lo deja en situación muy incómoda para el segundo turno. “Fue un resultado inesperado, pero en el balotaje mostraremos la verdadera foto de Brasil”, declaró tras el escrutinio.


Foto: Brasil de Fato


Por Gustavo Veiga.


A las dos horas de finalizada la votación, la diferencia con que se había adelantado Bolsonaro a su rival rondaba los 7 puntos. Una distancia que en el búnker de Lula ya era percibida como una catástrofe. El espíritu de la militancia del PT y sus aliados en el lobby del hotel paulista donde se alojó el comando electoral lo sintetizaban las caras largas y las charlas en voz baja.


Algo andaba mal y sobre todo el desarrollo del escrutinio que, incluso, arrojaba como posible un triunfo de la extrema derecha en la primera vuelta. Pero a medida que pasaban los minutos, esa cuasi certeza empezó a desflecarse. Los números ya fueron otros y Lula, a casi cuatro horas de cerrada la elección, había estrechado aquella diferencia a menos del 3 por ciento.


La algarabía que se veía en el territorio del estado de San Pablo, donde el actual gobernador Tarcisio de Freitas ganó con una holgura desusada, con guarismos semejantes a la ola bolsonarista de las elecciones de 2018, es la radiografía más lograda de la victoria de un proyecto de país. Aquel que dejará –en caso de imponerse Flávio en el segundo turno– a Brasil en manos de las transnacionales de EE.UU, intentará darle la espalda a China (el primer socio comercial del país) y con el regreso al Planalto, se constituirá una especie de gabinete en las sombras para consultas con el Departamento de Estado. Anunciado por el propio candidato Bolsonaro.


Al menos en esta primera vuelta, las apelaciones soberanas de Lula, sus palabras contra la injerencia de Trump, aquello que con ironía denunciaban los grafitis callejeros sobre la avenida Paulista, como el que decía “Make Brazil Quintal Again (Hagamos de Brasil nuestro patio trasero otra vez), no dieron resultado. Entre la militancia petista corrió rápido una hipótesis que acercara una explicación. Que el aparato de la ultraderecha se volcó masivamente a las urnas para sentar presencia en los principales estados del centro-este, donde se concentra la mayor proporción del electorado brasileño.


Lula: “Fue un resultado inesperado, pero en el balotaje mostraremos la verdadera foto de Brasil”


De Freitas, un exmilitar, soldado disciplinado de la causa bolsonarista y gobernador con claroscuros en su gestión, le ganó por paliza a Fernando Haddad, el exministro de Economía de Lula. Con el 99,66 por ciento de los votos contados, la diferencia era de 62,64 % a 36,43. San Pablo reúne a casi un cuarto del electorado nacional.


Los resultados fueron una demostración del músculo derechista en todo el país. La réplica en buena medida de elecciones anteriores cuando se regionalizan los resultados. Bolsonaro ganó en 15 estados, contando el distrito federal de Brasilia, y Lula en 12. El nordeste se tiñó, como tantas otras oportunidades, de rojo y el centro y sur del país de azul, el color del PL.


Sí hay un dato en que el PT y sus aliados pueden apoyarse para soñar con una remontada a finales de octubre, y es que el promedio de abstención nacional rondó el 20 por ciento. No es, por el contrario, que en la pesca de votos, el Partido de los Trabajadores deba ir a buscarlos entre los electores que apoyaron a los otros once candidatos que se presentaron a la votación. Entre ellos, los tres con mejores registros son Ronaldo Caiado, gobernador de Goiás, Renán Santos, un político de São Paulo, y el psiquiatra y escritor de libros de autoayuda Augusto Cury. Tres referentes menores de la derecha que, con matices, tienen más proximidad con Bolsonaro que con Lula.


No hubo ni movilizaciones exultantes ni bocinazos ni festejos por anticipado en este centro financiero que se destaca por su enorme desigualdad, donde a menudo por las calles se cruzan moradores de rua (nuestra gente en situación de calle) con empresarios de trajes elegantes o que conducen sus autos de lujo por las avenidas de los barrios más acomodados de la ciudad.


Aquel es el mayor indicio de que toda la adrenalina política acumulada en este último tramo de campaña deberá canalizarse el 25 de este mes, cuando se sabrá si Lula continúa en el gobierno o si el apellido Bolsonaro volverá a recobrar fuerza con su líder detenido.


Otra tabla de salvación a la que puede aferrarse el PT en este mar bravío en que se convirtió el proceso …

author: anred
title: Se suspendió el juicio por el Jujeñazo de 2023
content:
Lo resolvió la Corte Suprema de Jujuy. El debate debía comenzar el 26 de octubre. Sin embargo, la causa contra los 19 militantes sociales que participaron de la enorme movilización por mejoras salariales y en contra la reforma constitucional que impulsaba el entonces gobernador Gerardo Morales continúa abierta.

Por Red Eco Alternativo.


La decisión del máximo tribunal provincial se dio a conocer luego de que las defensas de los acusados informaran formalmente sobre la existencia de conversaciones avanzadas con la Fiscalía con el objetivo de alcanzar una solución alternativa y global al conflicto procesal.


En diálogo con El Submarino Radio (FM Conectar 91.5), la abogada Mariana Vargas confirmó la notificación del tribunal y expresó que la suspensión representa un avance clave: “El motivo es que informamos a la Corte que estábamos en conversaciones con la Fiscalía para una solución alternativa. Lo habíamos pedido con una queja ante la Corte y con muchos otros planteos (…). Es un gran alivio para las 19 personas, para sus familias y para toda la comunidad, porque en definitiva era un intento de disciplinamiento del conjunto del pueblo respecto de reclamos justos, como fue el Jujeñazo”, explicó la abogada Mariana Vargas al programa El Submarino Radio, que se emite por FM Conectar 91.5).


El juicio contemplaba acusaciones por atentado y resistencia a la autoridad, lesiones leves agravadas a personal policial y daños.


La suspensión deriva en la prescripción de los delitos de mayor carga penal dentro de la causa. Según señala la letrada, las figuras de atentado y resistencia a la autoridad y lesiones se encuentran al límite de su plazo legal de persecución. Al frenarse la apertura de las audiencias, ambas calificaciones quedan virtualmente extintas por prescripción: “Lo que podría estar en debate, que es el tema de la prescripción de los delitos, ahora ya no estaría en debate (…). Lo central es que hay una decisión, una voluntad política de que no se haga el juicio. Esa es la esencia de la cuestión. Es lo que estábamos buscando y es lo que logramos”, agregó la abogada a El Submarino Radio.


Compartimos además la entrevista realizada por el Colectivo Radio Pueblo a Miguel Ramos, de AJI20 – Biblioteca Niñxs Pájaros, quien contó cómo reciben esta decisión y qué significa para quienes siguen reclamando que se termine la persecución y se haga justicia:


ESCUCHAR Y VER LA ENTREVISTA

author: Esperanza
title: Entrevista a Martin Curiche, Camila Huaracan y Sofía Dietz: Operación Huracán, a 9 años aún no hay justicia
content:
Para este registro, nos reunimos con Martin Curiche ex-preso político mapuche incriminado en el montaje de la llamada «Operación Huracán 1» en septiembre de 2017, junto a otros siete dirigentes mapuche y no mapuche, mediante una serie de pruebas falsas implantadas y manipuladas por Carabineros y un civil.


«Cuando se dio toda la operación fue por un tema específico, por dos temas en este caso: estaba el juicio

Luchsinger Mackay

 y a la vez, el

Caso Inglesia

. Fue en ese entonces cuando nos reunimos amigos, pu lamngen y familiares de los presos y decidimos que podiamos hacer algo, podíamos romper ese círculo mediático que la prensa no estaba dando, en conjunto con una red de secundarios y la red de apoyo infantil. El dia 100 de huelga de hambre, porque los peñis del caso inglesia para poder anular un tema que era la asociación ilícita, nosotros empemos a hacer movilizaciones y decidimos levantar un punto de reunión permanente a las afueras de la cárcel». Relata Martin.


El dia 23 de septiembre de 2017, luego de producirse un segundo desalojo en el punto de reunión fuera de la cárcel, Martín Curiche es detenido bajo una orden emanada por el Tribunal de Temuco.


Curiche fue acusado de «asociación ilícita,incendio territorista y de estar en un supuesto grupo de WhastApp donde se comunicaban para comenter ciertos detilos». Imputaciones que finalmente fueron desacreditadas al quedar al descubierto la implantación de pruebas falsas por parte de funcionarios y altos mandos de Carabineros con el apoyo de un civil.


Han pasado 9 años desde la Operación Huracán 1 y Martin, cuenta que hasta la actualidad existen recupercusiones. La exposición mediática y el papel de las grandes cadenas nacionales de comunicación influyeron en la opinión pública de manera negativa.


«Cuando ya se descubre que fue un montaje de todo, el tema de buscar trabajo se vio difícil… (9 años después) Pensando que ese tema estaba zanjado hasta la fecha sigue con réplicas. Cuánto tiempo más tiene que pasar para que eso se borre del expediente de uno, del curriculum en este caso, porque es lo primero que se muestra cuando uno postula a un trabajo».


El otorno familiar y de la comunidad también ha quedado marcada, dice Martin «se empieaza a ver más visitas de carabineros en ese tiempo, para mi zona era escaso ese tema pero después que sucedió eso, la visita de carabineros en el territorio fue excesiva en ese período que duró la famosa Operación Huracán».


Camila Huaracan, una de las abogadas de Martin, quienes actualmente están el en juicio «Operación Huracán 2» como querellantes, comenta:


«trabajamos en el mayor fraude procesal sistemático en el cual se pudo acreditar que los altos mandos realizaron obstrucción a la investigación, también falcificación de prueba y esto netamente, fue perpetrado por altas esferas de Carabineros de Chile, a través de la dirección de inteligencia de la Dipolcar y también de Uioe; Unidad de Inteligencia Operativa Especializada».


Las representantes en este juicio donde Curiche, ahora en calidad de víctima, se refieren al grave hecho de cómo altos mandos de carabineros actuaron para encarcelar injustamente a dirigentes mapuche y la lentitud para encontrar justicia. «Vemos con preocupación cómo ha existido, un obstáculo para acceder a la justicia… vemos cómo acá se ha retrasado a tal punto de que ocurrieron casi 7, 8 años para que recién se comenzara la preparación de juicio oral y ahora vamos a los 10 años y tenemos una sentencia condenatoria en pimera instancia, pero aún así tampoco se condenaron a todos los carabineros…»


Ahora a casi 10 años, existe una sentencia condenatoria hacia los entonces, funcionarios de Carabineros y un civil, sin embargo no todos fueron condenados, sino sólo seis de ellos.

«Por ejemplo el General Blu, el capitán Marín o también Teuber, que ellos participaron en estos montajes, no van a ir a la cárcel, van a estar con libertad vigilada y a muchos de ellos igual se les abonó todo el tiempo que estuvieron en medida cautelar… Vemos que la justicia sí funciona de manera distintas cuando los imputados o las víctimas son mapuche o son altos mandos de Carabineros. Lo vemos como el mayor ejemplo de la crisis de esta república y de estos órganos de Carabineros». Camila Huaracan, abogada.


«La rápidez con la que se efectua cuando los imputados son pertenencientes al pueblo mapuche es muy distinta cuando los imputados son pertencientes a altos mandos de carabineros»

title: Transmisión en vivo, 18:00 horas y palabras del Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés en la reunión del 3 de octubre del 2026 a las 1100 hrs.
content:

Palabras del Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés en la reunión del 3 de octubre del 2026 a las 1100 hrs.

.- El principal objetivo: el encuentro-abrazo con buscadoras. Es importante que esto se entienda bien y quede bien claro. Porque no vamos a cancelar una reunión o actividad con Buscadoras por cualquier otra cosa.

Llevamos muchos años esperando el momento de encontrarnos con ellas.

Entonces, la prioridad o lo más importante en nuestra agenda o programación son las reuniones, encuentros y actividades con las Buscadoras, el día y la hora que ellas establezcan.

Cualquiera otra propuesta de actividad o reunión, deberá ser cuando no haya encuentro o actividad con buscadoras.

Incluso la celebración del aniversario del alzamiento será dependiendo de nuestro abrazo con las Buscadoras.

.- Ya está la paga para los buses de la delegación. Se consiguió gracias al apoyo de la Europa Insumisa, que donó lo que se había juntado para el Capítulo Europa de la Gira por la Vida, y que no se usó completamente. Estas compañeras, compañeros y compañeroas nos dijeron, desde hace tiempo, que esa paga es de los zapatistas, pero, hay que decirlo, es producto de su trabajo, su esfuerzo y su dedicación, y hay que reconocerles esa solidaridad incondicional. Esperamos que ese ejemplo sea luego replicado en capítulos siguientes de la Gira por la Vida, de modo que cada capítulo apoye la realización del siguiente.

Mientras tanto, aquí reconocemos el trabajo desinteresado de todas las personas, grupo, colectivos, organizaciones y movimientos de la Europa de abajo y a la izquierda.

También ha sido fundamental el trabajo de apoyo del colectivo de la Sexta México. “Mujeres y la Sexta”, para conseguir los autobuses.

Gracias compañeras, compañeros y compañeroas. A las Buscadoras les haremos saber de su apoyo.

.- Por lo tanto, toda la campaña económica será ahora para apoyar el traslado de todos los grupos, colectivas y organizaciones posibles a la Ciudad de México, en las fechas que les parezcan más adecuadas a ellas, dentro del mes de diciembre del 2026 y la primera semana de enero del 2027.

En el caso de amenazas y peligros, se tratará de que su traslado ida y vuelta sea por vía aérea, de modo que no corran riesgos al transportarse por tierra.

.- Les vamos a quedar mal porque no vamos a ir 1,111, sino que hasta ahora van 1,509. Más los que se suben de última hora. Pero hay lugar para el Frayba por si quieren acompañarnos.

.- el segundo objetivo es reunirnos con algunos grupos, colectivos, movimientos y organizaciones de la Sexta para planear juntos, en común, lo que sea posible para la segunda etapa de la Gira por la Vida-Capítulo México.

Esto es, cuando vamos a ir a escucharles de lo que son y están haciendo, y hablarles de lo que somos y estamos haciendo, o sea del común.

.- Si hay tiempo y modo, podemos movernos a lugares cercanos geográficamente a la Ciudad de México.

Pero sólo si hay condiciones y somos invitados. Hasta ahora hemos recibido invitación a Oaxaca, Oaxaca; a Querétaro, Querétaro, y se está viendo si a Puebla, Puebla. Si es posible en otros lugares, hay que organizarse y proponer.

Las compañeras de Oaxaca empezaron a organizarse desde que se anunció la salida a la Ciudad de México. Tienen ya resuelto el hospedaje y la alimentación para un parte de la delegación zapatista.

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Sastre sin fumigaciones: “Lo que debería venir es la agroecología para las futuras generaciones”
content:
Por Mariángeles Guerrero


Desde Santa Fe


Siete líneas en una hoja membretada de la Corte Suprema de la Nación pusieron punto final a la batalla judicial que emprendieron, en 2018, vecinas y vecinos de la localidad de Sastre y Ortíz (Santa Fe). Los jueces Horacio Rosatti y Carlos Rosenkrantz desestimaron un reclamo de la municipalidad y convalidaron la decisión que ya había tomado la Corte santafesina: se deben establecer mil metros de distancia para las fumigaciones terrestres en relación a toda esa ciudad. El ministro Ricardo Lorenzetti se excusó de intervenir. Tras conocer el fallo, Sonia González, una de las impulsoras de la causa, pide: “Que no se dude ante la salud”. Asegura que ahora irán por la reforma de la ordenanza local, de acuerdo a lo establecido en los sucesivos fallos favorables que tuvo el expediente.


Sastre y Ortiz es una ciudad de 6.000 habitantes ubicada en el sudoeste santafesino, zona núcleo del agronegocio. A lo largo de la provincia, pueblos y ciudades conviven a diario con las avionetas y los mosquitos. Santa Fe cuenta con una ley obsoleta, que data de 1995, cuando aún no se había aprobado la soja transgénica en Argentina. La soja modificada genéticamente implicó un mayor avance de la frontera agrícola y un mayor uso de herbicidas, principalmente el glifosato. Pese a urgir una actualización, la Legislatura provincial cajoneó varios proyectos de reforma impulsados desde 2010 por organizaciones socioambientales.


En 2018, Zoe Giraudo tenía dos años y un diagnóstico: linfoma linfoblástico tipo T. Estaba internada en Rosario pero, al momento de poder regresar a su casa para continuar los tratamientos de quimioterapia desde allí, los médicos advirtieron a la familia: no podía estar cerca de los venenos. En la localidad ya se venían reuniendo vecinos para intentar que el Concejo local y de que la intendenta, María del Carme Amero, tome alguna medida preventiva ante los mosquitos que fumigaban a menos de cien metros de las viviendas. A fin de ese año se presentó el amparo colectivo que ahora concluyó en la última etapa procesal posible con una nueva sentencia a favor.


La demanda se presentó contra la Municipalidad tras varios intentos de diálogo con el Ejecutivo y el Concejo para que se reformara la Ordenanza Municipal 951/2004, que fijaba el límite de fumigación a solo cien metros a partir de la finalización del área urbana. En el juicio se presentaron como terceros interesados la provincia y una decena de productores. Si bien en 2020 el juez Francisco Hail, de Rafaela, dio la razón a los vecinos, la municipalidad apeló. Y siguió apelando hasta llegar a la Corte Nacional.


Desde la Capital Federal se puso fin al litigio alegando que el último recurso de queja presentado por la Municipalidad de Sastre carece de “fundamentación autónoma”. Cuando refiere a esta falencia, el máximo tribunal indica que una queja determinada no cuenta con un relato prolijo de los hechos y una crítica ordenada al fallo que se busca impugnar. En este caso, el de la Corte de Santa Fe.


El fruto de la lucha colectiva


En el contexto de una provincia donde se plantea la tensión entre salud y modelo productivo y se priorizan los intereses de los grupos concentrados que están detrás del glifosato, de los transgénicos y del monocultivo de commodities, vecinas y vecinos iniciaron un camino que no abandonaron. Y lograron un fallo que ahora implica un precedente relevante para las localidades de Santa Fe y para otros pueblos fumigados del país. Hoy Zoe Giraudo tiene 10 años y su mamá siente que, con esta resolución, deja de cargar una mochila que llevó por años. “Estamos orgullosos como grupo y yo como mamá, porque siento que hice un montón por mi hija”, dice González.


—¿Cómo comenzó la movilización en Sastre?

—La lucha de los vecinos empezó hace muchísimo tiempo, porque había muy pocos vecinos que estaban tratando de alejar estos venenos que ya se sabía que hacían mal. En 2018, una vecina que vive a una cuadra vio un mosquito que estaba fumigando a 70 metros de su casa. Y coincidió con el tiempo en que yo tenía a Zoe, mi nena, internada en Rosario. Esa vecina empezó a buscar soluciones: yendo a la municipalidad, a juntar firmas, a levantar publicaciones en las redes. Zoe se estaba atendiendo con los mejores médicos, pero al final no tenía resguardo con respecto a los venenos. Ellos se juntaron como vecinos, juntaron firmas, fueron al Concejo Municipal y nada. No hubo soluciones. Eso pasó en marzo. Los vecinos …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Comunicado público ppm Caso Grollmus
content:
Frente a las exuberantes condenas y tras un viciado proceso declaramos:

Mari mari pu machi, pu lonko, pu werken, kom pu che. El día de hoy nos dirigimos a la sociedad en general, a todos y todas quienes nos han brindado su apoyo y respaldo en este proceso denominado “Caso Grollmus”.

Actualmente a nosotros como comuneros mapuche se nos ha condenado a penas que marcarán un precedente como obscenamente políticas, se nos condena por decisión política, por ser mapuche que vivimos y recuperamos nuestro territorio.

Tras el gigantesco despliegue comunicacional, y tras el espectáculo montado por el Ministerio Público y la PDI, la familia Grollmus demanda al estado en busca de indemnizaciones y reparaciones.

La fiscalía con el aval del tribunal logró su objetivo: condenar a una pena que ponderada resulta en 1055 años de prisión contra nosotros. La prensa vociferó la sentencia y el poder político respaldo, claridad absoluta.

Les decimos, su ocupación contra nuestro pueblo y su territorio apenas tiene 143 años. Nuestro pueblo resistió al imperio español casi 300 años.

Hoy Chile soberbio y republicano nos condena a más de 1000 años. Por el único motivo de luchar por nuestra soberanía, por nuestro buen vivir y dignidad. Lo anterior tendrá la más necesaria respuesta: continuar con el legado de nuestro pueblo, luchar por nuestra dignidad y libertad.

Los Grupos de Tarea y la BIPE de la PDI recorren los penales de forma morbosa buscando testigos a quienes poner corbata de protegido y sin rostro. Sólo por cuatro relatos de estos “testigos” se dictó sentencia y veredicto. Nuestro territorio se militariza y vuelven a saquear nuestros recursos naturales, vuelven las concesiones mineras, CMPC y Mininco cual mecenas entregan dinero y donaciones a Postas y Escuelas.

Queremos manifestar nuestro agradecimiento por todo el respaldo de nuestros hermanos y hermanas en otros territorios y ciudades. No renunciaremos jamás a la lucha por un debido y objetivo proceso.

Nos movilizaremos por nuestra libertad y juicio justo.

Finalmente los invitamos a sumarse a la próxima movilización articulada en distintos territorios para este 12 de octubre, Día de la resistencia de nuestros pueblos.

¡NULIDAD Y LIBERTAD! ¡NO MÁS TESTIGOS PROTEGIDOS! ¡UNIDAD EN EL WEYCHAN! ¡LIBERTAD A TODOS LOS PRESOS POLÍTICOS MAPUCHE!

Presos Políticos Mapuche del Caso Grollmus de la Franja Lavkenche, CP Biobio, CERECO Coronel, Cárcel Llancahue de Valdivia.

author: Riyad Insanally
title: La autonomía indígena en el sistema interamericano: a cinco años del informe de la CIDH sobre libre determinación
content:
El sistema interamericano reconoce la autonomía de los Pueblos Indígenas y Tribales como un derecho preexistente. De este modo, no debe ser entendido ni como una concesión ni como una cuestión otorgada. El fallo de la Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos a favor de la autonomía del pueblo U'wa de Colombia es la expresión más reciente del derecho de los Pueblos Indígenas a autogobernarse, a definir sus propias instituciones y a decidir sobre sus asuntos internos.

El 4 de julio de 2024, la Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos condenó al Estado colombiano en el caso del Pueblo Indígena U’wa y sus miembros, por no haber garantizado la consulta previa, libre e informada frente a decenas de proyectos extractivos superpuestos a su territorio ancestral. Dictada tres décadas después de que el pueblo U’wa hiciera pública su resistencia frente a la exploración petrolera en su territorio, la sentencia reafirmó estándares centrales sobre la libre determinación indígena: la relación indisoluble entre el territorio, la identidad cultural y la capacidad de un pueblo de decidir su propio destino.

Ese pronunciamiento no aparece de la nada. Confirma y aplica estándares que la Comisión Interamericana de Derechos Humanos (CIDH) había sistematizado cinco años antes, cuando el 28 de diciembre de 2021 aprobó su informe temático “Derecho a la libre determinación de los Pueblos Indígenas y Tribales”. Allí, la Comisión identificó a la autonomía, es decir, al derecho de los pueblos a autogobernarse, a definir sus propias instituciones y a decidir sobre sus asuntos internos, como uno de los elementos constitutivos de la libre determinación, junto con la autoidentificación, la identidad cultural, la propiedad colectiva, los derechos políticos y de participación, y la consulta y el consentimiento previo, libre e informado.

A cinco años de ese informe, y con un caso reciente que vuelve a poner el tema en la agenda regional, vale la pena revisar qué ha dicho específicamente el sistema interamericano sobre el derecho a la autonomía y al autogobierno de los Pueblos Indígenas y Tribales, en sus distintas dimensiones. Ese es el propósito de este artículo: recorrer los estándares desarrollados por la Comisión y por la Corte, mostrando que el caso U’wa no es un hecho aislado, sino la expresión más reciente de una línea de trabajo institucional sostenida durante más de dos décadas, a través de informes temáticos y de casos de la CIDH, y de una jurisprudencia interamericana en constante desarrollo.

La libre determinación de los Pueblos Indígenas y Tribales no se agota en el reconocimiento de la propiedad colectiva de sus tierras. Según ha señalado la CIDH, ese derecho conlleva también la facultad de autogobernar los territorios a través de las propias autoridades, en ejercicio del derecho a la autonomía o al autogobierno reconocido expresamente en el artículo XXI de la Declaración Americana sobre los Derechos de los Pueblos Indígenas (DADPI) y en el artículo 4 de la Declaración de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de los Pueblos Indígenas (UNDRIP). La Comisión advierte que el ejercicio de la gobernanza territorial es una de las expresiones más relevantes de la libre determinación indígena y tribal, porque supone el reconocimiento de sistemas de gobierno propio que asumen el control, el manejo y la administración del territorio ancestral.

Ese control no se limita a un título de propiedad. La CIDH subraya que un componente esencial de la autonomía indígena y tribal es el control efectivo de los territorios ancestrales y de los recursos naturales que allí se encuentran, en tanto son la base material de la existencia de estos pueblos como sujetos colectivos, y no una mercancía: son “la base de su subsistencia económica” y también “fuente de su identidad cultural y bienestar espiritual”. Sin embargo, la Comisión constata con preocupación que, a la fecha, muy escasos Estados de la región han establecido mecanismos legales o administrativos que garanticen la autonomía de los Pueblos Indígenas y Tribales sobre sus recursos naturales y medios de subsistencia. Por el contrario, señala que los ordenamientos internos, en general, impiden que estos pueblos sean titulares de derechos sobre los recursos naturales de su propio hábitat.

Ya en 2001, en el caso de la Comunidad Mayagna (Sumo) Awas Tingni Vs. Nicaragua, la Corte Interamericana había reconocido la estrecha relación entre el territorio y la subsistencia de los Pueblos Indígenas como colectivos …

author: Comunizar
title: Revista Crítica Anticapitalista 6 – La Comuna, la clase y la lucha de clases
content:
PRESENTACION


¿Qué relación existe entre la Comuna como forma política de la emancipación social y la clase, entendida ésta no como categoría positivizada y sociológica, sino en su carácter dual y contradictorio? ¿Es la Comuna una manera de entender la clase y la lucha de clases en clave no identitaria, no positivizada? ¿La oposición entre Comuna y clase es algo derivado de una concepción anti-dialéctica de la lucha de clases? En ese campo ¿a qué dialéctica nos referimos? ¿A la dialéctica hegeliana orientada a la síntesis estatal como forma política de la identidad? ¿A la dialéctica negativa que la cuestiona? ¿La lucha de clases, entendida en clave dialéctica no-identitaria, permite entender la Comuna como proceso contradictorio de disolución de la clase? ¿Implica esto un desafío a nuestro concepto de proletariado y a la idea de revolución calcada en el canon leninista?


CONTENIDO

author: Thiago Domenici
title: Recordar é votar: 7 dos 13 investigados pela CPI da Covid saem eleitos das urnas
content:
Cinco anos depois do Senado pedir o indiciamento de personagens da vida pública por crimes durante a pandemia, a maioria dos investigados pela CPI da Covid que concorreu neste domingo, 4 de outubro, passou pelo crivo do eleitor. Dos 81 nomes com pedido de indiciamento no relatório final da CPI, 13 eram candidatos este ano, como

mostramos

 na

Agência Pública

. Ao final do primeiro turno, sete foram eleitos, cinco perderam e um segue na disputa.


Flávio Bolsonaro terminou o primeiro turno à frente, com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula, e os dois voltam às urnas em 25 de outubro. A CPI pediu o indiciamento de Flávio por incitação ao crime, por estimular aglomerações, o não uso de máscara e a recusa à vacina; à época, ele chamou a acusação de “vingança”.


O candidato à presidência da República Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) vota na Escola Municipal Barão Homem de Mello, em Vila Isabel


No Senado, três cadeiras


No Distrito Federal, Bia Kicis (PL) ficou com a segunda vaga, com 27,44%, atrás de Michelle Bolsonaro. No Rio, Carlos Jordy (PL) foi eleito com 24,56%, atrás do colega de partido Carlos Portinho. Em Santa Catarina, Carlos Bolsonaro (PL) conquistou a segunda cadeira, com pouco mais de 25%, atrás de Carol de Toni. Carlos construiu toda a carreira no Rio, onde foi vereador por sete mandatos, e entrou na disputa catarinense por indicação do pai. Nenhum dos três tinha função executiva na pandemia e a CPI os investigou por campanhas nas redes sociais contra máscaras, o distanciamento social e as vacinas.


Já os ex-gestores que miravam o Senado perderam. No Amazonas, as vagas ficaram com Eduardo Braga (MDB) e Plínio Valério (PSDB); na Paraíba, com João Azevêdo (PSB) e Veneziano (MDB). Ficaram de fora Wilson Lima, governador durante o colapso do oxigênio em Manaus, e Marcelo Queiroga (PL), ex-ministro da Saúde, que terminou em quarto lugar.


Governadora do DF e candidata ao governo, Celina Leão, acompanhada das canditadas ao Senado, Michelle Bolsonaro e Bia Kicis, vota no CEF 01 do Lago Norte, cidade satélite de Brasília


Na Câmara e nas Assembleias


Eduardo Pazuello (PL) foi reeleito no Rio de Janeiro com 146.148 votos, o décimo mais votado do estado. Em 2022, ele recebeu 205.324 votos e foi o segundo mais votado. Osmar Terra (PL) foi reeleito no Rio Grande do Sul com 116.647 votos, e Ricardo Barros (PP) renovou o mandato pelo Paraná com 94.050. Onyx Lorenzoni não aparece entre os 31 eleitos gaúchos, com 100% das urnas apuradas.


A médica Nise Yamaguchi também não se elegeu. O PL conquistou 19 das 70 cadeiras de São Paulo na Câmara, e o nome dela não está entre elas. Foi a terceira derrota seguida da médica. Em 2022, disputou a Câmara pelo PROS e recebeu 36.690 votos. Em 2024, tentou a Câmara Municipal de São Paulo pelo União e ficou na suplência, com 16.554 votos.


Mayra Pinheiro (PL), a “capitã cloroquina”, foi eleita deputada estadual no Ceará com 34.752 votos, na penúltima das 46 vagas. No Amazonas, a bancada do União Brasil na Assembleia ficou com cinco nomes reeleitos. Marcellus Campêlo, secretário de Saúde durante a crise do oxigênio, não está entre eles.


Eduardo Pazuello foi reeleito deputado federal pelo Rio de Janeiro com 146.148 votos


O que a CPI apontou


Pazuello reúne a lista mais extensa como emprego irregular de verbas, prevaricação, comunicação falsa de crime, crimes contra a humanidade e epidemia com resultado em morte. Este último crime também foi atribuído a Mayra Pinheiro, Nise Yamaguchi, Osmar Terra, Wilson Lima e Queiroga. Pazuello, Onyx e Mayra foram apontados, ainda, por crimes contra a humanidade, pelo foco no tratamento precoce em Manaus. Barros é suspeito de integrar uma organização criminosa no caso Covaxin. Para os senadores, as normas do governo indicavam “uma estratégia de propagação do vírus conduzida de forma sistemática”.


Segundo pesquisadores da USP, da FGV, do Butantan e da London School, ao menos 127 mil mortes poderiam ter sido evitadas apenas em 2021 sem o atraso na compra de vacinas. O país terminou a pandemia com mais de 700 mil mortos.


A PGR, então comandada por indicados de Bolsonaro, pediu o arquivamento de todas as denúncias. Em setembro de 2025, o ministro Flávio Dino, do STF, mandou abrir inquéritos contra parte dos indiciados, mas Mayra, Campêlo, Pazuello, Nise, Queiroga e Wilson Lima ficaram de fora. Nenhum foi julgado antes da eleição. Os eleitos tomam posse em fevereiro de 2027.

author: Unknown
title: Iran steps up military presence in Eastern Kurdistan
content:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has deployed heavy military equipment in the Şaho Mountains near Rewanser in Eastern Kurdistan and closed parts of the region to civilians. At the same time, artillery fire is targeting mountain ridges under the pretext of a military exercise.


According to the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), citing a resident of a village at the foot of the Şaho Mountains, the Revolutionary Guards have deployed a convoy carrying heavy military equipment to the region in recent days.


Residents were informed through village councils that certain areas of the Şaho Mountains are off-limits until October 7. According to a notice issued by the Şiwankar village council, the restrictions apply to the mountain ridges stretching from Bedrawa through Pir-Xidir to the Goliçî Pass. The area around Pir-Xidir, among others, is being subjected to artillery fire.


The Şaho Mountains and the adjacent Kosalan Mountains were officially designated as a protected area by Iran’s Supreme Environmental Council in 2009. Nevertheless, the Revolutionary Guards have been expanding their military infrastructure there for years. At the end of August, the Revolutionary Guards heavily shelled the ridges of the Şaho Mountains in the Kamyaran area with artillery. Footage published by the KHRN subsequently documented extensive fires across the mountainous area.


According to environmental activists, the Revolutionary Guards have been establishing military bases in the Şaho-Kosalan protected area since 2007 under the pretext of combating Kurdish opposition forces. Parts of the forests and grazing lands have reportedly been destroyed during the construction of the bases and military access roads. The activists also say that vegetation and pastureland around some military posts are deliberately set on fire. The Revolutionary Guards justify this by saying they aim to prevent Kurdish forces from using the vegetation as cover for attacks.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Recent Incidents Highlight Chinese Transnational Repression in Taiwan
content:
A NUMBER OF recent incidents illustrate new tactics in China’s playbook for transnational repression.

For one, a comedy club in Taipei–known as Comedy Club or Comedy Plus +–had its entrance smeared with a mixture of feces and white paint. It is thought that this occurred due to performances by comedian Huang Yi-hao. Huang previously mocked Chinese president Xi Jinping during a stand-up routine in December 2025, clips of which recently went viral online.

A 35-year-old man surnamed Kuo was reportedly paid 50,000 NT by a 33-year-old man surnamed Liu to carry out the attack. It is unclear whether the two were acting at China’s behest.

Past similar incidents include when Hong Kong pro-democracy singer Denise Ho and bookstore owner and publisher Lam Wing-kee, one of the Causeway Bay booksellers, were splashed with red paint by attackers. Some of these attackers were linked to Taiwanese pro-China organized crime groups such as the Bamboo Union gang.

Likewise, Aegis, a restaurant that assisted Hongkongers seeking refuge in Taiwan, and a gym owned by a pro-democracy Hongkonger who had previously stood as an electoral candidate, had faced similar incidents. Aegis was splashed with chicken feces by men who were paid by a Chinese national to carry out the act.

The gym in question was splashed with red paint by two individuals who arrived from Hong Kong. The two individuals departed back to Hong Kong before they could be caught.

Nor would this be the only case in which China has apparently flown individuals to Taiwan to carry out actions that they try to quickly flee from in short order. This was also the case when political commentator Akio Yaita was attacked in a Taichung hotel where Yaita was giving a speech, with the individual in question having been flown in for the attack from Hong Kong, and subsequently attempting to flee abroad. The use of Taiwanese and Hongkongers, or Chinese nationals with Hong Kong passports, for such attacks, however, allows for plausible deniability that avoids being directly traced back to the Chinese government.

Still, the attack serves as a reminder of what Taiwan stands to lose if it were to fall under Chinese control. Even the simple act of mocking one’s political leaders in a comedy show could lead to violent reprisals.

To this extent, reports indicate that cases of Chinese impersonation seem to be on the rise. The distributor of the documentary State Organs, which details Chinese organ harvesting of members of the Falun Gong, has reported cases of individuals attempting to pose as him to carry out threats using his phone number. Kuan Chien-chung is the head of Lion Movies Culture Company. This seems to follow up on preceding reports of individuals connected to civil society groups receiving suspicious e-mails with interview requests from people that they were often already connected to.

author: groundxero
title: ‘The Struggle Continues’ for Today’s Generation of French Students
content:
The French student movement has a long history of political activism based on organized protests and occupations not only for the improvement of their learning experience and school conditions but also against capitalism, consumerism, imperialism, and police repression.


 


By

C.J. Polychroniou


Common Dreams


 


France

 is presently in the throes of nationwide student

protests

 that have turned increasingly violent as the police crack down on students, using tear gas and heavy-handed tactics as students blockade entrances to their schools and even set fire to several schools across France.


 


The students, aged between 15 and 18, are protesting over poor school conditions (overcrowded classrooms, crumbling

infrastructure

, heavy workloads, teacher shortages) and demand increased funding for schools. Thousands have been

detained

, mostly minors, and dozens injured, including some 50 law enforcement officers.


 


The high school protests begun in Aubervilliers, a low-income Paris suburb, but quickly spread nationwide, as usually happens with students protests in France. University students have now joined high school schools across France, thus creating an even more volatile situation for the French government. Incidentally, the student protests are unfolding alongside massive public-sector protests over pay and working conditions.


 


French students have also shown that they are always on the side of the workers’ fight for better working conditions and in their struggle for an alternative socioeconomic and political order.


 


France is indeed in crisis mode, economically, politically, and socially. Weak growth and deteriorating public finances have been the norm for several years now, while

austerity

 is being advanced by the political establishment as the only available solution to the country’s economic problems and financial misery. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu presented an austerity-driven government

budget

 on October 1 that proposes 43 billion euros in new fiscal measures to reduce the deficit.


 


However, the

budget

 bill is surely expected to face a rough ride as France has a deeply divided parliament that has repeatedly rejected austerity-driven budget proposals, forcing in fact several prime ministers since 2022 to step down. Lecornu’s government may very well be the next one to collapse as it is highly unlikely that either Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party or Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s left-wing France Unbowed (LFI) party (which France’s

Interior Ministry

 has actually classified as far left) will make compromises, especially in light of the fact that France’s next presidential election is scheduled for April 18 and May 2, 2027, and looks like the

run-off election

 will be between Le Pen and Mélenchon.


 


In addition, France’s

bond market

 is under growing pressure as its 10-year yield has reached the highest level since 2002. With the cost of borrowing money hitting a peak, France, which has faced sluggish growth for years, is likely to see even slower growth in 2027 than in 2026. This situation seems to be serving the far-right RN party particularly well, which has already scored a “

historic victory

” by securing enough seats in the recently held Senate election to establish its own caucus for the first time.


 


In the meantime, the student protests are being used both by Le Pen and government officials to

target

 Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s party for allegedly deploying agitators and using rhetoric to stoke students’ anger.


 


There is little doubt that the concerns of French students are legitimate. Their grievances with the poor state of schools have been building since this summer’s

heatwaves

, which exposed “the poor state of schools, with poor insulation and no air conditioning,” according to

Vincent Latour

,

 a professor of British Studies at the University of Toulouse-II-Le Mirail. Moreover, the president of Union Syndicale Lycéenne (USL), 19-year old

Ryad Rani

, said that student grievances had elicited no response from the government and that the movement will continue with the protests until its demands are satisfied.


 


The French student movement has a long history of political

author: rti_admin
title: The Algorithm of the Ballot: How Data Decides Democracy Before We Vote
content:
Elections used to be loud. Street-corner rallies, hoarse loudspeakers, campaigners going door to door, entire neighbourhoods gathered around a television for the evening debate. That version of democracy is dying, and most of us haven’t quite noticed the funeral. The real contest now happens somewhere quieter — inside a smartphone screen, in the space between a thumb and a feed. Political persuasion doesn’t shout at crowds anymore. It whispers to individuals, one at a time, and the whisper has been tested, refined, and timed with a precision no rally could ever match.

This isn’t speculation about some AI-run future. It’s already part of how political communication works in India and elsewhere with widespread mobile internet access.

Campaigns describe their own methods as “smart” and “surgical,” and for once the marketing language is accurate. Nobody is addressing an anonymous mass anymore. Every voter is a profile being built in real time — every scroll, every pause, every like or skip can become another data point feeding a model of who you are and what might move you. Linger two seconds longer on a video about unemployment, and your feed may begin showing you more content like it, each one worded slightly differently, until what started as manufactured content starts to feel like your own settled opinion.

What makes this so effective is precisely that it doesn’t feel like anything is being done to you. A curated feed never announces itself as curated. It just feels instinctual — as if the device has learned to think alongside you rather than manipulate you. Two people can work in the same office, live in the same city, share the same friend group, and still inhabit completely different informational worlds. One sees hope where the other sees decline. One sees progress where the other sees collapse. The algorithm isn’t necessarily lying to either of them. It’s simply reflecting their inclinations at them, amplified, until the reflection becomes impossible to distinguish from the self that’s supposedly thinking.

Try this yourself, and it gets uncomfortable fast: spend one full day deliberately engaging with the opposite side of your politics. Like the arguments you find weak. Click into the topics you usually scroll past. Within hours, your feed may begin to recalibrate. The old version — the one that felt so personal, so obviously true — can start to look different, as if it never existed. That should bother you more than it probably does. If a belief can be reshaped in an afternoon just by changing what you click, how solid was it to begin with? Political conviction, it turns out, isn’t always bedrock. Often it’s just a data point that hasn’t been nudged yet.

A Global Infrastructure of Influence

None of this is a local phenomenon. In the United States, campaigns use predictive modelling, experimentation, and targeted advertising to identify voters and test which messages are more persuasive. In China, the digital infrastructure is subject to extensive state regulation, including rules governing algorithmic recommendations and the presentation of information. In the European Union, regulators have moved beyond drafting rules: new regulations governing the transparency and targeting of political advertising became fully applicable in October 2025, imposing significant restrictions on the use of personal data for political targeting.

Different governments, different justifications, same underlying playbook. None of it necessarily depends on coercion, because coercion is visible, and visible things get resisted. The real method can be subtler: build the environment so precisely that a person mistakes the nudge for their own free judgment. Nobody feels manipulated when they’re convinced the idea was theirs all along.

There’s a specific kind of unease in standing inside a polling booth and asking yourself a plain question: was this decision actually made here, in this moment of privacy — or weeks ago, in a server room, by a system that had already modelled the outcome? When results appear close to pre-poll forecasts, “good analytics” is one explanation. Successful engineering is another. At a certain level of precision, the two can start to look identical.

This matters more, not less, in a country as vast and unequal as India. Behavioural targeting doesn’t treat every citizen the same way. Voters with less digital literacy, fewer alternative sources of information, or less social capital to question what their …

author: Jessa Agad, Mira Bueno at Jenelle Nuqui
title: Ano ang papel ng US sa krisis sa langis?
content:
mga kuha nina Jessa Agad, Colline Nobleza, Mira Bueno

“Itigil ang gyerang agresyon ng US sa buong daigdig”

Iyan ang panghuli sa anim na hiling ng mga tsuper mula sa ikinasang dalawang araw na transport strike sa bansa noong Setyembre 29-30.

Sa patuloy na pag-atake ng US-Israel sa Kanlurang Asya, apektado ang pangunahing industriya ng langis na nagpaparalisa sa pag-aangkat ng suplay sa iba’t ibang bansa. Ngunit sa Pilipinas, paano nga ba ito nakakaapekto sa karaniwang mamamayan?

Nang sumiklab ang giyerang agresyon ng US-Israel laban sa Iran noong Pebrero 2026, naging malaki ang epekto nito sa daloy ng langis sa iba’t ibang rehiyon, partikular sa Strait of Hormuz, isang mahalagang ruta ng mga pandaigdigang kalakalan.

20% ng pandaigdigang suplay ng crude oil at liquified natural gas (LNG) ang dumaraan sa Strait of Hormuz. Dahil sa matinding tensyon at mga banta ng pag-atake sa rehiyong sakop ang ruta, naantala at bumagal ang trapiko ng mga barkong pang-kargamento na siyang nagpalaki ng pangamba sa suplay ng enerhiya at nagtulak sa presyo ng krudo mula $65 patungong mahigit $100 bawat bariles sa pandaigdigang merkado.

Bukod sa Strait of Hormuz, inatake ng Iraqi drone ang East-West oil pipeline ng Saudi Arabia noong Setyembre 11 dahilan para pansamantalang isinara ang naturang pipeline na kilala rin bilang Petroline.

Ang imprastraktura ay direktang nag-uugnay sa mga pangunahing oil fields ng Saudi Arabia sa Silangang Lalawigan patungo sa port terminal ng Yanbu sa Red Sea, ito ang nagsisilbing pangunahing alternatibong ruta ng bansa upang maiwasan ang Strait of Hormuz.

Sa katunayan, ginagamit ito upang iangkat ang humigit-kumulang 4 milyong barrels ng langis kada araw na katumbas ng halos 4% ng pandaigdigang suplay.

Ayon sa pinakahuling datos mula sa Department of Energy (DOE), ang Pilipinas ay pangyunahing umaasa sa pandaigdigang merkado dahil halos 98% ng crude oil imports ay nagmula sa Middle East, partikular sa Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates (UAE), at Iraq.

Bukod sa krudo, ang mga pinong produktong langis na ginagamit sa mga sasakyan tulad ng diesel at gasolina ay 97 porsyento na inaangkat naman mula sa mga karatig-bansa sa Asya gaya ng South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, at Japan. Gayunpaman, ang mga refinery ng mga bansang ito ay umaasa rin sa krudo na nagmumula sa Middle East na kailangan dumaan sa makitid na ruta gaya ng Strait of Hormuz.

Hindi lingid sa kaalaman ng nakararami na 50% ng industriya sa bansa ay nakaaasa langis. Sa halos pitong buwang pagpapatuloy ng giyera, nagpapatuloy pa tumitinding krisis sa global supply chain na higit na nakaapekto sa presyo ng langis tungong $200 kada barrel.

Ayon sa Department of Energy, umabot na sa P73.68 kada litro ang netong pagtaas ng presyo ng diesel mula sa unang kwarto ng taon. Samantalang sa loob lamang ng Setyembre, tumaas pa ng P18.31 kada litro ang presyo ng diesel, bunsod ng magkasunod na dagdag-presyo.

Sa ulat ng IBON Foundation, 65% ng suplay ng langis ay napupunta sa sektor ng transportasyon, sumunod ang services (11.9%), industriya (7.6%), gamit pangbahay (7%), at sa agrikultura (1%).

Kaya naman sa bawat pagtaas ng presyo ng langis, tsuper at operator ang unang umaaray.

“Sa maghapon naming pamamasada, nag-uuwi na lang kami ng mahigit P200, pinakamataas [na ang] P400. Sa kinu-krudo namin sa isang araw mahigit P3,000. Kaya kakapiranggot na lang ang aming kinikita sa aming pamilya.” ani Tatay Mario, jeepney driver-operator sa Novaliches,

Noong Setyembre 28, ipinatupad ng LTFRB ang minimum na pamasahe sa tradisyunal na jeepney mula P13 tungong P14 para sa unang apat na kilometro. Ayon sa PISTON, insulto ang baryang dagdag-pasahe para sa mga tsuper at operator na gumagastos ng P3000 kada araw para sa langis.

“Dahil sa ganitong presyo ng langis grabe eh, hindi kakayanin. Kasi yung piso na dinagdag nila, wala rin epekto yan dahil sa sbrang taas [ng presyo].” dagdag ni Samuel Soria, driver-operator ng Don Bosco-Delpan-Divisoria route.

Sa kabilang banda, dalawang ‘oil giants’ sa Pilipinas ay nag-ulat ng paglaki ng kita ngayong taon.

Ang Petron Corporation, na pagmamay-ari ni Ramon Ang, ay nakalikom ng P3.8 billion kita sa unang hati ng 2026. Habang ang kampanyang Shell Pilipinas Corporation naman ay dumoble sa P1.62 billion ang kita kung ikukumpara sa P743.6 million nilang kita noong 2025.

Ayon sa PISTON, ang pabago-bagong dikta ng pandaigdigang merkado ng langis ay pakana ng US kagunay sa nagpapatuloy na giyerang agresyon sa Kanlurang Asya na …

author: ALR Editors
title: Announcing Asian Labour School Oct-Nov 2026 Semester
content:
Dear friends,


We are back with an amazing list of new and returning courses for the Asian Labour School. If you are interested in

acquiring democratic facilitation skills, navigating conflicts and taking collective care, working cooperatively, strengthening a union core or leading your own radical walking tours

, please check out the course information below and study with Asian Labour School.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Chie Matsumoto


We all have attended meetings where decisions were made by only a few members, most outspoken ones or someone at the top. We may have once thought, “Why am I even here?” and left without saying a word. Democracy starts in the smallest conversations, dialogues and meetings by raking in most diverse opinions and ideas, piecing them together to create something new and meaningful to all participants.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Facilitators: Emi Do and Matt Noyes


Worker cooperatives are enterprises that are owned and governed by workers. When all of our working experiences have been in profit-maximizing enterprises, or in workplaces that are structured hierarchically, it is no wonder that we can encounter challenges when attempting to work together cooperatively. In this course we will explore the challenges and tensions when there are no bosses to hate!


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Facilitator: Nash Tysmans


Movements are built through relationships. Yet the pressures of organizing (urgency, conflict, exhaustion, political disagreement, and unequal power) can strain those relationships and undermine our collective capacity. How can we build movements that are both effective in challenging injustice and caring in how we work together?


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Sithar Chhim


In order to win any campaign at workplace, unions need to be strong enough to pressure the company. Building a strong and representative committee is the only way to win over the bosses who have well organized structure at workplace compare to workers.


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)


Facilitator: Kevin Lin


Have you ever thought about leading your own radical walking tour to share with friends the significance of places and histories in your city? Leading and participating in a radical walking tour is not only educational but fun and always memorable. A walking tour provides a concrete sense of places, people, and histories. This course will walk you through the conceptualisation, research and logistics of a radical walking tour, and hear ideas and experiences from other participants across Asia.


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)

title: Sleeper-Cell Report July 2026 – Global Coalition reports 0 confirmed ISIS attacks
content:
An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside


 


Key Points


– Six sleeper-cell attacks recorded by RIC, but the Global Coalition claims 0 attacks were officially claimed by ISIS


– One military personnel was killed, and a further five injured


– A minimum of seven alleged ISIS members were arrested


– A total of 36 civilians were injured, two killed


– An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in Deir ez-Zor


–

Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS mercenaries repatriated from Roj camp


 


In-Depth


In July of 2026, RIC

recorded six sleeper-cell attacks which some publications have attributed to ISIS, according to


North Press Agency

 one of these attacks was claimed by ISIS whereas the


Global Coalition


reported that July was the first month since the territorial defeat of ISIS in 2019, where they claimed 0 attacks. Also this month at least 7 members of ISIS cells were arrested.


On July 7, Bombings struck central Damascus near the Ministry of Tourism and the Four Seasons Hotel, during the visit of Macron the president of France to Syria. Ministry of Interior has attributed the attack to ISIS, the bombing resulted in the killing of one civilian and injury of 36.


On July 8, three attacks happened during the same day and the are believed to have been carried out by ISIS members.

Unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle used machine guns to target an oil truck in Abrahyah town in eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, killing the driver.


Similarly, unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle, attacked a checkpoint of the Internal Security Forces near al-Baserah city bridge.


According to North Press Agency, also on July 8 ISIS

claimed responsibility for the killing of Rashad Khalaf al-Ghurair in the northern countryside of Deir ez-Zor.


On July 15,

unknown gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire on a member of the 72nd Division on the road linking al-Arimah and Manbij in eastern Aleppo countryside, injuring the him.


On July 18,

two unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire directly on member of the Defence Ministry


near al-Awsajli junction in eastern Manbij city.


On July 9,

Syria’s Interior Ministry announced its security forces had dismantled several ISIS cells in southern Syria, arresting a senior leader and several members accused of involvement in assassinations and financing terror.


On July 28,

Syrian Internal Security Forces and the General Intelligence Service in Aleppo announced the arrest of individuals allegedly affiliated with the ISIS, during a security operation in Aleppo and its surrounding countryside.


An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, in an incident that sparked widespread concern among residents.


During July, Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS were repatriated from


Roj Camp, which houses families of ISIS members, and returned to Tunisia. Additionally, Tunisian citizen Bilal Chawachi was sentenced to 55 years in prison after being convicted on terrorism-related charges, specifically traveling to Syria and fighting alongside the extremist organization.


Germany sentenced an Iraqi man to life imprisonment and his former wife to nine years and six months in prison after convicting them of enslaving and torturing two Yazidi girls while they were members of ISIS in Syria and Iraq between 2015 and 2017.


Three U.S. citizens pleaded guilty to terror charges, prosecutors said the defendants communicated through encrypted messaging applications between July and November 2025 and planned to travel to Turkey before crossing into Syria to join ISIS. 


* Due to the low rate of confirmed ISIS attacks RIC has decided to stop publishing monthly sleeper-cell reports and instead share a bi-annual summary of ISIS activity throughout Syria.

author: Unknown
title: ISIS member arrested in Sulaymaniyah
content:
Counter-terrorism units have arrested a wanted member of the “Islamic State” (ISIS) in Sulaymaniyah. The man is said to have moved to Sulaymaniyah following the military collapse of ISIS and continued his activities for the organization there.


According to the Kurdish Counter-Terrorism Group Lexoman-Parastin (CTG), the arrest followed an extended period of surveillance and the analysis of detailed intelligence. The detainee reportedly belonged to a unit designated by ISIS as the “210th Division.”


Following the collapse of the jihadist group, the man settled in Sulaymaniyah. According to the security forces, however, he remained active as an ISIS member within the province until he was tracked down and arrested by counter-terrorism units.


His father had also held senior positions within ISIS. He initially served as commander of a military unit in the so-called “North Baghdad Province” and was later appointed ISIS “governor” of Fallujah. He was killed in an airstrike in the Abu Ghraib district.


A brother of the detainee, who was also a member of ISIS, was killed in the an-Nibāʿī area northwest of Baghdad, according to the security forces. No further information was provided about the detainee’s identity or his specific activities for ISIS in Sulaymaniyah.
