author: Derek Seidman
title: A Growing Movement Is Working to Evict ICE From Its Buffalo Command Center
content:
Activists are pressuring Buffalo corporations to kick ICE out of the office building where it is imprisoning children.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

A glimmering 12-story building towers over the intersection where Delaware Avenue meets Chippewa Street in downtown Buffalo. The building is owned by Uniland Development, a major Buffalo real estate developer. Surrounded by coffee shops, luxury hotels, and boutique restaurants, the building’s facade is emblazoned with the corporate logo of its anchor tenant, Delaware North, one of the world’s largest concessions corporations, headquartered in Buffalo.

But amid the daily humdrum at 250 Delaware Avenue — paper shuffling inside, cars honking outside — is, to many Buffalonians, something more shocking: The building’s seventh floor serves as the operational hub of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) machinery of detention and deportation across much of New York State, and it is a “hold room” site used to detain immigrant neighbors, including children.

For years, ICE’s Buffalo field office has lived inside the Delaware North Building. Now, an escalating campaign, Evict ICE from 250 Delaware, is determined to pressure the building’s corporate owners — Uniland Development, owned by the Montantes, a prominent Buffalo area family — and its flagship renter — the Delaware North corporation, owned by the billionaire Jacobs family — to cut ties with ICE when its current lease expires on March 31, 2027.

Backed by a broad coalition of community organizations and immigrant rights groups, and driven by dozens of volunteers, the campaign is working actively — canvassing and petitioning, protesting weekly, staging direct actions — to not only shame and compel Buffalo’s corporate class into evicting ICE from its properties, but also to use the campaign’s momentum to advance the more sweeping movement goals of kicking ICE out of Buffalo and abolishing the agency altogether.

On September 26, eight people were arrested as they sat down and occupied the intersection in front of 250 Delaware — which the campaign is now calling the “Montante Detention Center” — to protest “the Montante family’s continued profiteering from deportation,” according to a press release.

“The people of Buffalo will not allow mass deportation profiteers to hide any longer,” the arrestees said in a statement. “There can be no more business as usual at 250 Delaware Ave until the Montantes EVICT ICE.”

Buffalo is a border town — a city shaped by immigrants, past and present. The region is a focal point for Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) operations, with raids, detentions, and deportations of immigrants a constant reality. Buffalo made national headlines in February after the death — ruled a homicide by the county medical examiner — of Nurul Amin Shah Alam, a blind Rohingya refugee who Border Patrol left at a downtown coffeeshop without notifying his family of his release.

The Evict ICE campaign describes ICE’s field office in 250 Delaware as the “command center” of the agency’s operations across most of New York State — essentially all areas upstate of New York City and its vicinity. Its purview also includes the nearby Batavia holding center, the state’s only ICE federal detention facility, which is expanding its capacity to hold detainees. In Buffalo, ICE arrests have soared over the past year.

“The masked men kidnapping people off the streets — that is orchestrated out of 250 Delaware,” Jennifer Connor, the executive director of Justice for Migrant Families, told Truthout.

Additionally, the building houses the Buffalo office for Homeland Security Investigations and Buffalo’s Office of the Principal Legal Advisor. Both are arms of DHS’s machinery across New York State.

The Evict ICE campaign and numerous sources say 250 Delaware contains more than piles of paperwork and ringing phones.

The campaign’s analysis of data from the Deportation Data Project found that 237 people were held at the “Buffalo Hold Room” on the 7th floor at 250 Delaware Avenue from February 2025 to March 2026, including 18 children under the age of 12. Many people were held for multiple days, exceeding ICE’s short-term holding policies, and in overcrowded conditions.

author: Corey Larocque
title: An Early Inuit relocation scheme – Part 1
content:
On August 13, 1877, an unusual expedition left New London, Conn., bound for Cumberland Sound on the southeastern coast of Baffin Island. Known officially as the Howgate Preliminary Arctic Expedition, it was to be the first stage of a much grander enterprise planned by Captain Henry W. Howgate of the United States Army.


Howgate had been inspired by the recent British expedition to the High Arctic led by George Nares. With two ships, Nares had tried to reach the North Pole by way of Smith Sound, the narrow channel separating Ellesmere Island from Greenland. One ship, the Alert, had reached a point on Ellesmere Island farther north than any other ship had ever gone and wintered there.


Howgate thought that Americans should do one better than the British. He wanted to establish a permanent scientific colony at Lady Franklin Bay. For that, he would need Inuit — for he knew that none lived that far north — and dogs and skin clothing.


And so a plan was hatched that a preliminary expedition would travel to Cumberland Sound and winter there. It would be under the command of Captain George Tyson, a whaler well known to the Inuit of the sound. During the winter, Tyson would hire Inuit who were willing to relocate to Ellesmere Island and collect supplies. Two scientists would accompany the preliminary expedition. Because the entire scheme was underfunded, it was planned that Tyson would also hunt whales to support the expedition financially. The following spring, the vessel would travel across Davis Strait to Greenland where it would liaise with a larger ship from the U.S., to which the Inuit would transfer for the trip to Ellesmere Island.


The expedition, aboard the tiny vessel, Florence, reached Cumberland Sound in September. She headed first for Naujartalik (Niantilic), a popular destination for whalers on the southern coast of the sound. There, Tyson learned that four whaling ships were planning to winter there, and two others at Kekerten on the northern side of the sound. Tyson knew that both were popular wintering places because early ice breakup would allow early spring whaling.


But the competition for trade would not augur well for the success of his efforts to acquire skin clothing and encourage Inuit to join his expedition. So he decided that he would have to be farther up the sound. He put into winter quarters on Oct. 7 at the head of the sound at a place the whalers knew as Ananito Harbour, or Annanatook Harbour, the place later spelled by Franz Boas as Anarnitung — the Inuit place name Anarnituuq.


The expedition’s two scientists were Ludwig Kumlien, an ornithologist and naturalist, and Orray Taft Sherman, a meteorologist. They immediately set to work. Tyson busied himself collecting skin clothing, purchasing dogs and convincing Inuit to relocate. Three Inuit families had been living at Anarnituuq when the Florence made anchor there. But over the winter, the location became a popular destination for more Inuit coming to trade with Tyson.


“The Cruise of the Florence” is a scarce book telling about the Inuit relocation scheme.


Tyson described his efforts to convince Inuit to relocate to Ellesmere Island: “I have had several conversations with the Esquimaux in regard to their going with us to the East Land, as they always call the coast of Greenland. Some say they will go; others fear to go. The latter are afraid of the ‘mulling’ (sea) in such a little vessel as the Florence. Others, again, have mothers who do not want them to go; then, again, brothers and sisters, uncles and aunts and cousins, and I do not know what else.”


Five men promised to go, as did several from Naujartalik. In the spring, the disadvantages of Tyson’s choice of wintering harbour became apparent. His ship was firmly locked in the grip of the ice, while the other ships which had wintered farther to the mouth of the sound had been released from their harbours and gone about the business of whaling. By the time the Florence was free, there was no time for whaling.


When the ship left harbour, it carried ten Inuit (four men, two women and four children) who had agreed to relocate to Ellesmere Island. They were Nep-e-ken and his family; Al-o-kee; a man named Ete-tun and his family; and a man nicknamed Chummy. He is also referred to as Thu-nu-ping-nar or Shu-mar-ping-uter. What this confusing agglomeration of letters was intended to represent in Inuktitut is a mystery to me.

author: Daniel Opasinis, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Grassy Narrows River Run brings demands for mercury justice to Tkarón:to
content:
On Wednesday, Sept. 23, members of Grassy Narrows First Nation, Whitedog, and organizers in Tkarón:to came together for the annual Grassy Narrows River Run. Photo by Daniel Opasinis


On the front lawn of Queen’s Park in Tkarón:to stands a tall statue of Sir James Pliny Whitney, Ontario premier from 1905 to 1914, whose government promoted mining and forestry development in northern Ontario.


Over a century later, Glenn Cameron, councillor for Wabaseemoong First Nation (Whitedog), stood below that same statue. Holding a microphone connected to a portable sound system, he addressed a crowd gathered to demand action on the mercury contamination that continues to affect his community.


On Wednesday, Sept. 23, members of Grassy Narrows First Nation, Whitedog, and organizers in Tkarón:to came together for the annual Grassy Narrows River Run. They are calling on Ontario and “Canada” to fairly compensate people in Grassy Narrows

for the mercury crisis and stop the Dryden mill

.


People rally for justice for Grassy Narrows in Toronto on Sept. 23. Photo by Daniel Opasinis


Between

1962 and 1970

, Dryden Chemicals Limited discharged approximately nine tonnes of mercury into the Wabigoon River. The contamination spread through the river system, poisoning fish that people in Grassy Narrows and Wabaseemoong relied on for food and their livelihoods. 


Eating contaminated fish exposed people to methylmercury, a highly toxic form of mercury that accumulates in the food chain and can damage the brain and nervous system. Exposure during pregnancy can also harm developing children. 


People rally for justice for Grassy Narrows in Toronto on Sept. 23. Photo by Daniel Opasinis


Earlier that day, participants gathered in Grange Park in the downtown core holding signs and papier-mâché fish. Some played instruments as people got to know one another. It wasn’t long before the crowd filed along McCaul Street, led by a banner reading “Justice for Grassy.”


At the head of the march, participants carried photographs fixed to wooden dowels of loved ones from Grassy Narrows and Whitedog who had died. 


Cameron said malnutrition and mercury contamination from the Dryden Pulp and Paper Mill have been

a constant concern

 within his community. 


People rally for justice for Grassy Narrows in Toronto on Sept. 23. Photo by Daniel Opasinis


“Now, you can actually see the effects of it — from 1970 and onward,” Cameron said. “A lot of birth defects, a lot of problems in the community, the body, nerve, eyesight, you name it.”


Research conducted with Grassy Narrows has examined how exposure before birth may affect vision decades later. A study published in the

International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

 compared adult retinal scans with historical measurements of mercury in participants’ umbilical-cord blood. Among the 59 participants studied, higher prenatal exposure was associated with thinner retinal layers in adulthood. 


People rally for justice for Grassy Narrows in Toronto on Sept. 23. Photo by Daniel Opasinis


Outside of the Native Canadian Centre’s

Dodem Kanonhsa’

 — a cultural facility dedicated to Elders and knowledge preservation — the march paused to honour community members who had died, with non-Indigenous allies invited to sit in the roadway for a moment of silence. 


The march resumed along Bay Street, with protestors chanting in unison.


“What happens to the water—happens to the people!”


People chant in unison at the rally on Sept. 23.


Continuing along University Avenue, the crowd finally settled outside the Ontario Legislative Building at Queen’s Park. 


People rally for justice for Grassy Narrows in Toronto on Sept. 23. Photo by Daniel Opasinis


“We travel from afar. Whitedog and Grassy united together as one. To fight this process of getting the provincial government and the federal government on board to do something about this,” Cameron said.


Organizers in the city had been instrumental in planning the rally, Cameron added. 


“Being one, as we walked through this corridor, and we all sat down, gathered here. That was the message today.”


People rally for justice for Grassy Narrows in Toronto on Sept. 23. Photo by Daniel Opasinis

author: Kate Sharpley
title: Tensions in Anarchism - Barry Pateman
content:
This is a transcript of a talk by Barry Pateman at the Bay Area Anarchist Bookfair in San Francisco. It shows something of his approach to anarchism, and the history of anarchism, and mentions some of the important people and experiences in his life. Barry spoke with passion and a greater concern for people than abstract ideas. As you’ll see, his humour (and swearing) were always self-deprecating: ‘Thank you for your time. I’m really sorry that you’ve got nothing else to do.’

I just want to talk about some tensions I think that us as anarchists or people sympathetic to anarchism need to try and consider. ’Cause… I suddenly realised last night when I was laying in bed and just looking at the ceiling that I’m tending to become a bookfair groupie. There’s a bookfair in London. I go to a bookfair in London. It’s an anarchist bookfair, I sell anarchist books. I come to San Francisco. And I’m really talking, I guess, about how we as each other, as a group, as an organisation, as people who share a similar – what Galleani called the ideal, the dream – How we gonna make that real? And so, there are some tensions I think we have to face.

The first tension is ourselves and our history. There is a history of anarchism. But within that history of anarchism, there are things and people who have been forgotten. Now, with the Kate Sharpley Library, we have two reasons to exist. One is, yes, flowers for the fallen. We printed a pamphlet called Anarchists against Franco1 where there were twenty anarchists who’d been killed between 1942 and 1960 in guerrilla warfare against Franco. And Frank Torres who wrote it in Spanish says – and I couldn’t agree more – it doesn’t matter whether you think libertarian communism, anarchism will happen, it doesn’t matter whether you think it’s silly, it doesn’t even matter if you think you’re cleverer than those anarchists who went out there. What matters is how dare we forget them? How dare you and I sitting in this room not know about them? How dare we forget their bravery and their courage when they went over the mountains against stupidly impossible odds for that dream? So, any anarchist, any person sympathetic to us has to be aware of our history, not the history of ideas, that’s something I’ll talk about in a second, but simply the people who have suffered physically and emotionally for our belief. You’ll know some of them, nah? But we’ll also not know a lot of them and one of the things we must do is to revise history, to give them that dignity of that memory.

And the second thing of course is that if we’re canny we learn from history. We have to learn. Look, I’ve been an anarchist for thirty years, so you’re not going to learn much from me because we haven’t got that far. But I do know what’ve we done wrong. I do think I’ve got an idea that what we’ve done has gone wrong. But we have to learn from our history. We can’t just pretend that we exist now and that really that those people were a bit strange or not like us because they spoke a different language. If we’re not guided by our history, we have no foundation, nothing, except living on our wits. So that I think is the first tension, how we discover and make our history come alive for all of us.

The second tension is, is between us as anarchists or sympathetic who are clever buggers ’cause we are… and ordinary people… who aren’t. I don’t mean racist, nasty people, I mean ordinary people who get up every morning, go to work, watch telly, watch baseball, go to bed… yeah? I mean those people. And you know what, there’s a lot more of them than us.

OK, so one of the things that’s disturbed me lately is there’s been a trend in anarchism to think that ordinary people are sort of fucking stupid. Yeah? They’re not clever or, really, they’re the problem. No, they’re not the problem. Look, every time there’s been some type of thing kicking off, starting, some insurrection, its come from dispossessed, poor people, ordinary people. And if we’re not there, if we don’t know them, if we’ve got no relationship with them… what’re we? Who are we? Just somebody else. It means nothing. Our relationship, surely, is with ordinary people. How we get to them. If our belief, if our dream is something that we believe in and live by and suffer by… then we have to go out there somehow. That tension is a critical one. You know, I could sit down all night and convince myself that anarchism’s tomorrow. But actually anarchism’s nothing… it’s something up here …

author: Corey Larocque
title: Education must continue to be the counter to denialism
content:
Education remains the best way to ensure Canadians understand the legacy of residential schools, to preserve the memories of children who died, and to care for survivors.


Earlier this week, after the Second Sons white nationalist group held an ominous demonstration just outside the Tk’emlúps te Secwépemc reserve near Kamloops, B.C., it became easier to understand the calls to criminalize residential school denialism.


A recurring theme at the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation ceremony on Parliament Hill, residential school denialism is becoming an alarming, disturbing phenomenon.


“We must … confront all forms of denialism that persist despite extensive historical records and an indisputable body of evidence, including first-hand survivor testimony,” Gov. Gen. Louise Arbour said during Wednesday’s event. “This leaves no room for doubt about the history and impact of the residential schools.”


Several speakers spoke to the harms caused by denialism, which is the belief that either children didn’t die at residential schools or that survivors’ experiences were not as bad as they have made it out to be.


In fact, over a century and a half, approximately 150,000 Indigenous people attended residential schools. The Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s final report notes 3,201 deaths in residential schools. Its former commissioner, Murray Sinclair, believes at least 6,000 children died as a result of their time in residential schools.


National media have reported on what appeared to be Second Sons members’ deliberately provocative acts in the days leading up to Sept. 30, the annual National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.


On the social media platform X, Prime Minister Mark Carney called “the cowardly act” an “abhorrent” display and added it was a “stark reminder” of Canadians’ responsibility to confront the consequences of the residential school system that are felt today.


He paid tribute to the courage of survivors who have shared their stories so all Canadians can work toward reconciliation.


Nunavut survivors like Iqaluit’s Jack Anawak — once again a fixture at the city’s gathering at the cadet hall — and Cambridge Bay’s Jeannie Ehaoloak, who spoke in Ottawa, contribute to that truth-telling.


In June, Nunavut Sen. Nancy Karetak-Lindell tried unsuccessfully to criminalize residential school denialism.


She tried to amend the Liberal government’s Combatting Hate Act that would have made it a crime to “willfully promote hatred” against Indigenous Peoples by “condoning, denying or downplaying the Indian Residential Schools system.”


Karetak-Lindell’s amendment was supported by the Senate’s human rights committee but was defeated in the Senate.


A week later, this editorial space argued that

education

 — not jail time — is the way to counter the denial of the harmful effects of residential schools.


As abhorrent as the Second Sons’ actions were, the most effective way to counter the misinformation that deniers spread is with the spread of accurate information.


The residential school system is a horrible, dark, painful chapter in Canada’s history. But it’s one Canadians need to come to terms with.

title: 46 countries call for executions in Iran to be halted
content:
In a report published on 1 October 2026, the Iran Human Rights Organization reported that 46 countries had called for a halt to the rising number of executions in the Islamic Republic of Iran.


According to the report, a joint statement presented by the representative of Liechtenstein at the 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council on 30 September 2026, was signed by 46 countries.


The statement said that at least 31 protesters had been executed since the crackdown on protests in December 2025 began. It also noted that dozens of people, including women and children, were at risk of execution.


Citing findings by UN experts, the signatory countries emphasized that the death penalty in Iran was being used to instill fear, suppress dissent, and restrict the freedoms of peaceful expression and assembly.


The joint statement also raised concerns about secret trials, violations of fair trial guarantees, torture and ill-treatment, enforced disappearances, and forced confessions.


The 46 countries called on the Iranian authorities to immediately end the use of the death penalty.

author: Unknown
title: Workers dismissed from Amed City Hospital construction site launch strike
content:
At the construction site of the City Hospital, currently under construction in the Peyas (Kayapınar) district of Amed, 90 members of the Construction, Road and Highway Workers’ Union employed by the main contractor and subcontractor were dismissed.


Workers who launched a strike outside the hospital construction site in protest against the dismissals received visits of support from the Amed Labor and Democracy Platform and representatives of political parties. During a statement outside the site, a banner reading “The world will belong to labor” was displayed, and protesters chanted slogans including “Gürbağ, don’t be mistaken, don’t push our patience to the limit.”


Speaking at the gathering, Sabahat Sever, co-chair of the Amed No. 2 Branch of the Genel-Iş Union, affiliated with DISK, said they stood in solidarity with construction workers who had joined a union and were fighting for their rights by exercising their constitutional rights.


Sever stated that the rights violations at the construction site were inseparable from the working conditions faced by workers across the country. She said workers were struggling for humane working conditions and wages that would allow them to make a living.


Pointing to the heavy toll imposed on the working class by capital’s pursuit of profit and the lack of oversight, Sever said workers at construction sites, mines, factories and hospitals were being employed under conditions of insecurity, pressure and low wages.


Noting that the necessary measures to prevent fatal workplace accidents were not being taken, Sever said the existing system aimed to cheapen labor and leave workers unorganized.


Workers' demands


Stating that the Amed Labor and Democracy Platform supported the struggle of the dismissed workers, Sabahat Sever listed their demands as follows:


-The immediate reinstatement of all dismissed workers.


-Full payment of unpaid wages and other outstanding entitlements, and reimbursement of unjustified wage deductions.


-An end to pressure and dismissals targeting workers for union organizing.


-Respect for workers’ trade union rights.


-The provision of humane working conditions and an end to violations of workers’ rights.


-Necessary action against those responsible for preventing workers from exercising their rights and committing violations of those rights.


Following the statement, construction workers also said they would continue their protest until their demands were met. The gathering concluded with slogans.

title: First Kurdish Film Festival kicks off in Freiburg
content:
The First Kurdish Film Festival in Freiburg, has begun at Kommunales Kino. The festival is organized by the Avesta Cultural Association, established through the joint initiative of Kurdish cinema organizations in Freiburg.


Members of the Freiburg Film Commune Organizing Committee, Newroz Sönmez and Mustafa Özel, delivered the festival’s opening speeches. They were followed by a performance by Hozan Axîn.


On the first day of the festival, “Zare,” a 1926 Armenian-language silent drama written and directed by Hamo Beknazaryan, was screened. The film, produced in the Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic, was presented on screen accompanied by a live musical performance.


The program also featured a short film by a Kurdish director born in Kirkuk who lives in Norway. The film, which tells the story of three young people living in a refugee camp in northern Norway, was screened on the festival’s opening day.


 


16 films to be screened


The three-day festival, taking place from October 2 to 4, will feature a total of 16 films: four feature films, four documentaries and eight short films.


On the second day of the festival, the documentary “Vartinis,” directed by Mehmet Ömer Biçer, will be screened at Kommunales Kino to mark the anniversary of the Vartinis Massacre.


The festival program will also feature the films Hevras, Hemo Mori, Mein Vater, der Gastarbeiter and Hevî.


The first Kurdish Film Festival to be held in Freiburg will bring audiences the work of Kurdish filmmakers from different countries and showcase a range of narratives from Kurdish cinema.

title: Temelli: A new constitution cannot be discussed without Öcalan’s involvement
content:
As the Peace and Democratic Society Process, launched following Abdullah Öcalan’s call, reaches a critical stage, Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Deputy Group Chair Sezai Temelli spoke to ANF about Turkey’s economic crisis, the government’s approach to the process, Öcalan’s status as Parliament opened.


Turkey is one of the world’s five fragile economies


Temelli addressed the recent rise in fuel prices, the fund crisis and deepening poverty in Turkey, saying that the country’s economy remained structurally fragile: “Turkey’s economy is fundamentally fragile. It is one of the five fragile economies in the world, and this fragility simply does not go away. There are many reasons for this. There are structural problems as well as administrative and institutional ones. Of course, the current political situation also has a very serious impact. As a result, this fragile economy constantly generates crises. Because of this persistent mentality of plunder, it repeatedly produces cases of profiteering and corruption.


A very significant part of Turkey’s economy is already informal, and within that informal economy there is what we call the black economy as well as the grey economy. It is an economy with high unemployment that is trying to stay afloat amid high inflation and high interest rates, but beyond that, it has failed to meet social expectations or resolve social problems. Looking at all of this, the latest fund crisis was not actually unexpected.”


Temelli said similar crises had occurred throughout the Justice and Development Party’s (AKP) many years in power, adding that the government’s approach to economic management had contributed to their emergence.


The logic of a war economy remains intact


Temelli said one of the structural problems facing Turkey’s economy was that it remained a war economy, adding that the step taken by Abdullah Öcalan and the political climate he had created presented an important opportunity for Turkey: “One of the most important structural problems in the economy is this: it is a war economy. We are going through an important period. The step taken by Mr. Öcalan, the initiative he has taken and the political climate he has created are so valuable and important that anyone looking at the situation from the outside would say this is a major opportunity for Turkey. An outside observer would see it as a major opportunity for Turkey. Why? Because this may give Turkey, perhaps for the first time, an opportunity to normalise both its politics and its economy.


The impact of the process is not reflected in the 2027 budget. We are faced with a government that still retains the logic and underlying structures of a war economy.”


The issue is still approached as a fight against terrorism


Temelli said Turkey’s economy could improve if a significant proportion of the resources allocated to the war were redirected to the economy: “More than $40 billion a year is spent on the war. There is now an opportunity to redirect at least two-thirds of the resources allocated to the war economy. That would amount to around $20–25 billion. For Turkey’s economy, $20–25 billion could provide a significant means of improvement. But that option has not been chosen. This is the first structural problem, and despite the profound impact this process could have, no steps are being taken to address it. That is because we are still faced with an approach that views the issue as a fight against terrorism and continues to shape its politics accordingly.”


Democracy and the economy must advance together


Temelli said economic problems could not be addressed separately from democratisation, arguing that the absence of democracy in politics led to greater corruption in the economy: “First and foremost, this government is avoiding democracy. If there is no democracy in politics, there will also be a great deal of corruption in the economy. We need to understand that the two go hand in hand. The more democratic politics becomes, the more democratic the economy becomes. Democratising the economy essentially means ensuring economic justice. This government is avoiding that. We are faced with a government that has nothing to do with democracy, either in politics or in the economy. What does it do? It uses an authoritarian political system to create an economic sphere for profiteering and plunder.”

title: Journalist Derya Okatan remanded in custody
content:
Derya Okatan, a journalist and member of the Disciplinary Board of the Press-Iş union of the Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Turkey (DISK), was detained at her home in Ankara and taken to Istanbul Çağlayan Courthouse. Okatan was referred to a judge with a request for her arrest without even having her statement taken by the prosecutor. The court subsequently ordered Derya Okatan’s detention pending trial.


The Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG) reacted to Derya Okatan’s arrest. The DFG said: “We stand with Derya Okatan against the criminalization of journalistic activities and attempts to silence journalists through pressure and arrests, and we demand her immediate release. Journalism is not a crime.”

title: KNK conference begins: Kurds seek representation and status at the UN
content:
The Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) hosts a conference in Brussels with the aim of securing Kurdish representation at the United Nations (UN) and gaining international status, has begun. Attended by representatives of political parties and organizations from the four parts of Kurdistan and various countries around the world, as well as academics and experts in international law, the conference will discuss diplomatic efforts aimed at ensuring that 60 million Kurds are represented internationally with their own identity and political will.


The conference, held at Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB), is attended by American legal expert Barry Fisher, academic Miloon Kothari, who has worked within the United Nations, and his wife, as well as former Icelandic Foreign Minister Ögmundur Jónasson, and Coni Ledesma, who works in the field of international law.


The conference began with the singing of the Kurdish anthem “Ey Reqîb” and a one-minute silence. This was followed by the election of the conference presidium. Fehmi Vergili, Nilüfer Koç and Wirya Qaradaxi were elected to the presidium.


Nilüfer Koç: Why don’t Kurds speak in their own name?


Delivering the first speech on behalf of the presidium, Nilüfer Koç drew attention to the fact that Kurds have been left without a name or identity in the international arena for nearly a century. Asking, “Why don’t Kurds, like other nations, speak in their own name?” Koç stated that the main purpose of the conference was to discuss this question and the issue of Kurdish representation at the international level. She said that the identity of 60 million Kurds and their right to representation would be addressed, adding that the KNK has been working intensively on this initiative for nearly a year.


Zeynep Murad: A long-term and strategic mission


KNK Co-Chair Zeynep Murad said that they have been carrying out diplomatic efforts for nearly a year and have held meetings with political parties and organizations in Kurdistan. Stating that these efforts have been conducted by the KNK’s diplomacy group, Murad emphasized that the mission is long-term and strategic in nature.


“Sixty million people live in their own geography with their culture and identity. Yet they have no representation in an international institution. Today, we will hold a discussion on this issue,” she said.


Karamus: A common national position must be developed


KNK Co-Chair Ahmet Karamus said that the conference marked a historic day for the Kurdish people’s struggle. Stating that the demand for status in all four parts of Kurdistan and representation at the UN has now emerged as a common agenda, Karamus said:


“Today is a historic day in the Kurdish people’s struggle. Today is a day when the issue of the Kurdish people’s status in all four parts has taken shape in people’s minds. All four parts now demand representation and status at the UN.”


Karamus said that serious, sensitive and risky changes are taking place around the world, in the Middle East and across the four parts of Kurdistan, adding that the emerging new process brings both risks and significant opportunities for the Kurdish movement and the future of the Kurdish people.


Emphasizing that successfully advancing this process is essential for the existence, will and struggle of the Kurdish people, Karamus stressed the need to develop unity and a common national position in the face of the threats confronting them. He said that the application process initiated to secure status for the Kurdish people at the UN would contribute to greater Kurdish unity, adding, “Our people must remain united throughout this process.”


Karamus noted that the KNK has so far made intensive efforts toward national unity but has not yet achieved the desired results. He said that, as part of preparations for the UN application, a delegation had been formed to conduct work in different regions in order to assess and discuss the situation on the ground.


He stated that the planned work had been carried out in Rojava, Bakur and Europe, while meetings had also been held in Sulaymaniyah, Qandil and Hewlêr (Erbil).


Karamus stated that meetings with all political parties and sides had yielded positive results, saying: “For the first time, we held meetings and discussions with all political parties and the administration in Bashur (South) Kurdistan. title: Vartinis katliamında yaşamını yitirenler anıldı
content:
Muş – Muş Demokratik Kurumlar Platformu, 33 yıl önce Vartinis beldesinde 7'si çocuk 9 kişinin yakılarak katledildiği Vartinis Katliamı'nın yıldönümü dolayısıyla, Vartinis Müzesi'ne doğru yürüyüş gerçekleştirdi. Belde merkezinden müzeye doğru gerçekleşen yürüyüşte Türkçe ve Kürtçe “Em ê komkujîya Vartînîse jibîr nekin û nedin jibîrkirin” pankartı açıldı. Yürüyüşte sık sık alkış ve zılgıtlar eşliğinde "Şehîd namirin" sloganları atılırken, çok sayıda yurttaş katıldı. Yürüyüşün ardından Vartinis Müzesi önünde basın açıklaması gerçekleştirildi.

Katliamda ailesinden 9 kişiyi kaybeden ve şans eseri kurtulan Aysel Öğüt, askerler tarafından ailesinin yakılarak katledildiğini belirtti. Zulüm ve katliamı kabul etmediğini söyleyen Aysel Öğüt, "Ailem ne yaptı? 33 yıldır acısı yüreğimde. Tüm köy halkının yüreğinde. Acımız büyük ve unutulmayacak. Vartînîs'in tarihi olan bir acı. En küçük kardeşim süt emiyordu. Ne yapmış olabilir? Katliamı kabul etmiyorum. İçimdeki acıyı ancak Allah bilir" ifadelerini kullandı.

Ardından konuşan Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi Muş İl Eş Başkanı İlyas Aslan, yaşanan katliamın Kürt halkında büyük etki yarattığını belirtti. Katliamın yargılamasının gerçeğe rağmen kapatıldığını ifade eden Aslan, "Katliamın zaman aşımı olmaz. Dava bugün AYM’de. AYM’den gerçekten adil bir karar bekliyor ve faillere ceza vermesini istiyoruz. Dersîm, Zilan, Roboskî katliamlarından Vartinis’e kadar hiç bir yargılama gerçekleştirilmedi. Failler cezasız kaldı. Onurlu bir barış için bu katliamların ailelerin talebi dikkate alınarak çözüme kavuşturulmalıdır. Almanya şansölyesi Brant Polonya’da Yahudi Katliamının simge yerlerinden birine giderek burada Yahudi halkından özür dilemişti. Biz de buradan başta Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan olmak üzere tüm hükümet ve devlet yetkililerine sesleniyoruz. Bu halkın taleplerine kulak verilmeli ve bu katliamlar için özür dilenmelidir. Biz bu barışı tüm Türkiye halkları için istiyoruz. Eğer bu acıyı paylaşıyorsak buna dair karşılıklı adımlar atmalıyız. Bu katliamlar bir daha yaşanmasın diye her yıl bu anmaları yapmaya devam edeceğiz" diye konuştu.

Konuşmaların ardından kitle Vartinis Müzesini ziyaret etti. Müzede katliamda yaşamını yitirenler için dua okundu. Okunan duanın ardından müzenin bahçesinde yaşamını yitirenler için saygı duruşuna duruldu. Saygı duruşunda atılan "Şehîd namirin" sloganlarının ardından, anma sona erdi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: DİH okullarda 1 öğün ücretsiz yemek hakkını AYM’ye taşıdı
content:
Demokrasi İçin Hukukçular (DİH), okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı yemek hakkı için verilen mücadeleyi Anayasa Mahkemesine taşıdı. Sosyal medya hesaplarında yaptıkları açıklamada, “Anayasa Mahkemesinin çocukların eşit-parasız eğitim, maddi ve manevi varlığını geliştirme hakkını önceleyen bir karar vermesini talep etmek hakkımız” ifadeleri kullanıldı.

DİH açıklamasında; kadınların, sendikaların, siyasi partilerin ve meslek örgütlerinin sürdürdüğü mücadele sonucu 2022-2023 eğitim öğretim yılının ikinci yarısından itibaren okul öncesi eğitimdeki öğrencilere uygulanan ücretsiz beslenme uygulamasının 11 Eylül 2023’te Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı (MEB) tarafından kaldırıldığı hatırlatıldı.

Uygulamanın kaldırılması üzerine MEB’e açılan davada Danıştay 8. Dairesinin “devletin mali kaynaklarının yetersizliği, idarenin çocuklara yemek vermekte takdir serbestisi olduğunu” belirttiği dile getirilerek davanın reddedildiği ifade edildi. Bu durumun çocukların üstün yararı, Anayasa ve uluslararası sözleşmeleri göz ardı eden bir karar olduğu belirtilerek 2 Ekim 2026’da Anayasa Mahkemesine başvurulduğu ilan edildi.

Türkiye’de yaşanan fon vurgununa işaret edilen açıklamada, “İktidar temsilcilerinin, çocukların açlığını temel gündem yapması gereken eski Aile Bakanı ve pek çok iktidar elitinin haksız işlemlerle edindiği kişisel servetin, fonculara akan kaynağın ‘çok küçük bir kısmı’ bile çocukların beslenmesini sağlayabilirdi” denildi.

Çocuk açlığını devletin takdir yetkisine bırakan sürecin “Ailem Güvende” operasyonlarıyla da birlikte değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini belirtilerek, “Çocuğun beslenme sorununu çözemeyen aileler güvende değildir, kimlerin ve hangi ailelerin güvende olduğunu ise hep birlikte görmekteyiz” ifadeleri kullandı.

Çocuk açlığına karşı, her çocuğun eğitim hakkına eşit bir biçimde erişebilmek için mücadelenin devam edeceği söylenen açıklamada, “Anayasa Mahkemesinin çocukların eşit-parasız eğitim, maddi ve manevi varlığını geliştirme hakkını önceleyen bir karar vermesini talep etmek hakkımız” denildi.

author: Unknown
title: [Lecture] La rafle du Vél'd'Hiv, Maurice Rajsfus
content:
Loin d'être la seule, la rafle du Vél' d'Hiv reste la plus importante et la plus emblématique des opérations antijuives menées par la police française, «

 

corps de fonctionnaires ayant perdu ses repères

 

», pendant l'occupation nazie. Maurice Rajsfus, fin connaisseur des archives de cette période, analyse tous les aspects de cet évènement, dans l'espoir «

 

d'alerter les citoyens d'un pays libre sur les dérives des pouvoirs forts

 

».


Il rappelle tout d'abord rapidement la tradition xénophobe française, le premier statut des Juifs de France, dès 1937, par Louis Darquier, dit de Pellepoix, les décrets-lois Daladier, l'année suivante, qui permirent l'assignation à résidence des étrangers en situation irrégulière, puis l'internement dans des camps de concentration des «

 

débris des armées républicaines espagnoles

 

», celui des ressortissants allemands résidant en France, à partir d'octobre 1939, essentiellement des antifascistes et des Juifs, qui seront d'ailleurs livrés au nazis l'année suivante.


«

 

 Bien avant que l'Allemagne nazie, qui occupe les trois cinquièmes de la France, ne dicte sa loi au gouvernement de la zone dite libre, Pétain et ses ministres se préoccupent déjà de réprimer les étrangers, “cause des malheurs“ du pays et, plus directement, les Juifs

.

 

» À partir de juillet 1940, différentes lois écartent les juifs de certaines professions, médicales, judiciaires, puis commerciales et industrielles un peu plus tard.

 Le 3 octobre le premier statut des juifs de France est édicté, «

 

 selon des critères plus drastiques que ceux des nazis

 

».


Le 14 mai 1941, 6000 juifs étrangers de Paris sont convoqués au commissariat de leur quartier et les 3800 qui vont se présenter sont envoyés et internés dans deux camps du Loiret. Maurice Rajsfus illustre ces événements avec des extraits de circulaires officielles et des articles de presse, notamment d'extrême-droite.


Puis le 20 août, une rafle limitée au 11

e

 arrondissement, est décidée par les Autorités allemandes, pour tester «

 

la bonne volonté des cadres comme de la base policière

 

».


L'organisation des services de renseignements (en particulier la constitution du fichier juif à la préfecture de police, sous la responsabilité de l'inspecteur André Tulard), de police et de gendarmerie, est présentée, ainsi que leur synergie avec les services allemands. À la fin du mois d'avril 1942, avec le retour de Pierre Laval à la tête du gouvernement de Vichy, René Bousquet accède an poste de secrétaire général de la police.


La préparation de la rafle du Vél' d'Hiv proprement dite, est ensuite exposée en détail. Ainsi, une note adressée le 6 juillet par le

SS

 Dannecker à Adolf Eichmann, suite à sa rencontre avec René Bousquet, révèle que «

 

 le président Laval a proposé que, lors de l'évacuation des familles juives de zone non occupée les enfants de moins de seize ans soient emmenés eux aussi

 

». Le compte rendu du conseil des ministres du 10 juillet confirme que «

 

 dans un souci d'humanité, le chef du gouvernement a obtenu – contrairement aux premières propositions allemandes – que les enfants, y compris ceux de 16 ans, soient autorisés à accompagner leurs parents

 

».


Maurice Rajsfus évoque également des «

 

fuites

 

» venant «

 

de trop rares fonctionnaires de police

 

» permettant à un certain nombre de familles de se cacher. De son côté, l'Union générale des Israélites de France (

UGIF

) et d'autres institutions, informées de la date approximative de la rafle, n'ont aucune volonté de prévenir. Au contraire, l'organisation Solidarité, des communistes juifs immigrés, diffusent un trac très bien informé, avertissant de la «

 

rafle monstre

 

» qui n'épargnera ni les femmes ni les enfants. Par ailleurs, des rumeurs et des fausses nouvelles sont aussi propagées presque quotidiennement.


Il décrit ensuite avec la plus grande précision le déroulement des opérations, depuis le décompte des effectifs de fonctionnaires mobilisés, des interpellations heure par heure, des tentatives de suicide, des accouchements, etc. De très nombreux témoignages sont aussi rapportés. Puis les conditions abominables de détention au Vélodrome d'Hiver sont longuement détaillées : eau coupée, odeur pestilentielle, mares de déjections, fausses couches, cas de folies, tentatives de suicides, la trentaine de morts dont plusieurs enfants. Quelques évasions réussissent. Les rapports des évacuations vers les camps de Drancy …

author: Unknown
title: İbrahim Gündem’in kız kardeşi: Kemiklerine kavuşmadan ölmek istemiyorum
content:
Cumartesi Anneleri/İnsanları, gözaltında zorla kaybedilen yakınlarının akıbetinin açıklanması ve sorumluların yargılanması talebiyle Galatasaray Meydanı’nda 1123’üncü kez bir araya geldi.


Hak savunucularının da katıldığı buluşmada gözaltında kaybedilen ve öldürülenlerin fotoğrafları ile karanfiller taşındı.


Bu haftaki açıklamada, 25 Eylül 1991’de Diyarbakır’ın Hazro ilçesinde askerler tarafından evinden alınan ve bir daha kendisinden haber alınamayan İbrahim Gündem’in dosyası hatırlatıldı.


Basın açıklamasını İnsan Hakları Derneği (İHD) Merkez Yürütme Kurulu üyesi Gülseren Yoleri okudu.


Fotoğraf: Mezopotamya Ajansı


İbrahim Gündem’e ne oldu?


Yoleri, 39 yaşındaki İbrahim Gündem’in Hazro’ya bağlı Sarıerik (Qenderhel) köyünde ailesiyle çiftçilik ve hayvancılık yaptığını anlattı.


Açıklamaya göre, 25 Eylül 1991 gecesi saat 01.00 sıralarında Üsteğmen Kenan Şahin komutasındaki askerler Gündem’in evine baskın yaptı.


Gündem, ailesinin ve köylülerin gözü önünde gözaltına alınarak götürüldü. Müdahale etmek isteyen babasına, oğlunun ertesi gün serbest bırakılacağı söylendi.


Ancak aile ertesi gün karakola gittiğinde, Gündem’in gözaltına alınmadığı yanıtını aldı.


Yoleri, İbrahim Gündem dosyasının aradan geçen 35 yıla rağmen etkin biçimde soruşturulmadığını söyledi.


35 Yıldır Soruyoruz: İbrahim Gündem Nerede?

https://t.co/MhfiJN9QwG


— Cumartesi Anneleri (@CmrtesiAnneleri)

October 3, 2026


Ailenin başvuruları sonuçsuz kaldı


Gündem ailesi, İbrahim Gündem’in akıbetini öğrenmek için önce Hazro Cumhuriyet Savcılığı’na başvurdu.


Yoleri’nin aktardığına göre savcılık aileyi karakola yönlendirdi, karakola verilen dilekçelere ise yanıt verilmedi.


Baba Ahmet Gündem daha sonra Diyarbakır Valiliği’ne başvurdu. Valiliğin girişiminin ardından karakoldan yine “Biz almadık” yanıtı geldi.


Ahmet Gündem, İl Jandarma Alay Komutanlığı’na yaptığı başvuruda ise “Devleti suçluyorsun, devlet böyle şeyler yapmaz” denilerek azarlandı ve tehdit edildi.


Yoleri, ailenin baskı ve tehditler altında sürdürdüğü arayıştan sonuç alamadığını belirtti.


“Adaleti sağlamak devletin görevidir”


Açıklamada Gündem ailesinin üzerindeki baskıların sonraki yıllarda da sürdüğü ifade edildi.


15 Şubat 1993’te evlerinin askerler ve korucular tarafından yakılmasının ardından ailenin Diyarbakır’a göç etmek zorunda kaldığı belirtildi.


Yoleri, İbrahim Gündem’i aramaktan vazgeçmeyen anne ve babasının, oğullarının akıbetini öğrenemeden yaşamlarını yitirdiğini söyledi.


Şöyle devam etti:


Gündem Ailesi’nin 35 yıldır adalete ulaşamamasının nedeni, devletin etkin bir soruşturma yürütmemesidir. İbrahim Gündem’in akıbetini ortaya çıkarmak, sorumluları belirlemek ve adaleti sağlamak devletin görevidir.


“Kaybeden devletti, nasıl götürdüyse, öyle geri getirsin”


Buluşmada İHD üyesi Ümmühan Kaya, İbrahim Gündem’in kız kardeşi Feride Gündem’in gönderdiği mesajı da okudu.


Feride Gündem, anne ve babasının yaşamları boyunca oğullarından bir haber beklediğini belirterek şöyle dedi:


"Annemin ve babamın bıraktığı yerden ağabeyimi arıyoruz. Her Cumartesi saat 12.00’de Koşuyolu Parkı’nda ağabeyimin fotoğrafını taşıyoruz. Abim İbrahim’in kaybolduğu günden bugüne bir gün dahi huzur bulamadık."


Gündem, ağabeyinin kalıntılarına ulaşmak istediğini söyleyerek şöyle devam etti:


Ben de onun kemiklerine kavuşmadan ölmek istemiyorum. Bu hayattaki tek dileğim bu. Başka bir şey istemiyorum. 35 yıldır ağabeyimi arıyoruz. Onu alıp götüren, kaybeden devletti. Nasıl götürdüyse, öyle geri getirsin.


Ailenin mücadeleyi sürdüreceğini vurgulayan Gündem, “Biz bu davayı bırakmayacağız. Annem ve babam kardeşimi bulamadan yaşamlarını yitirdiler. Biz de onların izindeyiz. Ağabeyimi bulana, mezarına kavuşana kadar mücadelemizden vazgeçmeyeceğiz” dedi.


Buluşma, karanfillerin Galatasaray Meydanı’na bırakılmasıyla sona erdi.


(NÖ)

title: Vê hefteyê di biamag kurdiyê de
content:
biamaga kurdî ya vê hefteyê bi edîtoriya Aren Yıldırım û Ferhat Yaşar hat amadekirin. 


biamaga kurdî di vê hefteya xwe de cih dide xebat û lêkolînên li ser mijarên weke wêje, muzîk, serpêhatî, huner, helbest, zanist, ziman, tenduristî û wêjeyê.


Rûpelek nû ji bo bianet kurdiyê: biamag kurdî


5 Îlon 2026


Ev naveroka berfireh a ku vê hefteyê tê pêşkêşkirin, bi analîzên di qadên wêje, ziman, huner û muzîkê de hewl dide ku valahiya di vê qadê de ji bo xwêneran tijî bike. biamaga kurdî bi tevlêkirina nivîsên di warê zanist û tenduristiyê de, çarçoveya xwe ya weşanê ji sînorên rojeva siyasî derbas dike û ber bi hilberîna zanîna piralî ve dibe.


Naverokên vê hefteyê weha ne:


Sinem Aydinli

 di vê nivîsê de behsa çîroka xwe ya hînbûna kurdî dike û vê yekê di çarçoveya berpirsiyariya etîk û zextên siyasî û dîrokî yên li ser ziman de dinirxîne.


Samî Tan

 di nivîsa xwe de balê dikişîne ser daxwaza Kurdan a ji bo perwerdehiya bi zimanê dayikê. Her weha Tan modela waneyên vebijêrkî ya dewletê weke çareserî nabîne û weke polîtîkaya pişaftinê dinirxîne. "Modela Perwerdehiya Pirzimanî ya li ser Bingeha Zimanê Zikmakî" weke çareserî pêşniyar dike.


Dilşah Kaymaz

 bi analîz û rexneyeke kûr a sosyo-ekonomîk û çandî balê dikişîne ser bandora kapîtalîzma platformên dîjîtal û zextên algorîtmayan a li ser muzîka bi zimanê kêmneteweyan/bindestan.


Eser Çetin

 vê hefteyê jî li ser tenduristiyê nivîsiye. Bi zimanekî sade û fêmbar behsa apandîsitê kiriye. Çetin di nivîsê de hem têgehên bijîşkî radigihîne hem jî bi mînakên ji ziman û jiyana rojane mijarê şênber dike.


Berîvan Kayî

di nivîsa xwe de tecrûbeyeke vegantiyê û çîroka jiyanê ya aktivîsteke laz bi hev ve girê dide û behsa hevdîtina kampa veganan li Westana Wanê dike.


Mazhar Rojava

 di nivîsa xwe ya bi navê “Nivîsîn: Karê yezdan û sihêrbazan” de bi zimanekî wêjeyî û hestiyar behsa têkiliya xwe ya kûr û tevlihev a bi nivîsandinê re dike.


Ayşenur Ozelê

di nivîsa xwe ya vê hefteyê de geşedaneke girîng a fîzîk û teknolojiya quantûmî aniye pêşberî xwendevanan. 


Mehmet Erbeyi

 bi zimanekî xweş, herêmî, resen û bi şêwazekî mizahî û xwerû behsa serhatiya xwe ya tal û bi êş a çûna cem dixtorê diran kiriye.


Dilşêr Bêwar

 bi rêya metafor, hêmanên xwezayê, helbestiyeta ziman û hestên kûr ên aîdiyetê, behsa rastiya jiyanê dike.


Siya Robîn

 di vê nivîsa xwe de nirxandina berhema helbestvan Lal Laleş a bi navê

“Talibên Eşqê”

 dike.


Pêşniyara guhdarkirinê ya vê hefteyê


(AY)

author: groundxero
title: A Tale of Irony: The Sijimali Story from Odisha
content:
Vedanta’s Sijimali bauxite mining project has thrown Odisha’s Rayagada and Kalahandi districts into the eye of a storm. The predominantly tribal communities living in the villages at the foothills of Sijimali are opposing the project and the State has come down heavily on them.


 


Dr. Sankalpa Satapathy


 


Vedanta Limited’s Sijimali bauxite mining project aimed at supplying bauxite to the Lanjigarh refinery has thrown Odisha’s Rayagada and Kalahandi districts into the eye of a storm. The predominantly tribal, Kui speaking Kondh and Paraja communities have strongly opposed the project and the State has come down heavily on them. The violent clashes between the villagers and police personnel on April 7, 2026 were only the tip of the iceberg. The resistance has been ongoing for years now.


 


For the people living in the villages at the foothills of Sijimali, the mountain range, the forests, the streams are not just resources to be used but an integral part of their lives, an ecosystem that pervades every aspect of their lives. The dense deciduous forests along with non-timber produce, traditional ancestral lands, non-human dwellers and the watershed that these forested mountain range harbour, sustain traditional livelihoods and support the local economy. During lean agricultural seasons, families survive on wild food such as tubers, roots, fruits etc. They rely on deep traditional ecological knowledge built over centuries and transmitted through generations in orally codified forms which emphasize sustainable use rather than exploitation to maintain ecological balance. Indigenous community driven techniques and practices harvest, store, and manage rainwater and groundwater, protect trees, soil, and wildlife and use medicinal herbs, roots, leaves and barks for treatment of illnesses. They are culturally and traditionally deeply linked to these forests believing that their deity “Tij Raja” resides in the mountains. They get everything from the mountains and do not buy anything from outside adhering to Gandhi’s concept of self-sufficiency, Swadeshi and Gram Swaraj which focused on village independence, local production and simple living.


 


Beneath these forests lies an estimated reserve of 311 million tonnes of bauxite which is fundamental for the smooth running of the Vedanta Lanjigarh refinery to drive

“growth and development of the region”

. To reach the bauxite, the communities have to be displaced, the forests have to be felled and the mountains have to be dug in a large open cast mine. In short, the entire ecosystem has to be disrupted and destroyed. Felling forests in the mountain range leads to washing off of the rich top soil which is held together by the tree roots. These forests “catch” rain and refill underground aquifers, elevating water tables and nourishing local streams. Losing forests reduces local humidity and rain making the region hotter and drier.


 


The soil erosion, disruption of the local water cycle, destruction of natural wind and dust barriers turn fertile land dry and barren, leading to desertification. Ironically, India has ratified major UN environmental treaties like the UN Convention to Combat Desertification in 1996 and the Paris Agreement in 2016. After data confirmed that July 2023 was the hottest in recorded human history, the Secretary General of the United Nations, Antonio Guterres declared that “the era of global warming has ended, the era of global boiling has arrived”. It was in the same year 2023 that the auction of bauxite mining lease for Sijimali by the government of Odisha was won by Vedanta Ltd which as explained before, if comes to fruition will lead to desertification and add to the already soaring summer temperatures in Odisha.


 


Both the districts, Rayagada and Kalahandi, are designated as Scheduled Areas and fall under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution which exists to protect indigenous tribal communities, preserve their unique culture, and prevent their economic exploitation. A Tribes Advisory Council (TAC) with mostly tribal members is mandatorily set up to advice on tribal welfare in these areas. This raises the question that if all necessary legislative procedures were followed why are the tribals up in arms in dissent against the state and why is there a military buildup in the areas? Why are there allegations from the tribals that the signatures on the Gram Sabha documents are in English whereas the people of the region write in Odia or …

author: Unknown
title: ‘a glimpse of empire wondering at the actions of empire.’
content:
elodieunderglass

:

brehaaorgana

:

elodieunderglass

:

Not to get too real on main, but I live in a part of the UK where USAmerican fighter jets have been flying out in the morning - South, of course - and returning in the evening. It is impossible not to notice them. And myself and my friends and neighbours say, “crikey, off to Iran again,” because. Well, of course the USA doesn’t have the resource to regularly cross the Atlantic just to do that; wars in the Middle East are best fought from bases in the Old World; thus, even Trump maintains a fiction of politeness with The United Kingdom, as everyone knows, for the American airbases that are enshrined as a WW2 courtesy, allowing American access to Europe and the Middle East.

“Off to Iran,” we comment, looking up - you can’t help but look up - but we don’t know that for sure, of course. It’s not on Flightradar, not on the news; probably a secret, except it’s

our bloody sky and you can’t help but notice.

What are they doing? Friends say, with authority;

they’re fighter jets and bombers

, but I can’t say I know with authority. They leave and come back. Is there a bombing campaign we don’t know about? Do they flatten the sky over Iran, just to show off? There will be a flight path, country to country in a long linked line, whose stories will match up, where we could all work out what they’re doing; but who could follow that thread?

Do Americans know?

Everyone says they’re going to Iran - they certainly started flying distraction-low over us around then; they’re low-flying, impossible to hide. Are they? They certainly seem to thicken up - tearing apart the sky and frightening the children and setting all the dogs to bark - whenever America rattles a new sabre. But why? Of course there is not official information about why one must tolerate them. British people gather and complain and criticise, especially when they crash horribly through a Teams meeting or a conversation. They cannot quite talk about the planes like British people talk about weather; they’re fighter jets, and fearful, and still British people wonder;

is it a secret? Is it bad to notice them? Is it polite?

Perhaps it will simply be useful for future historians to know, in  2026, in a corner of England, people looked up and wondered, and worried, and put their heads down again: not knowing what it meant, and not liking it all.

Today my friend shaded her eyes, the children around us - we have seven between us - going silent and pointing like dogs at the planes. They screamed overhead - the end of the world -

with friends like these who needs anemones.

(Their shapes are bad, if you don’t know.)

 My friend said, simply, with sincerity, “I hate them so much.”

I was so very glad that she had admitted to having noticed them that I bumped her, affectionately, shoulder to shoulder.

What a good friend she is! Admitting to the planes!

Do you know about the planes? There are so many, so loud, so often - going and coming back -

Idk what is meant by

“it’s not on the news” and “not knowing what it meant at all…” Because it’s very much on the news and has been for the majority of the year thus far.

Reuters

 20 March 2026

The guardian

 12 Apr 2026

BBC

 24 July 2026

Air & Space Forces

 magazine 4 September 2026

Your

Commons Library

 which, and this isn’t me joking, idk if the prime minister who said “On 1 March 2026, the Prime Minister also said that the US could use UK military bases for a “specific and limited defensive purpose”, which he said was to “destroy the [Iranian] missiles at source”. On 20 March the government said that US use of the bases also includes “US defensive operations to degrade the missile sites and capabilities being used to attack ships” in Hormuz. Bases to be used are Diego Garcia (British Indian Ocean Territory/Chagos Archipelago) and RAF Fairford (Gloucestershire).” Is the prime minister you currently have?

But it’s not a secret when your prime minister said it out loud to everybody? Announced it, even?

this post is also interesting to me because I think it does make a valid point (some Americans

don’t

 really *think* about the global impact of our military bases)

 but it’s also like…a glimpse of empire wondering at the actions of empire. As if removed, somehow…? Different somehow?

You know the UK maintains 145 overseas military installations across 42 different countries, right? At least 60 are directly run by British Armed Forces, 17 of those in Cyprus …

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 3 octobre
content:
L'éphéméride des luttes du 3 octobre soutient les grèves, celles de la faim comme celle des cheminots. En bref, elle soutient celles et ceux qui luttent contre des conditions de vie toujours plus dures afin d'ouvrir la voie à une libération collective et totale.


1920 :

 En Angleterre, grève d'un million de mineurs contre l'allongement du temps de travail.


1975 :

 A Sienne en Italie, le siège du comité provincial de la Démocratie Chrétienne (le parti au pouvoir) est incendié.


1977 :

 A Rome, l'enterrement de Walter Rossi, assassiné le

30 septembre

 par les fascistes, a lieu à San Giovanni. Deux manifestations en partent pour se diriger vers un siège bien connu du MSI, le nouveau parti fasciste. Des affrontements s'y déroulent avec la police qui défend le local. Le deuxième cortège se dirige ailleurs, incendie un camion des carabinieri et attaque un bar fréquenté par les fascistes, qui est complètement détruit, tandis qu'un incendie et une charge de dynamite détruisent entièrement un autre siège du MSI. Des voitures sont incendiées et un policier est blessé par une balle reçue dans la nuque, tandis qu'une troisième antenne des fascistes est attaquée.


1981 :

 - A Belfast en Irlande du Nord, fin de la grève de la faim des prisonniers de l'IRA après 7 mois de grève tournante. Dix militants sont morts lors de cette grève de la faim.


 A Paris, une manifestation antinucléaire réunit autour de 5000 personnes. En fin de manifestation, des affrontements ont lieu entre les autonomes et la police : la porte du ministère des Transports est enfoncée et un véhicule présent dans la cour est incendié, tandis que les fenêtres sont brisées.


1984 :

 A Dilbeek (Bruxelles), les Cellules Communistes Combattantes (CCC) incendient les camions stockés dans le dépôt de la société MAN Truck, l'un des plus gros constructeurs militaires allemands. Vous pouvez retrouver le communiqué de l'action à

cette adresse

, ainsi que des photos.


1993 :

 En Allemagne, dernières actions des Cellules Révolutionnaires (RZ) contre des véhicules de la police des frontières à Francfort-sur-l'Oder et Görlitz.


2006 :

 A Silver Springs, dans le Maryland aux États-Unis, un groupe autonome revendique une nouvelle attaque contre un centre de recrutement de l'armée afin de saboter la machine de guerre américaine.


2014 :

 - Au Chili, mort de l'ancien militant du FPMR (groupe de lutte armée contre la dictature de Pinochet) Jorge Saldivia au cours d'une

attaque de fourgon bancaire

.


 A Santiago, toujours au Chili, sur un campus universitaire, le 'Groupe Anarchiste Coordonné (GAC) Bande Organisée Mauricio Morales / Cellule Incendiaire Sebastián Oversluij'

bloque les rues avec des pneus enflammés puis attaque la police au molotov

.


2017 :

 A Murcia en Espagne, des affrontements ont lieu contre la police après trois semaines de manifestions contre une nouvelle ligne de TGV. Des barricades

sont dressées et incendiées

 en travers des routes.


2018 :

 Tard le soir, une voiture de Bouygues

est incendiée

 dans le 17ème à Paris en soutien "aux anarchistes torturé-e-s et emprisonné-es en Russie, ainsi qu'aux 8 de Bâle qui passeront en procès fin octobre pour une déambulation sauvage et saccageuse un soir de juin 2016".


Voir aussi

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 3 octobre.

author: Gastbeitrag
title: Wer hat Angst vor der DDR?
content:
Diskussionsaufschlag zur Notwendigkeit eines wissenschaftlichen Bezugs auf die eigene,


sozialistische Geschichte für die kommunistischen Aufbauorganisationen der BRD


Debattenbeitrag von

Rote Wende Leipzig


Von der revolutionären Sozialdemokratie Liebknechts und Bebels über die USPD und KPD durch die historische Zäsur des faschistischen Massenmordes auch an deutschen Kommunisten bis hin zu den sogenannten „K-Gruppen“ der 1970er und 1980er Jahre – so liest sich die historische Selbstverordnung der kommunistischen Bewegung in einem kürzlich erschienen LCM-Artikel, in dem darüber hinaus viel vom sogenannten „Kontinuitätsproblem“ roter Gruppen die Rede ist, denen sich lebendig entwickelnde, politische Bezugspunkte aus dem eigenen Land mit Verbot der KPD 1956 quasi abhanden gekommen worden wären. Damit steht der Autor bei weitem nicht alleine da: Erst im Sommer dieses Jahres durften wir staunend dem Vortrag einer bundesweiten, kommunistischen Struktur entnehmen, dass man in Deutschland ja leider Gottes keine direkten historischen Bezugspunkte zum Sozialismus hat. Es hätte kein plakativeres Beispiel dafür geben können, dass „bundesweit“ in unserer Bewegung auch heutzutage noch in den meisten Fällen ein Synonym für „westdeutsch“ bleibt.


Die Tatsache, dass es von 1949 bis 1990 einen sozialistischen Staat in Deutschland gab, wird in öffentlichen Beiträgen von bzw. Diskussionen mit den meisten roten Organisationen geflissentlich ausgespart. Das Verhältnis unserer im Aufschwung befindlichen Bewegung zur eigenen sozialistischen Geschichte ist dadurch maßgeblich von einem erstaunlichen Ausmaß an Ignoranz geprägt. Dabei ist diese Ignoranz kein Zufall, sondern Konsequenz aus über 35 Jahren harter antikommunistischer Arbeit: Neben der totalen wirtschaftlichen und politischen Annexion der DDR wurden nach 1990 Tonnen von Büchern und Archivmaterial vernichtet, stolze DDR- Bürger aus sämtlichen Führungspositionen in Kulturbetrieb, Bildungswesen und Medienlandschaft entfernt und in den Städten hunderte Symbolbauten, aber auch einfache Wohnsiedlungen abgerissen und dabei teilweise ganz bewusst der Eindruck der Vorkriegszeit architektonisch wieder hergestellt (z.B. Innenstadt Dresden, Museumsinsel Berlin).


Das „demokratische Erfolgsprojekt deutsche Einheit“ war gleichzeitig ein überaus erfolgreiches Programm des BRD-Monopolkapitals, die Erfolge des Sozialismus im eigenen Land so schnell wie möglich zu verleugnen und (im wortwörtlichen Sinne) verschwinden zu lassen. Wie für unsere Genossen in anderen Ländern der Welt auch muss doch aber der politische Kampf für Partei, Revolution und Sozialismus dort ansetzen, wo er historisch zuletzt geschlagen wurde. Und das wurde er in Deutschland weder von der KPD, noch von den westdeutschen „K-Gruppen“ der 1970er, sondern bis 1990 von einem sozialistischen, ostdeutschen Staat mit 40-jähriger Geschichte.


Objektiv betrachtet war diese eine Erfolgsgeschichte, nur leider wird sie selten objektiv betrachtet. Wer der DDR wegen Vorbehalten gegenüber Honecker, dem MfS, der Mauer o.ä. absprechen will, ein erfolgreicher, sozialistischer Staat gewesen zu sein, argumentiert nicht marxistisch, sondern eher wie ein arbeitsscheuer Linkspartei-Fan, der ernst gemeinte Argumente gerne mit „In meinem Sozialismus gibt es aber…“ einleitet. Fakt ist, dass die DDR praktisch bewiesen hat, dass das, was wir heute als recht abstrakte ökonomische Forderungen auf die Straßen bringen, innerhalb deutscher Verhältnisse funktioniert: Sozialistisches Eigentum, Betriebe in Arbeiterhand und eine staatlich gelenkte und überaus produktive Planwirtschaft – all das hat es bis 1990 in unserem eigenen Land gegeben.


Kommunisten in anderen Staaten würden ihre Niere für die praktischen wie ideologischen Möglichkeiten verkaufen, die es in sich birgt, den Sozialismus im eigenen Land nicht aufbauen zu müssen, sondern wiederaufbauen zu können. Deutsche Kommunisten schreiben trotzdem Texte über „Kontinuitätsprobleme“.


Doch warum tun sie das? Entgegen der weitläufigen Meinung vieler (westdeutscher) Genossen ist die kategorische Ablehnung der DDR unter denen, die sie tatsächlich erlebt haben, nämlich eine eher seltene Einstellung. Selbst hinter einem polemischen „

wollen wir nicht wieder

author: Luis Cosme Pinto
title: Melhor do mundo
content:
Faltam 28 minutos pro domingo virar segunda e o vagão só esvazia na estação Guilhermina-Esperança. O ambulante me cumprimenta com a cabeça, senta e acomoda a sacola preta entre as pernas. Estico o pescoço e vejo, lá dentro, algumas cocadas.


Parece que o dia foi bom, mesmo assim quero perguntar das vendas. Daria, com muito prazer, um pouco do meu tempo, do meu sono e até parte do que tenho na carteira para saber não só das cocadas. Quero conhecer, um tiquinho que seja, este trabalhador. Quem vende cocadas até o último trem do domingo tem muito pra contar.


Dou sorte. Mesmo tendo falado o dia inteiro de suas cocadas, que são gostosas, que desfazem na boca, que são baratas, que são mineiras e que vêm direto do Vale do Jequitinhonha, ele ainda quer falar.


Ajeita o boné, pigarreia.


— Meu nome é Getúlio. Getúlio Pereira da Silva. G. P. S. Nunca me perco. Entendeu? (rimos os dois) Mas sou conhecido como Raimundo. Eu explico: Pro ambulante, o marketing é tudo. Entro no vagão e anuncio: “Chegou a melhor cocada do mundo, a cocada do Raimundo”. Eu experimentei essa publicidade porque a rima é boa e eu sempre adorei o nome Raimundo. Tem passageiro que comenta. “Olha aí o Raimundo”. Então, deixa ficar. Virei Raimundo. Quer provar uma? É de graça que hoje esvaziei a sacola três vezes.


Aceito e me delicio com a doce mistura de coco e rapadura.


— Cremosa, né?


— Maravilhosa, Raimundo. Respondo com a boca ainda cheia e uma lasca de coco entre os dentes.


— Tem uns que reclamam da confusão. A gente grita mesmo. O jogador não pede a bola? O motoboy não buzina? O feirante não zoa? Por que a gente não pode? Ninguém é obrigado a saber da vida dos outros, mas será que eles sabem que, por trás de uma cocada, tem uma criança com fome, às vezes doente? Que tem aluguel, um monte de boletos, agiota te ameaçando?


— Quantos filhos você tem?


— Três. Olha aqui no celular. Anderson, Henrique e a caçula, a Marcela.


— Eu não peço nada, eu ofereço. Quem quer, quer. Quem não quer, não quer.


— Muita gente compra?


— Compra. E sabe por quê?


— Por quê?


— Porque o produto é bom e barato. E tem mais (ele sussurra): pobre não tem medo de gastar. Ele me vê e pensa: amanhã eu posso tá desempregado, posso ter que trabalhar como camelô. Então, eu ajudo agora e, se depois eu tiver no sufoco, alguém vai dar uma força.


— Mas dizem que é barato porque é clandestino.


— Mentira. É barato porque não tem intermediário; no supermercado o preço é maior porque eles têm muito mais despesas e também querem mais lucro. Aqui é diferente, vou no depósito e pago à vista.


— Então, por que é proibido?


— Porque é fácil mexer com o pobre. Eu garanto pro senhor. Meu produto não deve nada ao do supermercado. Eu ando de metrô e de trem todo dia e pago a passagem, viu? Eu sou camelô e passageiro ao mesmo tempo e garanto: a gente não atrapalha ninguém. Sabe o que atrapalha?


— O quê?


— O

atraso e a superlotação

. Tem que botar mais trens para circular. Só que a empresa ou o governo não quer gastar. É simples: com o trem cheio ganham mais. Agora, com a privatização, o que já era ruim ficou pior. Os vigilantes vêm pra cima como se o camelô fosse um bandido. Eu não sou bandido, sou empreendedor.


— Você manda bem, Raimundo. Já tinha falado de marketing, publicidade, agora empreendedor.


— Estudei um pouco. Empreendedor, eu ouvi essa no tempo que tinha passeata, sindicato. Durante um protesto, um cara subiu no caminhão e disse bem assim: Camelô é empreendedor e empreendedor é quem faz o Brasil crescer, nunca esqueci.


— Já tomaram sua mercadoria?


— Já, mas não desanimo. Toda profissão tem risco e eu adoro esse meu trabalho. Só que as autoridades não dão valor. Eles podiam cadastrar a gente.


— Como seria?


— Um número certo de ambulantes em cada trem, todo mundo com crachá, uniforme. Trabalho organizado.


Última estação. Getúlio levanta e me olha.


— Ué, não vai descer?


— Vou voltar. Vim até aqui para te ouvir.


A porta fecha e a gente acena um pro outro.


A voz feminina se impõe.


— Diamante Negro na promoção: é 3 por 5, que eu não brinco.

author: Wanessa Celina
title: A “bancada” anti-indígena que vai às urnas neste domingo
content:
Nas duas últimas legislaturas no Congresso Brasileiro, 370 deputados e senadores foram responsáveis por propostas de lei que enfraquecem os direitos indígenas — e 270 deles disputam reeleição neste ano. Ao todo, esses políticos atuaram em 252 projetos, a maioria incidindo negativamente sobre o direito à terra para esses povos.


As informações são baseadas em um levantamento da

Agência Pública

 a partir da nova plataforma lançada pelo Conselho Indigenista Missionário (Cimi), o

Congresso Anti-Indígena

.


Entre os projetos de lei que afetam os indígenas, estão propostas que buscavam anular decretos de demarcação de territórios e outros que alteram a Constituição Federal, para que as decisões sobre a demarcação sejam feitas pelo Congresso Nacional — justamente onde estão os políticos que atuam contra a demarcação de mais terras.


Para Cleber Buzatto, missionário do Cimi Regional Sul, essa atuação mostra que o principal interesse é impedir as demarcações e também explorar as terras.


“Isso demonstra uma articulação dos setores anti-indígenas, seja do ponto de vista político, mas, também, dos grupos econômicos que têm interesses sobre as terras, portanto, se organizam e atuam de forma bastante enfática e violenta contra os direitos indígenas no Congresso Nacional por meio de um conjunto amplo de partidos e parlamentares”, explica Buzzatto.


Entre 513 deputados e deputadas federais eleitos em 2022, apenas cinco se autodeclaram indígenas, menos de 1% do total. Como a

Pública


mostrou

, neste ano, o movimento indígena lançou 47 pré-candidaturas para tentar mudar esse quadro

.

 “É importante que os próprios povos [indígenas] consigam acessar espaços nessas casas legislativas, especialmente no âmbito da Câmara dos Deputados, que é onde tem mais candidatos indígenas disputando as vagas, até para que essa diretriz seja coerente com a defesa de fato dos direitos e dos interesses dos projetos de vida e futuro dos povos indígenas”, afirma.


Atualmente, segundo dados do Cimi, 291 propostas legislativas que impactam os direitos indígenas tramitam no Congresso Nacional. Entre elas, 204 têm efeitos negativos, segundo o levantamento.


PL, de Bolsonaro, é o principal partido a votar em propostas anti-indígenas, aponta levantamento


A partir da análise de mais de 41 mil votos, a plataforma identificou, dentre os partidos políticos, 19 que votaram sempre ou quase sempre em projetos que vão contra os povos indígenas. Apenas oito partidos votaram favoravelmente.


O Partido Liberal (PL), do candidato à presidência Flávio Bolsonaro, fica em primeiro lugar tanto entre os partidos cujos políticos mais propuseram propostas anti-indígenas, quanto entre os parlamentares que mais votam em projetos contrários aos direitos desses povos. São 95 proposições e 6.630 votos desfavoráveis segundo a classificação do Cimi. Em seguida, está o MDB, com 47 proposições, e o Partido Progressista (PP), com 42. Já entre os partidos cujos políticos tiveram mais votos em projetos contrários aos direitos indígenas, após o PL, está o PP, com 3.232 votos, e, em terceiro lugar, o União, com 3.063.


Por outro lado, o Partido dos Trabalhadores (PT), do presidente e candidato Lula, é o que mais teve propostas e votos em projetos classificados como favoráveis aos indígenas, com 4.971 a favor e 71 proposições. Em seguida, está o PSB, com 1.127 votos a favor, e o PDT, com 1.114 votos. O PCdoB, mesmo com apenas 11 deputados na Câmara, tem 100% dos votos direcionados a pautas consideradas favoráveis aos indígenas. Após o PT, entre os partidos que mais propuseram propostas favoráveis, estão o Psol, com 31 propostas.


Políticos que fizeram mais propostas com efeitos negativos aos direitos indígenas, segundo o levantamento


Deputado federal Marcos Pollon (PL-MS)


Candidato à reeleição para deputado federal pelo Mato Grosso do Sul, o deputado tem um total de 26 propostas classificadas como contrárias aos direitos indígenas, sendo 24 delas sobre o direito territorial dos povos tradicionais. O deputado é o terceiro-secretário da Frente Parlamentar

Invasão Zero

, grupo criado em 2023 que defende o direito à propriedade contra o Marco Temporal.


Entre as principais propostas do deputado está o PL 2145/2023, que altera o “Estatuto do Índio” para impedir o reconhecimento de determinadas áreas como de ocupação tradicional.
