.


ᖃᕋᓴᐅᔭᒃᑯᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒃᓴᓂ ᐱᔪᒪᕝᕕᒃ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᑲᑎᕐᓱᐃᓇᓱᖕᒪᑕ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᕕᖕᒥ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᐅᔾᔪᑎᒃᓴᖏᓐᓂ ᔮᓐ ᐊᒪᕈᐊᓕᒃ, ᐊᒥᓱᓄᑦ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᑕᐃᔭᐅᕙᒃᑐᖅ “ᐊᑖᑕᒋᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ.”


ᐊᒪᕈᐊᓕᒃ, 78, ᑲᒪᒋᔭᐅᑲᑕᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐊᒻᐸᓯ ᕕᐊᑦᒥ ᐊᑯᓂᕈᓗ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᕐᕕᒃᒥ ᐋᑐᕚᒥ ᐱᓚᒃᑕᐅᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᓂᐅᖓᑕ ᐱᖃᑖᑕ ᐃᓚᖓᒍᑦ. ᑕᐃᑲᓂᓕ ᑭᐱᙳᖃᑦᑕᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᐅᑎᕈᒪᓕᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᓄᓇᕗᒧᑦ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᒐᓴᖕᓂ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᓐᓇᓱᒃᓯᒪᔭᖓᓂ ᓄᓇᑖᕋᓱᖕᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐋᔩᖃᑎᖃᑲᑕᖅᖢᓂ.


ᔫᓂᒥ ᐅᑎᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑕᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᑎᒍ ᐱᖃᓐᓇᕆᔭᖏᓐᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓚᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᑖᕋᓱᖕᓯᒪᓂᖏᓐᓄᑦ. ᑭᓯᐊᓂᓕ ᑖᓐᓇ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖅ ᓄᖑᓕᕐᒪᑦ ᐅᑯᐊ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᕐᓇᙱᑦᑐᓕᕆᔨᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᑲᔫᕈᒪᙱᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᒫᓂ $16,000-ᑖᓚᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒃᓴᐅᖁᔭᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᑕᖅᑭᕐᒧᑦ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᐅᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᕐᓇᙱᑦᑐᓕᕆᔨᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᒡᓗᖓᓄᑦ ᐱᔭᕆᐊᖃᖅᑕᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᓅᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᑐᕈᒪᔭᖓᓄ ᐊᖏᕐᕋᖓᓂ.


ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᓄᓇᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᔭᓯᑲ ᕼᐃᐊᓪ, ᐃᒻᒥᓂ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐅᕘᓇ GoFundMe ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓂ ᐱᔪᒪᔾᔪᑎᒃᑯ ᖃᓪᓗᓈᖑᒐᓗᐊᖅᖢᓂ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᖃᒻᒪᕆᖕᓂᕋᖅᖢᓂ ᐃᓅᓯᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᑐᕆᐊᖃᖅᑐᓂᒃ, ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒃᓴᓂ ᐱᔪᒪᓂᕐᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓯᓯᒪᓪᓗᓂ ᑎᑭᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᖕᓂᖓᓂ ᒪᐅᖓ $50,000-ᓂ. ᑎᑭᑉᐸᓪᓕ ᑖᓐᓇ ᐃᑲᔫᑎ ᑕᖅᑭᓂ ᐱᖓᓱᓪᓗᐊᓂ ᐊᑐᖅᑕᐅᔪᓐᓇᕋᔭᖅᑐᖅ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᐅᓂᖓᓄᑦ.


“ᔮᓐ ᐊᒪᕈᐊᓕᒃ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᑦ 25 ᐅᖓᑖ ᐃᓅᓯᖓᓂ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ,” ᕼᐃᐊᓪ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᓯᒪᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐅᕘᓇ GoFundMe ᒪᒃᐱᒐᖓᒍᑦ.


ᐅᓇ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒃᓴᓂ ᐱᔪᒪᔾᔪᑎ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᑐᓂᔭᐅᓯᒪᓕᕐᑐᖅ $5,400 ᓇᒡᒐᔾᔭᐅᓚᐅᕐᑑᑉ ᐅᓪᓛᖓᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑕᐅᓯᒪᓕᖅᖢᓂ ᓯᑎᐱᕆ 18-ᖑᑎᓪᓗᒍ.


ᐊᒪᕈᐊᓕᒃ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᕐᓇᙱᑦᑐᓕᕆᔨᓂ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑯᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᔭᐅᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᓕᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ, ᒪᓕᒐᕐᓂ ᕿᒥᕐᕈᐊᖁᔨᓯᒪᓂᕐᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᒻᒪᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᕐᓇᙱᑦᑐᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᑦ ᐃᑲᔪᕈᒪᙱᓐᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᐅᓂᖓᓄᑦ.


ᓯᑏᕝ ᑲᓕᕼᐅ, ᐊᒪᕈᐊᓕᐅᑉ ᐅᖃᕐᑎᒋᔭᖓ ᐱᖃᓐᓇᕆᓪᓗᓂᐅᒡᓗ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓗᐊᐃᔭᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᕼᐃᐊᓪ ᐱᖃᓐᓇᕆᔭᐅᓂᖓᓂ ᐋᓐ ᑯᕌᕗᑦᒧᑦ, ᐃᑲᔪᖃᑕᐅᖕᒥᔪᖅ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᐱᕈᖅᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᒃᑐᓂ ᐊᒪᕈᐊᓕᒃᒧᑦ.


“ᐅᖄᓚᕝᕕᐅᑲᑕᒃᑲᒪ ᑭᒃᑯᓕᒫᓂ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐃᑲᔪᕈᒪᔪᓂᒃ,” ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᒫᒃ ᓯᑕᐃᐅᔅ, ᐱᖃᓐᓇᕆᔭᐅᖕᒥᔪᖅ ᔮᓐ ᐊᒪᕈᐊᓕᒃᒧᑦ. ᐅᖃᖅᖢᓂ ᖁᔭᓕᔪᕉ ᐃᓄᖕᓄᑦ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓂ ᑐᓂᓯᑲᑕᒃᑐᓄᑦ ᐅᕗᖓ GoFundMe.


“ᐅᓇ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓂᐊᕐᑐᖅ ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᓄᓇᕗᒥ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᑦ ᑕᒪᑐᒥᖓ ᐃᓱᒪᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᕐᓴᐅᓕᕐᐸᑕ.”


ᐊᒪᕈᐊᓕᒃ ᓗᐊᐃᔭᕆᔭᖓ ᑕᒪᑐᒥᖓ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᔭᐅᓵᓕᖁᔨᔪᖅ ᐊᓯᐊᒍᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᖓᔪᓂᒃ ᑖᓐᓇ ᐊᒪᕈᐊᓕ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑕᐅᓵᓕᓂᕐᓴᐅᔪᓐᓇᕐᓂᐊᕐᒪᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖅᑐᓕᕆᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᒡᓗᖃᖅᑎᑕᐅᓂᖓᒍᑦ.

author: Claire Cleary
title: Kalshi Is Lobbying States to Fight Off Regulations for Prediction Markets
content:
Prediction market companies say they offer regulated financial swaps. Many states argue they are gambling operations.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

As prediction markets have exploded in popularity over the past two years, they have also become increasingly controversial – setting off a lobbying-fueled power struggle for regulation of the platforms.

Amid allegations of insider trading, bets on military operations, and deceptive marketing practices, some states are seeking to sue or ban prediction markets. But the federal government has taken an unusual role in the legal battle, with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission suing states that seek to enforce their gambling laws against prediction-market platforms.

Prediction market companies contend they are offering financial transactions known as swaps – which are regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, a federal agency – while many states argue they are gambling operations, akin to sportsbooks and casinos. Gambling is regulated by the states.

Several lawsuits addressing whether state law applies to prediction markets have advanced to federal courts, but because judges have split on their rulings, the question is still unsettled and moving towards the Supreme Court.

Although market leader Kalshi argues it should be regulated at the federal level, the company’s lobbying and spending demonstrates a push to gain state-level influence – especially in the states spearheading regulation.

So far in 2026, Kalshi, its competitor Polymarket and the Coalition for Prediction Markets have spent at least $3 million on lobbying and campaign contributions across the federal and state levels.

State attorneys general are leading the regulatory fight against prediction markets – and the majority are united in the opinion that CFTC regulation should not preempt state gambling laws. In July, a coalition of 44 state AGs signed onto a letter to the CFTC arguing that prediction markets are a “new form of casino.”

But just as attorneys general and prediction markets appear to be battling each other, Kalshi is pouring hundreds of thousands of dollars into the two major political organizations dedicated to electing and supporting AGs.

According to IRS filings reviewed by OpenSecrets, in the first half of 2026, Kalshi gave $147,500 to the Republican Attorneys General Association and $170,000 to the Democratic Attorneys General Association.

Kalshi has also donated directly to some attorneys general – including the super PAC supporting Ken Paxton’s run for Senate in Texas and the campaigns of Vermont’s Charity Clark, Oregon’s Dan Rayfield and Florida’s James Utheimer. In response to the contributions, Rayfield and Clark told local news outlets they are not influenced by political donations. A spokesperson for Paxton’s super PAC told Politico that Paxton “has fought at every turn to hold big corporations accountable.”

The New York Times reported in August that Donald Trump Jr., who serves as a strategic advisor to Kalshi and Polymarket, told Republican state AGs not to fight prediction markets. Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm is invested in Polymarket and he has an equity stake in Kalshi.

The head of Kalshi’s state relations, Blake Bee, was previously director of the National Association of Attorneys General’s Center for Leadership Development, where he worked directly with state attorneys general.

Kalshi also donated $100,000 to the Republican Governors Association and $150,000 to the Democratic Governors Association in the first half of 2026.

“Like many U.S. regulated companies, we support candidates on both sides of the aisle,” Dani Lever, a spokesperson for Kalshi, wrote in a statement to OpenSecrets.

Kalshi has ramped up state-level lobbying in the past several months. As of September, the company has at least one registered lobbyist in 41 states, nearly all of them brought on board since April.

Kalshi appears to be spending the most on lobbying in California and New York, though many states do not require financial disclosure by lobbyists.

In California, Kalshi spent $62,000 on lobbying in the first half of 2026. Disclosure reports reviewed by OpenSecrets show that Kalshi is lobbying on three assembly bills and the “Attorney General’s and Governor’s offices re: prediction markets.”

author: Jake Johnson
title: Trump Meme Coin Contest Over Dinner With the President Raises Ethics Concerns
content:
The top 185 buyers of Trump’s meme coin, which has lost investors billions, are promised dinner with the president.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The company behind US President Donald Trump’s meme coin has launched a competition giving participants an opportunity to attend “the most exclusive dinner in the world” — all they have to do is buy a digital token with no inherent value that has lost investors billions of dollars while further enriching the president.

The Washington Sun reported Thursday that winners of the competition, held by CIC Digital and Fight Fight Fight LLC, “will be chosen based on a formula that seems designed in part to increase sales of $TRUMP in the next two months.” The event invite promises the top 185 holders of the meme coin an evening with three unidentified “legends” and Trump, “plus a private meet and greet with a legend yet to be announced,” at the president’s golf club in Virginia.

The November 22 dinner will mark the second exclusive event for holders of Trump’s meme coin, which has netted the president at least $635 million, according to recent financial disclosures.

Investors in the digital token haven’t fared nearly as well: The cryptocurrency analytics firm Nansen has estimated that nearly a million people who purchased the meme coin through the end of June 2026 had combined losses of around $4 billion.

Last May, the top buyers of Trump’s meme coin — including Chinese billionaire Justin Sun, who has poured tens of millions of dollars into the president’s crypto ventures — attended an exclusive dinner at Trump’s Virginia golf club and received a VIP tour of the White House. Ethics experts and other critics described the event as “corruption embodied.”

News of the second dinner sparked similar outcry. “This is the most brazenly corrupt shit I have ever seen in politics and it’s not even close,” wrote Tommy Vietor, a podcast host and former spokesperson for Barack Obama.

Rep. Greg Landsman (D-Ohio) characterized the event as “the most exclusive dinner in the world with the most corrupt president in American history.”

author: Marina Amaral
title: A imprensa sem alma, os políticos oportunistas e a fé dos brasileiros
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a Newsletter da Pública, enviada sempre às sextas-feiras, 8h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Nove entre dez colunistas de política da grande imprensa lamentam que a gente esteja discutindo Nossa Senhora da Aparecida no final da campanha eleitoral. Enquanto isso, nunca o noticiário foi tão contaminado pela negação do subjetivo – a religiosidade do brasileiro -, e nunca soou tão parcial – por mais que se reafirme a “isenção” da imprensa. Além de críticas de diversos

veículos

 a respeito da cobertura do episódio, a própria Globo, uma das protagonistas do caso, se tornou

alvo

 de protestos de eleitores.


Sim, esse é um assunto relevante para a população e deve fazer parte do debate público em um momento em que a religião é explorada politicamente e invade até as decisões do TSE, como vimos acontecer mais uma vez.


E a imprensa errou de cabo a rabo

 – do desmentido da Globo sobre uma afirmação correta de uma jornalista responsável, ao bombardeio de títulos e notícias sobre a “fake news”,

criada

 e propagada pela própria imprensa a partir da “correção” e depois manipulada nas redes sociais.


Em vez de defender a jornalista, que jamais disse que Flávio pretendia destronar a santa, mas apenas comentou um fato que já viralizava nas redes – a existência de “um movimento da Igreja Católica de reação a uma parcela de evangélicos que está mobilizando um projeto de lei para tirar de Nossa Senhora da condição de padroeira” – que, segundo ela, poderia ter impacto entre “os eleitores católicos de Lula”, a imprensa embarcou no desmentido da Globo (com aquele comportamento de boiada que já comentei na

co

lu

na

 anterior). Até mesmo entidades como a

Abraji

 e a

Fenaj

 demoraram a manifestar solidariedade e não citaram o nome da empresa que cometeu o erro que gerou agressões à jornalista.


A imprensa também não questionou o fato gravíssimo que foi a censura de opinião do humorista Antônio Tabet, que apenas exerceu o direito à liberdade de expressão como reconheceu o próprio TSE na quarta-feira, após o ministro André Mendonça

mudar

 o seu voto. A reação foi a de “proteger” Flávio de prejuízos eleitorais pela alegada falsa informação – logo ele, que usa a desinformação como ferramenta de campanha e conta com aliados que agridem pessoas nas redes – como

fez

 o blogueiro foragido Allan dos Santos em reação violenta e repugnante ao protesto da CNBB. Nem quando o direito de expressão dos brasileiros foi massivamente cerceado pelas Big Techs depois da determinação de censura de Mendonça – um tema eminentemente jornalístico – reviu sua posição.


De lá para cá cometeu também o erro da arrogância elitista (ou seria constrangimento por seu papel?) ao desvalorizar o tema de um debate público que acontece e precisa acontecer no Brasil sob a desculpa cínica de que eleitores e candidatos deveriam estar discutindo propostas que podem mudar o Brasil (como se a imprensa estivesse fazendo isso, em vez de se embrenhar em vazamentos seletivos de escândalos de corrupção).


A separação de Igreja e Estado é condição necessária para a democracia, estabelecida no Brasil na Constituição de 1891 e reforçada no

artigo 19

 da Constituição de 1988, que inspirou a legislação eleitoral que proíbe a propaganda política em igrejas e a doação de recursos para campanhas, assim como a destinação de recursos públicos para igrejas – embora isso aconteça, como sugere a ligação da Igreja da Lagoinha com o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e seu cunhado Fabiano Zettel, maior doador das campanhas de Jair Bolsonaro e Tarcísio de Freitas nas eleições de 2022.


Mas a mesma Constituição cidadã, pilar da redemocratização brasileira, foi

promulgada

 pela Assembleia Constituinte “sob a proteção de Deus”, o que não retira a laicidade do Estado, já que o impede de privilegiar uma religião determinada. Talvez seja apenas uma reafirmação da fé que ressoa na nossa alma brasileira, também formada por histórias milagrosas como a dos pescadores que no século 18 encontraram uma pequena imagem de uma santa negra, que fez jorrar peixes em suas redes, e depois se tornou a padroeira do Brasil.


Não se brinca com a fé, como sabe Fernando Henrique Cardoso que perdeu a primeira eleição para prefeito de São Paulo depois da ditadura, em 1985, para qual era francamente favorito, depois de se embananar para responder se acreditava em Deus, pergunta feita pelo jornalista Bóris Casoy …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Quieren echar del INTA a la científica que investigó el impacto de agroquímicos en personas
content:
La investigadora Virginia Aparicio, del INTA-Balcarce, enfrenta un sumario y podría ser exonerada tras participar de un estudio que detectó agrotóxicos en el cuerpo de 73 argentinos, entre 2 y 10 plaguicidas en sangre y hasta 18 en materia fecal, además de glifosato en todas las muestras.


Aparicio es ingeniera agrónoma, doctora en Ciencias Agrarias, investigadora independiente del Conicet y desde hace dos décadas trabaja en la Estación Experimental Agropecuaria Balcarce del Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA), donde desarrolla investigaciones vinculadas con suelo, agua y plaguicidas. “Se nos prohibió difundir los resultados”, aseguró esta científica, una de las personas con mayor conocimiento en la investigación de agrotóxicos en el país, en referencia a las muestras obtenidas de los 73 voluntarios argentinos que participaron del proyecto internacional SPRINT (Transición Sostenible de Protección Vegetal), luego de encontrar mezcla de agrotóxicos en sangre, orina y materia fecal.


“Encontramos plaguicidas en matrices animales, vegetales y humanas. Durante el proyecto medimos más de 200 agrotóxicos diferentes en muestras de suelo y agua, pero también en sangre, materia fecal y orina. Tenemos una idea de la ruta de los plaguicidas, las combinaciones que cuidan al cultivo, pero estamos sometidos a una alta exposición y de lo cual se sabe muy poco porque es crónica”, explicó la científica.


El problema es que no solamente fue censurada sino que por participar del proyecto SPRINT enfrenta un sumario administrativo en su contra y la posibilidad de ser exonerada de la Administración Pública Nacional. El conflicto ya había comenzado a hacerse público en 2023, cuando el INTA suspendió la presentación de los resultados argentinos y posteriormente decidió retirarse del proyecto.


Su defensa denuncia presiones y persecución con el objetivo de silenciarla a ella y a la investigación. “El glifosato es lo que conocemos como Roundup, en su marca comercial, que es un herbicida que se utiliza inicialmente con el cultivo de la soja transgénica, entonces es resistente: vos podés matar malezas sin matar al cultivo. Hay una tesis doctoral que demuestra que ese herbicida pasa al tallo y al trigo, e ingresa a nuestro cuerpo por la alimentación”, agregó la investigadora.


Uno de los aspectos previstos por el proyecto Sprint era que los participantes pudieran acceder a sus propios resultados. El trabajo con personas había sido sometido previamente a una comisión de ética en Europa y luego a la evaluación correspondiente en cada país. Allí se establecía que quienes participaran podían solicitar información sobre sus resultados individuales. Cuando las muestras comenzaron a regresar de Europa, Aparicio consultó a los 73 participantes si querían conocer sus datos. Sólo una persona respondió que ya no estaba interesada. Para el resto, elaboró informes individuales con los valores obtenidos en sangre, orina y materia fecal.


En paralelo, comenzó a organizar una reunión virtual para presentar los resultados generales. Mientras realizaba un posdoctorado en España, con una beca del CONICET, coordinó el encuentro junto con el equipo de comunicación del INTA. La intención era que la reunión tuviera carácter institucional y permitiera explicar los resultados de manera responsable. La reunión estaba pactada para el 21 de junio de 2023. Pero cuando ya estaba organizada y las invitaciones habían sido enviadas, una decisión del Consejo Directivo del organismo dispuso que debía suspenderse. “Como ya había mandado la invitación a la reunión y los datos, muchos de los voluntarios se empezaron a organizar entre ellos. Yo les advertí a mis superiores. Igual me prohibieron esa reunión”, relató. El 27 de septiembre de ese año, en el marco de la cumbre científica de la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas (UNGA 78), fueron presentados en una conferencia virtual desde Nueva York parte de los resultados de Sprint.


El 7 de diciembre, tres días antes de la asunción de Javier Milei, el entonces presidente del INTA, ingeniero Mariano Garmendia, firmó la resolución 1081/2023 que dispuso el cierre de la participación argentina en el proyecto Sprint. La resolución fue adoptada por el consejo directivo del INTA, integrado por representantes del sector público y del sector privado: Sociedad Rural Argentina (SRA), Federación Agraria Argentina (FAA), Confederación Intercooperativa Agropecuaria (CONINAGRO) y Asociación Argentina de Consorcios …

author: Unknown
title: Tu hîn Kurdî nizanî?
content:
*Bu yazıya bilinçli olarak editoryal müdahalede bulunulmamıştır- Tiştek ji vê nivîsê nehatiye guhartin û bi zanebûn weke xwe hatiye hîştin.


Di sala 2014’an de bû. Demsal payiz bû. Min dest bi hînbûna Kurmancî kir. Wê demê, mamosteyê me li zaningehe ders dida. Wê demê disa em digotin “îhtîmale aştiyê heye”. Lê hat bira we? Piştre yani di salan 2015 û 2016’an de, havin u zivistan pir dijwar bûn. Vê gavê jî pêvajoya nû heye. Wek “ihtimale me heye, qey aşti ye?”. Lê em nizanin ku aşitiya ku her kes behs dike, heman aştiye? Neyse, niha mijara me ne ev e.


Li vir, mijara me zimanê Kurdî ye. Ez bi gelemperî kesekî dilbaz im. Lê wexta ez bi Kurdî diaxivim ez hineki stres dibim. Yanî ez fedi nakim lê hin peyvan carinan nayen bira min. Neyse. Eger ez di kurdi de dinivîsim, hest u zimanê min rehattir e. Wekî niha. Lê hevalen min dizanin ku Kurmanciya min “baş e, baş e” (Erê, ji bo hevalê min ê ku min nasnake: zimanê dayika min ne kurdî ye, le ez kurdê polîtîk im. Temam? Pirsgirêk heye? Me le hev kir?: Ger ez dibêjim ku ez siyasi Kurd im, ez wisa me!)


Niha, ji bo vê nivisê, hin hevokan ez bi tirkî difikirim, piştre ez wan ji 

werdigerîni

m kurdî. Hin hevokan ji ez direkt kurdî dinivîsim. Lê ev ne rast e, divê ez bi kurdî bifikirim û ez bi kurdi binivîsim.


Û strana, “Rojek tê”, strana yeke min bû ku min hevok bi hevok wergerand. Ev jî di heman salê de bû. Tu zanî, ya duyemin çi bû? Ev “Destana Egîdekî”(stranbêjê vê stranê Ciwan Haco ye) . Min vê stranê jî hevok bi hevok wergerand.


Di hînbûna ziman de aliyekî psîkolojîk jî heye. Yani, rewşa dilê te bandorê li te dike (wekî di her tiştî de). Carinan, rewş te bilez dike, car caran jî te hêdî dike. Wekî mînak, rewşa siyasi hebû (yani, bi rasti, zeman tune ku rewş siyasi nebe), Tu dikari bibejî, “ev berpirsiyarî min e ku divê ez Kurmancî hîn bibim” û tu dixwazî tu dikari zû bi zû hîn bibî. Piştre, yani ji bo te, her der xuya dike ku “Kulîlka Azadîyê”( Koma Amed) an “Siwar Hatin Ji Zozanan” (Mehmud Berazi). Te fehm kir, ez çi dibejim. Te fehm kir? Erê, erê, te fehm kir hevala min ê heja.


Carinan, mixabin, demekê hat û em dibejin: destê min ji te nabe. Li vir, tu dizanî, jiyan hinekî dijwartir bû.


Carinan mirovên ku ketin jiyana te, tu hîs dikî ku ew ji li “çîroka vê bayê” (stranbêjê vê stranê Agit Işık) guhdar dike. An jî tu ji vî kesî hêrs dibî û dibêjî: “Ya Star!” Ez jî ji bikaranîna “Ya Star” pir hez dikim. Nepirse çima. Li vir, hêrs jî hîsek girîng e ku tu dikari bijî.


An jî, dema dilê te li kesekî ye, di stranên ku tu guhdarî dikî de tu evina xwe her der dibînî û deng ji te wek “Nav şêrîna min” (stranbêjê vê stranê Kasım Taşdogan e); "Ez Dê Herim Nav Baxçê Gulan" (Lawje), an jî “Nergîsa serê çiya” (Mehmet Atlı) dibe.


Ez niha dibînim ku min qet stranbêjekê jin nenivîsand. Gelo ev rewş ji bo me çi dibêje? Ew hest, hest ne yê min e, yan ez belkî hestên kesekî din hîs dikim?  Em ê di nivîsa paşê de li ser vê mijarê biaxivin.


Guhdarîkirina stranan bi hevalên xwe re hêzê dide. Mînak, ez ketim jiyana kesekî. Wexta ew stran veke, em bi hev re carinan xemgîn bûn, carinan jî hêvîdar bûn. Lê em her dem bi hev re bûn — dil bi dil. Yanî, ez dibêjim ku mijara stranan pir girîng in. Muzîka kurdî jî pir taybet e. Muzîk di her zimane de alîkariya te dike ku tu bijî.


Di dawiyê de, ger tu bi rastî dixwazî Kurmancî hîn bibî, kes tune ku ji te tutmuş biki. Mijar tu yî, mijar ew e ku tu çiqas bawer dikî. Yani ez dixwazim bibêjim: Ger tu mirokevi “tutarlı” û “samimi” yi tu bawer diki ku ziman sedema hebûnê ye, tu Kurdî hin bibe. Sedemên hînbûna Kurmancî pir in.


Yanî, ez çi dibêjim? Ez dibêjim ku stran hene, kesên pir delal û xweş li derdora te hene, li vê dinyayê 45 milyon Kurd hene. Mamosteyên li Instagramê jî hene. AI jî heye. Yanî, eger tu dibêjî: “Ez politik im, ez bi entegrasyona demokratîk bawer dikim,” tu Kurmancî hîn bibe!


*Têbinî: Nivîskar bi eslê xwe ne Kurd e û bi hewldanên xwe fêrî kurdî bûye û her weha çîroka fêrbûna xwe ji bo me nivîsiye.

author: Randi Beers
title: The people we carry with us
content:
Annie Qimirpik


There are some people you expect to see forever. You see them around town, talk to them, tease each other, make plans without thinking too much about whether those plans will happen.


Because why wouldn’t they? When you live in a small community, people become part of the landscape of your life. You know where they live; that is their family. You recognize their voice before you see them.


And then suddenly they’re not there anymore.


I think one of the strangest things about grief is how ordinary the world continues to feel.


The sun is still rising. People still go to work. Kids still play outside. Planes come and go.


Life doesn’t stop just because someone you love is no longer living it with you.


That can feel unfair, confusing and sometimes angering.


In a small community, loss is rarely experienced alone. When some dies, their absence can be part of the community itself.


There’s an empty place where they used to sit.


A name that comes up in conversation, a story someone tells, a song that suddenly means something: g

rief has a strange way of making ordinary things significant.


Sometimes, we talk so much about how someone died that we forget how they lived.


We remember tragedy because it’s the moment that changed everything. But the person was so more than the way we lost them. They were someone’s friend, cousin, child. Someone who made people laugh. Someone who had favourite things, annoying habits, inside jokes, plans and ordinary days that mattered simply because they were theirs.


I think one of the hardest parts of grief: trying to remember a person as a human instead of reducing them to statistics or what their worst day of life was. 


That’s why we tell stories. We tell the funny ones; we repeat the things they used to say. We name our children after them to carry their legacy. We remember the little details that probably seemed meaningless at the time. We keep photos, visit familiar places to remember them. Sometimes a person can be present in a story without being identified. A memory doesn’t always need a name attached to matter.


There are people I carry with me who will never know how often I think about them.


There are moments I wish I could go back to, so I could pay more attention. I would listen longer, laugh harder. I would take ordinary moments more seriously because we never know which ordinary moment will become a memory. Grief doesn’t get smaller; we grow around it.


We learn how to carry it alongside everything else: our jobs, our families, friendships, celebrations, our ordinary Tuesday afternoons. 


And sometimes, something catches us completely off-guard. A place, colour, song, a joke. A date on a calendar.


And suddenly, for a moment, that person doesn’t feel like someone who’s gone. They feel close again. Maybe that’s what it means to remember someone.


Not to keep ourselves trapped in the past, it’s to allow the people we’ve loved to remain part of who we become. And we can carry them forward.


Perhaps that is one of the quiet responsibilities of being left behind: to remember they were here, that they mattered, that they were loved and that their life was more than the way it ended.


We carry around pieces of them for the rest of our lives.


Annie Qimirpik is a writer living in Iqaluit who maintains a self-titled blog about life in the North.

author: Unknown
title: Xebat Andok: If the state does not address the causes of the Kurdish question, it cannot resolve it
content:
According to Xebat Andok, the Peace and Democratic Society Process has not come to a standstill, but is progressing only very slowly. The KCK Executive Council member sees the continuing fundamental differences between the two sides over the aims and nature of the process as the decisive reason. While the Turkish state, under the formula of a “terror-free Turkey,” is primarily focused on disarmament and security, the Kurdish movement views the process as being about addressing the root causes of a conflict that has remained unresolved for more than a century. “If the state does not address the causes of a problem but focuses exclusively on its consequences, it cannot resolve that problem,” Andok said in an interview with Stêrk TV.


Andok is calling in particular for concrete working and communication opportunities for Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, whom he regards as the central negotiator and coordinator of the process. At the same time, he is critical of the Kurdish movement and broader social forces, saying that the opportunities created by the end of the armed struggle have so far not been sufficiently used to build a democratic society and mobilize broad sections of society for peace.


He argues that the process can neither be left to Öcalan alone nor reduced to steps taken by the state. What is needed, he says, is social pressure capable of compelling the state to undertake fundamental change.


We publish the first part of the in-depth interview below:


The Peace and Democratic Society Process continues, and different circles are engaging in discussions regarding it. So far, some steps have been taken, but to what extent are these steps sufficient? Overall, how do you assess the Peace and Democratic Society Process and the past two years it has spanned? What stage is the process currently at?


First of all, I would like to take the opportunity to commemorate the martyrs who gave their lives in the ‘You Cannot Darken Our Sun’ campaign and all the revolutionary martyrs, represented by comrade Bêrîtan, with gratitude, love, and respect. I reaffirm our pledge of victory to our martyrs.


The Peace and Democratic Society Process is entering its third year. And of course, there are different approaches to this process. This, in fact, is a source of richness. It affects society, it affects state-society relations, and it affects relations between states. Therefore, it is natural for different approaches to emerge. But quintessentially, one can say that this process has two sides. One side is the Republic of Turkey, and the other side is us – the Kurdish people – as a movement. If one looks at the process within this framework, perhaps one can provide a more accurate answer to your question.


First of all, the approaches of these two sides are not the same. Even the naming of the process differs – from the Turkish state’s perspective, it is “Turkey Without Terrorism,” while from our perspective, it is the “Peace and Democratic Society Process.” These terms and the different ways the process is defined alone reveal just how different the two sides’ approaches to the process are in every respect.


Both sides are parties to this process and are trying to carry it out. But even from the way they name it, one can see how different they are from one another. When the definitions differ, everyone’s actions will naturally align with their own definition. So, what have we seen over these past two years? The Turkish state is acting in accordance with its own definition. It refers to the process as “Turkey Without Terrorism” and seeks to address everything within the framework of the label ‘terrorism’ and within the framework of ‘security policies.’ Its approach to the Freedom Movement is primarily framed in terms of laying down arms and disarmament. Beyond this, it does not prioritize anything else on its agenda. Generally speaking, in its relations with the Kurds and other entities – as well as with Kurds living in other nation-states and those states themselves – it also frames these relationships within the context of “terrorism,” “the fight against terrorism,” and the disarmament of the Kurds. Its practices to date have largely followed this pattern.


One has to see the problem at hand. And this is the Kurdish issue. It is an issue that dates back at least a century. If the state does not address the causes of the problem but focuses solely on the consequences, it cannot resolve the issue. First, the diagnosis must …

author: Unknown
title: Iran has executed at least 28 women since start of 2026
content:
At least 28 women have been executed in Iran since the beginning of 2026. The Women’s Committee of the National Council of Resistance of Iran (WCNCRI) published a report on the execution of women in the country.


The report said the most recently recorded execution was that of Mahrokh Mirzaei on 26 September. It stated that Mirzaei had killed her husband in self-defence after being subjected to violence during their marriage: “Mahrokh Mirzaei experienced constant disputes and tensions with her husband throughout their four-year marriage. Over time, these circumstances affected her mental and psychological health, leading to serious problems. She was arrested four years ago on charges of killing her husband and was sentenced to death. With the execution of Mahrokh Mirzaei, the number of women executed in Iranian prisons since the beginning of 2026 has reached at least 28.”


The report also stated that at least 356 women had been executed by the regime since 2007. It said: “Most of the women executed by the Iranian regime were themselves victims of domestic violence and discriminatory family laws. A significant number had acted in self-defence. Since Masoud Pezeshkian took office, the clerical regime has executed 4,110 prisoners, including 116 women.”


More than 950 executions in Iran in the first nine months of 2026


Figures from human rights organisations indicate that more than 950 people have been executed in the country since the beginning of the year.


Data from the Abdorrahman Boroumand Center for Human Rights in Iran showed that 911 executions were carried out between January and July 2026. The addition of executions recorded in August brought the figure to at least 916. Washington-based rights organisations, meanwhile, reported that 901 people were executed during the first seven months of the year.


At least 59 executions in September


The September 2026 report by the Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) said at least 59 people were executed in September alone. A significant proportion of the executions were reportedly carried out in cases involving murder and drug-related charges, while some were linked to political charges.


The figures indicate that, once the executions recorded in September are added to the toll from the first seven months of the year, the number of executions carried out in Iran in 2026 exceeds 950.


Most executions are not publicly announced


Human rights organisations say Iranian authorities officially announce only a limited proportion of executions, while many others are documented and recorded by independent human rights organisations and local sources.


Rights groups have reported that death sentences are imposed not only for murder and drug-related offences but also for charges linked to political activity and national security. Data covering the first seven months of the year showed that at least 56 executions were linked to political or national security charges.


The overall figures vary because human rights organisations use different methodologies and cover different sets of cases when documenting executions in Iran. Available data nevertheless indicate that more than 950 people were executed in Iran during the first nine months of 2026.

author: Unknown
title: Protest in Hamburg against police raid on Kurdish Community Center in Hanover
content:
A protest was held in Hamburg against the police raid on the Democratic Kurdish Community Center (DKTM) in Hanover. Kurds and people from left-wing and antifascist groups gathered outside the autonomous center Rote Flora in the Sternschanze district and expressed solidarity with those affected by the raid.


The protest was directed against the police operation last weekend, during which a Kurdish commemoration event in Hanover was prevented and the community center was subsequently stormed by a large police contingent. Numerous people present were detained for hours.


At the rally, Fatma Doğan, co-chair of the Hamburg DKTM, criticized the police operation as “unlawful and unacceptable.” She said it was unacceptable for such a raid to take place at a time when the PKK has ended its armed struggle and a peaceful solution to the Kurdistan question is being discussed.


Doğan recalled the heavy sacrifices made over decades of the Kurdish freedom struggle. She said that attempts to criminalize the commemoration of the martyrs could not prevent Kurdish society from preserving their memory. “Until the last drop of our blood, we will follow the path of our martyrs,” she said.


At the same time, Doğan stated that police pressure and criminalization could not prevent the Kurdish population’s struggle for freedom and expressed solidarity with those affected in Hanover. During the rally, slogans including “Şehîd namirin” Martyrs are immortal) and “End the repression” were chanted.

author: Unknown
title: Long-term political prisoner denied permission to attend his father’s funeral
content:
Political prisoner Aydın Altığ, who has been imprisoned in Turkey for 30 years, has been denied permission to attend the funeral of his late father. The prison administration justified the refusal by stating that Altığ is subject to a “strict prison regime.”


Mahmut Altığ, the prisoner’s father, died on September 29. His son subsequently applied for permission to attend the funeral. Altığ is currently being held in a high-security prison in Kırşehir, central Anatolia.


Aydın Altığ was arrested at the age of 17 in the southern Turkish province of Mersin and, according to the Human Rights Association (İHD), was severely tortured. A State Security Court (DGM) in Adana subsequently sentenced the Kurdish man to life imprisonment on charges of “separatism.” During his many years in prison, he was repeatedly transferred and held successively in prisons in Erzurum, Amed (Diyarbakır), Çankırı, Çanakkale, Adana, and Kırşehir.


On February 3 of this year, Altığ completed 30 years of his prison sentence. However, his scheduled release was postponed for six months by the prison’s Administrative and Observation Board. The decision was justified on the grounds that he had shown no remorse for the offense of which he was convicted. When the prison board reviewed his release again on August 3, his imprisonment was extended for another six months. Altığ therefore remains in prison beyond his originally scheduled release date. He has now also been denied the opportunity to say farewell to his father.

author: Unknown
title: 10-week ‘Women, Justice and Memory Vigil’ against femicides to be launched in Amed
content:
The Amed (tr: Diyarbakır) Network for Combating Violence announced that it will launch a “Women, Justice and Memory Vigil” against femicides and suspicious deaths of women.


According to a press statement issued at the Rosa Women’s Association, the vigil will begin outside the Diyarbakır Courthouse at 12:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, and will continue at the same location every Tuesday for 10 weeks.


Speaking on behalf of the women, İrem İlhan, a member of the Amed Bar Association’s Women’s Rights Center, said that in some cases, women’s deaths are classified as “suicide,” “accident,” or “suspicious death” and are not effectively investigated.


İlhan stressed that femicides should not be treated as isolated incidents, and factors such as domestic violence, threats, stalking, access to firearms, failure to enforce protection orders, ineffective investigations, and impunity must be assessed together.


Call for effective and comprehensive investigations


The network is calling for comprehensive investigations, particularly in cases where the cause of death remains unclear, including thorough examination of crime scenes, forensic and digital evidence, as well as any history of violence experienced by the women.


İrem İlhan said they oppose investigations into suspicious deaths and disappearances of women in Kurdish cities being limited from the outset to explanations such as “suicide,” “fall,” “drowning,” or “disappearance.”


The network also called for the effective implementation of Law No. 6284 on the protection of women, the adoption of necessary protective measures in high-risk cases, independent investigations into negligence by public officials, and guarantees of investigative independence in cases where public officials are alleged perpetrators.


Women’s stories to be told each week


As part of the vigil, the lives of women who were killed and the unanswered questions surrounding their cases will be highlighted each week.


İrem İlhan said the vigil is not only aimed at ensuring that perpetrators are sentenced, but also at holding accountable the institutions responsible for protecting women and officials who fail to conduct effective investigations.


The Amed Network for Combating Violence called on women’s organizations, legal and human rights organizations, democratic institutions, and members of the public to join the vigil beginning on October 6.

author: Jim Loucks
title: What Washington Agreed to Last Month
content:
Berbera sits on the Gulf of Aden, about 150 miles south of Yemen. Its deep-water berth and the Emirati investment behind it are what Somaliland has been offering Washington. Illustration generated by the author, not a photograph of the port.


Somaliland’s president spent two weeks in Washington this month offering almost everything he has. Access to the port at Berbera. Access to the territory’s minerals. Military access, which he called a matter for negotiation and declined to rule out. He only asked for one thing in return. Recognition. He went home without it. The same month, the United States secured expanded security rights in Greenland and agreed in writing that sovereignty stays with Denmark.


What Somaliland Offered


Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, known as Irro, arrived on September 5 for his first visit to the United States since winning Somaliland’s presidency in November 2024. On the 14th, he gave the keynote address at the Hudson Institute, at an event titled

Somaliland as a Strategic Partner in the Horn of Africa

.


His pitch was the seaport. Irro described Berbera as a modern deep water facility that United States Africa Command had already assessed and in which the Emirati operator DP World has

invested $442 million

. More than twelve percent of global maritime trade passes through the Bab el-Mandeb strait every day. He argued that Somaliland has protected its coastline from militants and pirates for three decades without any recognition at all.


Two days later he went further. In an interview with Semafor he said Somaliland was not giving anything away for free. He offered American investors the port and the minerals. On military access he said it

was a matter for negotiation

, and he would not rule out a future base agreement. Ten days later he added more. In an interview with the Council on Foreign Relations he

suggested renaming Berbera International Airport after President Trump

, having earlier floated a Trump Tower in Hargeisa.


Berbera lies inside Somaliland, which declared the restoration of its independence in 1991 and which no African state recognises. Mogadishu, which holds the recognition, is about 600 miles to the south. Map by the author, using public-domain Natural Earth boundary data.


What They Got


Nothing, so far. Irro himself said there is

no American promise on recognition

. A source told Politico there is

no change

 in American policy towards Somaliland.


On September 16, China warned Irro that crossing its line on Taiwan would bring serious consequences, and

publicly affirmed that Somaliland remains part of Somalia

. That handed Mogadishu an endorsement from a permanent member of the Security Council in the middle of a rival’s tour.


The Hudson appearance also drew criticism at home. Clips circulated of Irro hesitating on questions about minerals and regional security. The event’s moderator, Joshua Meservey of the Hudson Institute, said afterwards that Irro had made the right argument, while also observing that

Somaliland has not consistently made the case

 for the reason recognition is necessary.


What Happened For Greenland


On the evening of September 18, President Trump announced an agreement with Denmark and Greenland giving the United States

permanent control over security

 in Greenland. He described it as an agreement with no end, at no cost. The three governments signed it in New York on September 22, and the White House released the text the same day.


Copenhagen and Nuuk described something narrower. Greenland’s prime minister, Jens-Frederik Nielsen,

said the agreement recognises the sovereignty and territorial integrity

 of the Kingdom and the right of Greenlanders to self-determination. A State Department official told CBS News it gives permanent access and overflight rights, allows more bases and

bars non-NATO members from building their own

.


None of this is new ground. American forces have been in Greenland since 1941, and

a 1951 defence agreement

 gave the United States the right to operate bases there, with Danish sovereignty expressly preserved. Reading the text signed this month,

ABC News reported

 that it does not appear to add materially to that access. What Washington secured was a broader scope and a bar on rival powers. The access itself it already had.

title: Эррико Малатеста - Ещё о «Науке и Анархии». Необходимость и свобода
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

: Ещё о «Науке и Анархии». Необходимость и свобода

Дата

: 1 февраля 1926

Источник

: Pensiero e Volontà год 3й, №2


Ещё о «Науке и Анархии».

Необходимость и свобода


 Замечания, которые я здесь и там писал в последнее время об отношениях между Наукой и Анархией, и особенно тот факт, что я назвал абсурдным определение, которое Кропоткин давал Анархии – «

Анархия есть миросозерцание, основанное на механическом понимании явлений, охватывающее всю природу, включая сюда и жизнь человеческих обществ

», – возмутили некоторых товарищей, которые, не понимая, конечно, по моей вине, того, что я имел в виду, заставили меня сказать, будто анархизм не знал, что делать с наукой и философией, и пустились доказывать великие заслуги науки и утверждать, что анархизм есть общая концепция жизни, то есть философия, так и не коснувшись вовсе того пункта, который я действительно поставил на обсуждение.


 Постараюсь объясниться яснее.


 Оставим философию, которой дают тысячу разных определений и которая часто поистине есть, как иронически говорит один философ, сам не блистающий чрезмерной ясностью, искусство делать туманным то, что ясно. Я профан и потому, эмпирически, для личного пользования, делю то, что говорят «философы», на две части: то, что я понимаю, и то, что я не понимаю. В той части, которую я понимаю, я нахожу истины, ошибки, сомнения, гипотезы, проблемы – всё вещи в высшей степени интересные, но которые в конечном счёте все входят в область научного исследования, если среди наук включать логику и психологию. В той части, которую я не понимаю, мне чудится видеть фантазии, тавтологии, споры о словах... но поскольку я не понимаю, будет разумнее воздержаться от суждений.


 Останемся на твёрдой почве науки.


 Цель научного исследования – изучать природу, открывать факт и «законы», которые им управляют, то есть условия, при которых факт

необходимо

 происходит и

необходимо

 воспроизводится. Наука составляется тогда, когда может предвидеть то, что произойдёт, – неважно, умеет ли она или нет сказать, почему: если прогноз не сбывается, это значит, что была ошибка и потому нет нужды делать более широкое и более глубокое исследование, чтобы спасти прогноз

[1]

. Случай, произвол, каприз – понятия, чуждые науке, которая ищет то, что фатально, то есть то, что не может быть иначе, то, что необходимо.


 Эта необходимость, связывающая между собой во времени и пространстве все естественные факты и составляющая задачу науки – искать и открывать, – охватывает ли она всё, что происходит во вселенной, включая психические и социальные факты?


 Механицисты говорят «да» и думают, что всё подчинено одному и тому же механическому закону, всё предопределено физико-химическими предшествующими причинами: и ход светил, и рост цветка, и трепет влюблённого, и развитие человеческой истории. И система, охотно соглашусь, представляется прекрасной и грандиозной, менее абсурдной, менее непостижимой, чем метафизические системы, и, если бы её можно было доказать как истинную, она полностью удовлетворяла бы ум. Но тогда, несмотря на все псевдологические усилия детерминистов примирить систему с жизнью и с моральным чувством, не остаётся места – ни малого, ни большого, ни условного, ни безусловного – для воли и для свободы. Наша жизнь и жизнь человеческих обществ была бы вся предопределена и предвидима,

ab eterno

 и навечно, во всех мельчайших подробностях, как и любой механический факт, и наша воля была бы простой иллюзией, как та иллюзия камня, о котором говорит Спиноза, – будто, падая, он сознавал своё падение и верил, что падает, потому что хочет падать.


 Допустив это, – а механицисты и детерминисты не могут не допустить этого, не противореча себе, – становится абсурдным желание контролировать свою жизнь, желание воспитывать себя и других, желание изменить в том или ином смысле общественную организацию. Вся эта суета людей, готовящих лучшее будущее, была бы бесполезным плодом иллюзии и не могла бы продолжаться после того, как обнаружилось, что это иллюзия. Правда, и иллюзия, и абсурд были бы фатальными продуктами механических функций мозга и как таковые входили бы в систему. Но, ещё раз, какое место остаётся для воли, для свободы, для действенности человеческого труда в жизни и в судьбах человека?


 Чтобы у людей была уверенность или по крайней мере надежда, что они могут делать полезное дело, нужно допустить творческую силу, первопричину или первопричины, независимые от физического мира и от механических …

title: Los jueces de la Corte fueron escrachados en San Martín de los Andes
content:
Organizaciones sindicales, vecinos y vecinas de San Martín de Los Andes, junto a espacios políticos se movilizaron a las puertas del hotel donde se desarrolla el 26° Congreso de Funcionarios de Tribunales Orales Federales. En el lugar se encontraban los jueces de la Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación Horacio Rosatti, Carlos Rosenkrantz y Ricardo Lorenzetti.


Escuchar el reporte de Laura Cotescu Fm Pocahullo de San Martín de los Andes


La Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación revocó el martes el fallo que había declarado la inconstitucionalidad del artículo 154 del DNU 70/23, el cual derogaba la Ley de Tierras Rurales. La sentencia fue firmada por los jueces.


La Asociación Trabajadores del Estado (ATE) convocó a la movilización para escrachar a los jueces en el centro de San Martín de Los Andes.


“Estos tres tipos son unos cobardes, no los tenemos que dejar caminar por la calle. No los votó nadie y sin embargo están entregando la soberanía sobre la tierra que es de todos los argentinos”, reclamó Rodolfo Aguiar, Secretario General de ATE.

En este momento el sindicato protesta en el Hotel Le Village donde se encuentran Rosatti, Rosenkrantz y Lorenzetti.

Estos tipos designados por decreto usurparon el Poder Judicial.

La presencia de los jueces también causó la indignación de los vecinos de la ciudad patagónica que se hicieron presentes en las puertas del céntrico hotel.


Con cantos, carteles por la soberanía argentina, y arrojando papel higiénico hacia el edificio, los manifestantes hicieron oír su mensaje.

author: David Swanson
title: World BEYOND War Asia Celebrated the International Day of Peace
content:
By Jhay de Jesus, World BEYOND War, October 2, 2026


2026 marks the 45th year since the United Nations established the International Day of Peace. It is ironic that while this year’s theme is “

Invest in Peace – For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day,

” we are witnessing continuous attacks in different nations, ongoing genocide against innocent people, especially children, and the occupation of lands and territories.


World BEYOND War

 continues to vow to work for the abolition of wars and the establishment of a just and sustainable peace system in the world.


This year, as we commemorate the day of peace,

World BEYOND War Asia

 partnered with several organizations and institutions to conduct two major events. With the help of movements and academic institutions like

Kilusan para sa Pambansang Demokrasya (KILUSAN)

,

PEACE Philippines

, and the

Philippine Normal University (PNU)

, we held symbolic actions depicting our advocacy for peace and our opposition to war and militarism.


Peace Umbrellas


Entitled “

PEACE Umbrellas: Shield against Continuous Rain of War and Militarism

,” World BEYOND War Asia, KILUSAN and its member organizations gathered at the Bantayog ng mga Bayani (Heroes’ Memorial) in Quezon City, Philippines, to hold white umbrellas bearing various calls such as “Free Palestine,” “Peace Not War,” “Reject Pax Silica,” and other anti-militarism and pro-peace demands. Five larger umbrellas spelled out “PEACE” to highlight the main call of the event.


The venue, Bantayog ng mga Bayani, is significant because its walls of remembrance bear the names of many anti-Martial Law activists who fought during the dark days of the regime of former dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr. The International Day of Peace also fell on the exact date when the former dictator declared Martial Law, a 14-year period that resulted in atrocities including abductions, incarcerations, killings, massacres, torture, and the displacement of communities.


Umbrellas also hold special significance as the country continues to face massive flooding due to a lack of government response to natural disasters like typhoons. For a year now, Filipinos have used umbrellas in protests to remind everyone of the effects of typhoons and monsoon rains flooding our communities, while government officials swim in millions of pesos diverted through corruption in flood-control projects. Now, as the country strengthens its ties with the U.S. and pawns the nation to continuous war games, the people hope to shield themselves from further atrocities this partnership will bring to the Philippines and its citizens.


Kite-Flying and Conversations of Peace


To conclude the International Day of Peace week, WBW Asia partnered with the Philippine Normal University (PNU) and PEACE Philippines to host an event dubbed “

PEACE UP! Sending our Messages of Peace High Up for the World to See

,” hosted at PNU in Manila City, Philippines


Attended by over 200 students, faculty members, and representatives from several student and thematic (off-campus) organizations, the event focused on the overarching call for global peace. Before the actual kite-flying activity, we held a conversation on peace featuring stories from various individuals and organizations.


We were fortunate to have with us Dr. Swee-Hin Toh, the 2000 UNESCO Peace Education Laureate, and Mahadia Abu Dalal, a Filipino-Palestinian educator and refugee based in a province in Southern Luzon. Dr. Toh shared how they have tirelessly worked in peace education even as the world continues to suffer from war and militarism, how the vision of peace inspires young people to join the advocacy, and the lessons learned from decades of peace education.


Mahadia shared how recent attacks in Palestine have affected their lives, creating refugees and tearing families apart. As an educator, she emphasized the importance of continuous conversations to share stories from the ground, ensure they are heard, and find ways to improve difficult situations.


We also heard a response from the PNU student body, represented by Christine (Luna) Zonio, a student in the Social Sciences program. She called on everyone to get involved in efforts to end U.S. imperialistic wars and militarism. Luna also stressed that partnerships and agreements like those the U.S. and the Philippines continue to enter into must be rejected, as they pose greater threats and place communities in serious danger.

author: Veridiana Alimonti
title: Ola Bini Ordered to Leave Ecuador Under Obscure Accusations
content:
In a new blow to

Ola Bini’s

 legal guarantees, Ecuadorean authorities retained the free software developer and security expert yesterday in Quito and ordered his immediate deportation from the country. He is barred from returning to Ecuador for 10 years.

 


According to

information released

 by his lawyer, Bini was intercepted by a car with four people who identified themselves as immigration agents. He was then taken to an immigration office without further information or a formal order from a competent authority. There, officials told Bini that his visa had been revoked but didn’t show any supporting document.

 


Bini's defense

filed

 a

habeas corpus

 to safeguard his freedom and prevent his deportation. Yet, Ecuadorian authorities affirmed that the developer represents a threat or risk to public security and the state structure, and must leave the country. The ground for deportation is

a secret report

 which allegedly asserts that Bini committed acts against the security of Ecuador. The defense could not access its contents.

 


The deportation hearing started yesterday at 5pm Quito time. Human rights organizations tried to attend the hearing but were

denied entry

. The hearing was suspended but later reinstalled establishing his immediate deportation. Ola Bini was relocated to Quito's airport and must stay there until fly back to Sweden.

 


The case that led to Bini's

unfounded criminal conviction

 has expired (the statute of limitations ran out) and the court had already formally lifted all precautionary measures against him

. Yesterday's e

vents open a new chapter in the nefarious persecution of Ola Bini by Ecuadorean authorities.

 


Since Bini’s arbitrary arrest in 2019, EFF

has reported

 about his criminal prosecution fraught with misconceptions and rights violations. The script of what happened yesterday follows the same patterns we saw in the entire case, from its outset with unjustified allegations that Bini was a national security risk. The Observation Mission of Ola Bini’s case, joined by EFF and other digital and human rights organizations, has published

reports

 and

raised international awarenness

 about the perils of this case to the protection of rights online and the beneficial work of security experts.

 


In a case surrounded by 

political interests

, Ola Bini’s 

unanimous acquittal

 by the lower court in 2023 was overturned after the prosecution’s appeal. The majority of the appeals court convicted Bini

 

for


attempted unauthorized access of a telecommunications system without 

actual evidence

 to corroborate the accusation claims. 

 


Now, once again we must sound the alarm.


Ecuadorean authorities must explain

 the accusations against the sec

urity expert

. We will remain vigilant

and

 

ensure that at least this time his

rights are respected.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Quebec Conservative Marc Damant says Nunavik needs a local MNA
content:
Nunatsiaq News reached out to each candidate running in the Ungava riding ahead of Quebec’s Oct. 5 provincial election. Here’s what Quebec Conservative party candidate Marc Damant had to share with us.


Marc Damant says he wants to represent Ungava because Nunavik needs a local representative in the Quebec national assembly.


“I think it’s time that Nunavik had someone who was more of a full-time MNA,” said Damant, who lives in Kuujjuaq and is the Quebec Conservative party’s candidate in the Oct. 5 provincial election.


He said that previous MNAs didn’t enough of an interest in the region, and that people feel like they don’t matter.


While he acknowledged logistical and financial challenges make it difficult for candidates to visit Nunavik’s villages, he said nothing beats face-to-face conversation with electors.


“We have to do better for everyone,” said Damant, adding he’s the only candidate with posters up in Kuujjuaq right now.


Damant works as an airport manager for the Kativik Regional Government, where he’s responsible for airport operations and safety for multiple communities across Nunavik. From 2007 to 2014, he was a grounds operations co-ordinator for Air Inuit, a role that allowed him to travel across Nunavik.


He also spent 11 years as a reservist in the Canadian Armed Forces and previously taught in China, Akulivik and La Tabatiere, Que. From 2010 to 2011, he was the president of the federal Conservative chapter in his riding of Lac-Saint-Louis, which represents Montreal’s West-Island, where Damant is from.


He said the Conservative party is a solid choice for federalists who want to pay less in taxes and to reduce government expenditures.


The party is promising to abolish taxes on carbon and used goods and to raise the amount citizens can earn without paying taxes from $19,000 to $35,242 by 2030. It’s also promising to reduce government spending by $47 billion over five years, by cutting public sector jobs, for example.


The party also wants to prioritize Quebec’s natural resources, he said, adding consultation is an important step in that development.


“We’re big on bringing our natural resources to market,” he said.


Damant is among five candidates running for Ungava in Quebec’s provincial election. Advance polls have been open since Saturday and will stay open until Wednesday. Election day is on Monday, Oct. 5.

author: Unknown
title: Cimici al carcere delle Vallette
content:
In questi giorni, a seguito di alcuni articoli di

giornale

 e in particolare dai racconti di alcuni detenuti recentemente usciti dal carcere torinese Lo Russo e Cutugno, sono emerse nuovamente le criticità sanitarie e di vivibilità minima della Casa Circondariale. 


In particolare è stata riportata sia dai giornali che da racconti diretti, la presenza di una infestazione di cimici da letto. Con gravi conseguenze sulla vita dei detenuti della sezione maschile. 


Le cimici da letto sono un parassita ematofago, che si nutre di sangue umano, che morde l’uomo causando lesioni cutanee della pelle solitamente in forma di gonfiore e arrossamento e prurito. In alcuni casi si possono avere anche reazioni di livello allergico più grave. Anche se non sono segnalate malattie trasmissibili tramite questo fastidioso parassita, le punture sono molto fastidiose e danno forte prurito. In più, ogni cimice morde solitamente più volte e se il materasso o la cella ne sono infestati, possono rendere la vita invivibile. Sono esseri notturni quindi concentrano l’attività nella notte, con i risvolti immaginabili per la vita dei detenuti. 


E’ un fenomeno infestante che molti conoscono magari per presa diretta o per racconti e può essere preso sottogamba, ma immaginiamo come si aggrava la situazione quando si presenta in un ambiente di scarso igiene come il carcere e dove, come in questo caso, gli interventi di disinfestazione sembrano essere nulli. 


In particolare sarebbero coinvolti sicuramente il Blocco B e la decima sezione in particolare. Ma, stando alle ricostruzioni, sembra molto probabile un’infestazione del magazzino dei materassi del carcere, oltre che delle celle. 


Il carcere non è nuovo a problemi di questo tipo: topi, scarafaggi, formiche, zanzare sono segnalati da anni, anche dai secondini. Numerose segnalazioni hanno evidenziato carenze dovute al sovraffollamento ma soprattutto alla fatiscenza della struttura. A questo si sommano la scarsità di mobilio e il fatto che in alcune sezioni non vengano distribuite abbastanza lenzuola e che i cuscini non siano un’opzione per molti detenuti.


Il fatto che una possibile infestazione da cimici da letto si possa allargare all’intero carcere, ha qualcosa di molto allarmante e non è solo una questione sanitaria, anche se le implicazioni possono essere gravi visto che anche i medicinali normalmente reperibili fuori tante volte scarseggiano. Ne va della vivibilità e sanità mentale dei detenuti. Possiamo immaginare cosa voglia dire rimanere svegli per notti e notti di fila e avere coscienza che la cella in cui si è rinchiusi è popolata da insetti che si cibano del tuo sangue? Uno stress e una tortura a cui nessuno dovrebbe essere sottoposto. 


Dopo le denunce pervenute ai giornali tramite le ispezioni della Consigliera Regionale Ravinale, difficilmente le istituzioni possono dire di non essere a conoscenza del problema e il fatto di non agire tempestivamente non può che aggravare la situazione. La salubrità è talmente deteriorata all’interno del carcere, che addirittura i sindacati della penitenziaria, fanno dichiarazioni e lamentele ogni pochi giorni. Di sicuro avranno anche altri fini, ma il quadro complessivo è drammatico. 


Chissà se il Sindaco Lo Russo, il Presidente della Regione Cirio o il ministro della Giustizia Nordio se ne fregheranno altamente anche questa volta. Certo è che i detenuti e le detenute devono aver riconosciuta la loro dignità e molte volte trovano anche da soli il modo per farla rispettare, come successo nei giorni scorsi nel carcere Don Bosco di Pisa.

author: Equality Now
title: UNGA 2026 Reflections: Legal equality, feminist multilateralism, and the road ahead
content:
2nd October 2026


UNGA 2026 Reflections: Legal equality, feminist multilateralism, and the road ahead


12 min read


News and Insights


Achieve legal equality


Global


What you’ll read:


Despite pushback, many are firmly committed to gender equality

: in a climate of global conflict and anti-rights pushback, we saw evidence of real progress, genuine political will and concrete support for gender-equal laws and policies.


Multilateralism matters more than ever, and it must include women

: alongside a UN Secretary General race featuring more women candidates than ever, we saw Member States leaning into, not away from, both multilateralism itself, and the idea that women are central to its success.


Everyone benefits from equality, and everyone has a part to play

: we know that whole societies reap the rewards of gender equality, but we also know that getting there requires all hands on deck. From intergenerational leadership to multisectoral coalitions and unexpected alliances, only by working and persevering together can we make equality reality.


The state of gender equality at UNGA 2026 and what has changed since last year


Observing the world during the UN General Assembly (UNGA) 2026, one could be forgiven for having a pessimistic outlook: since

UNGA last year

, conflicts and humanitarian crises are rampant, and concerns about weakening multilateral institutions have grown, while anti-rights movements continue to target gender equality and human rights across regions. But such a dark view of the state of things can mean we lose sight of the actual  progress and positive change that is happening, despite such forces. 


Throughout this UNGA, again and again we saw evidence of political will for advancing gender equality among many Member States. They not only proudly announced laws they had reformed, but also actively shared best practices and emphasised the importance of going beyond legal frameworks to ensure implementation. 


For possibly the first time, we heard the phrase

“feminist multilateralism”

 used by governments, and saw how discussions surrounding multilateralism are evolving beyond individual national foreign policies into collective commitments, underscored by the historic UN Secretary-General race featuring more female candidates than male candidates – meaning there is a real possibility that the next Secretary-General of the UN could be the first woman to lead it since its founding in 1945.


Highlights and key takeaways


From equality in family law and nationality rights, to economic justice, digital rights and safety and the power of intergenerational leadership, the conversations Equality Now took part in and witnessed in and around UNGA were informative and energising.


                                        Legal equality front and centre


Multiple events provided opportunities to learn about

positive law reforms

, why they benefit all of society and how they were achieved. At the Equality in Law for Women and Girls by 2030: Renewing Global Leadership event we co-sponsored with

UN Women

, the

Inter-Parliamentary Union

 and the

Global Campaign for Equal Nationality Rights

, we heard from representatives of Azerbaijan, Malaysia, Serbia, Sierra Leone and Uganda about how they’ve made their laws more gender equal. Speakers emphasised the importance of cooperation between legislators and civil society, as well as affected people. As H.E. Mr. Sofian Akmal Abd Karim, Deputy Permanent Representative of Malaysia to the United Nations, said of the constitutional reform related to nationality law in his country, “We must also acknowledge the central and important role played by Malaysian mothers themselves. Their voices, experiences, and sustained engagement contributed significantly to the national conversation on this issue, and helped build momentum for change.” 

 

We look forward to answering the event’s Call to Action from the Presidents of the Inter-Parliamentary Union and the Global Campaign for Equal Nationality Rights, as well as Nyaradzayi Gumbonzvanda, Deputy Executive Director of UN Women, to make legal equality a reality for everyone.


At another event, together with the

World Bank

’s

Women, Business and the Law

 (WBL) division, we reiterated the connection between family law reform and economic equality – and how family law reforms benefit all of society.  This

joint event

 hosted at

APCO

 focused on our recent policy brief, coauthored by WBL …

Я замедлил с ответом моему любезному и учёному оппоненту из Conscientia. Для него это не будет иметь значения, а читатели легко простят мне задержку, видя, что в эти бурные моменты вопрос вовсе не является животрепещущим.

Тем не менее мне не кажется бесполезным попытаться внести ясность.

Г. г. из Conscientia оценил меня как обладающего «догматическим складом ума». Я ответил, и он возражает, говоря, что мой ответ подтверждает его мнение, будто у меня «сциентистский склад ума»[1]. Думает ли он, следовательно, что эти две противоположные характеристики означают одно и то же?

Я протестую против характеристики «догматик», потому что, будучи твёрдым и решительным в том, чего хочу, я всегда сомневаюсь в том, что знаю, и думаю, что, сколько бы усилий ни было приложено для понимания и объяснения Вселенной, до сих пор не достигнуто не только достоверности, но даже вероятности того, что наши знания достоверны, — и не знаю, сможет ли человеческий разум когда-либо это исправить.

Напротив, характеристика «научный склад ума» мне вовсе не неприятна, и я был бы польщён, если бы её заслужил; ибо научный склад ума — это тот, который ищет истину позитивным, рациональным и экспериментальным методом, никогда не обольщается мыслью, что нашёл абсолютную Истину, и довольствуется тем, что с трудом к ней приближается, открывая частичные истины, которые всегда считает предварительными и подлежащими пересмотру. Учёный, каким он, по моему мнению, должен быть, — это тот, кто исследует факты и делает из них логические выводы, какими бы они ни были, в противоположность тем, кто создаёт себе систему и затем ищет ей подтверждение в фактах, а чтобы найти его, бессознательно выбирает факты, которые им подходят, пренебрегая другими и, может быть, насилуя и искажая реальность, чтобы втиснуть её в тиски своих концепций. Он использует рабочие гипотезы, то есть делает предположения, которые служат ему руководством и стимулом в его исследованиях, но не остаётся жертвой своих фантазий, принимая, в силу привычки к ним, свои предположения за доказанные истины и обобщая и возводя в закон, с произвольной индукцией, каждый частный факт, который подходит к его тезису.

Сциентизм, который я отвергаю и который, вызванный и питаемый энтузиазмом, последовавшим за поистине изумительными открытиями, сделанными в ту пору в области физикохимии и естественной истории, господствовал над умами во второй половине прошлого века, — это вера в то, что наука есть всё и может всё; это принятие как окончательных истин, как догматов, каждого частичного открытия; это смешение Науки с Моралью, Силы в механическом смысле слова, которая есть сущность определяемая и измеримая, с моральными силами, Природы с Мыслью, естественного Закона с Волей. Он логически ведёт к фатализму, то есть к отрицанию воли и свободы.

Г. г. говорит, что следовало бы обсуждать мою статью фраза за фразой, что было бы слишком долго, и потому ограничивается тем, что ставит мне вопросы, чтобы я убедился, насколько его постановка проблем далека от моей. Я уже был убеждён; но вот:

Я говорил, что не верю в божественное происхождение Священного Писания, и он отвечает: Но что понимает Малатеста под Священным Писанием? Бумагу и печатные слова? Нет, я не дохожу до предположения, что г. г. верит, будто Предвечный Отец на горе Синай или где-либо ещё написал что-то на папирусе или в священных книгах; но верит ли он, да или нет, что Библия боговдохновенна, а не является собранием легенд и поэзии, чем-то вроде фольклора еврейского народа?

Что понимает Малатеста под божественным происхождением? Если под божественным он допускает то, что абсолютно, не эмпирично, то Малатеста признает, что по крайней мере сознание имеет божественное происхождение, поскольку оно позволяет ему, Малатесте …

title: "The School That Became a Grave": Jeremy Scahill on U.S Bombing of Minab, Killing 120+ Iranian Kids
content:
Drop Site News

 released a major investigation this week into the U.S. bombing of the Shajareh Tayyebeh children’s school in the Iranian city of Minab on February 28, the first day of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

Drop Site

 spoke to survivors, first responders, parents and witnesses in one of the most in-depth reports on the massacre to date. The bombing killed at least 156 people — 120 of the victims were children, 26 were teachers, and the rest were parents. A United Nations fact-finding mission recently concluded that the U.S. strike was a war crime, but the Trump administration has not yet even acknowledged U.S. responsibility.


“This was not a single bombing or collateral damage,” says

Drop Site News

’s Jeremy Scahill, lead author of the investigation. “There were at least two direct hits on a school packed with children … and a couple of hours after those initial hits, as first responders came, as parents came, the U.S. launches more strikes.”


Scahill points out that until 2013, the area where the school is was a facility operated by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps. But in satellite photos from just weeks before the strike, “You could see the murals on the wall. You could see the soccer field. Some of the satellite photos show shadows of tiny people playing outside.”

title: "Cruel & Torturous": Christa Pike in Critical Condition After Botched Tennessee Execution
content:
Tennessee’s Governor Bill Lee has halted executions for the remainder of the year after a death row prisoner survived two lethal injections on Wednesday. According to her lawyers, Christa Pike was still breathing after she was strapped to a gurney and injected with two syringes of pentobarbital in a botched execution that spanned more than two hours. Prior to the scheduled execution, Pike and her lawyers argued a single-dose lethal injection could be tantamount to torture due to Pike’s small veins. Pike was sentenced to death for a 1995 murder she committed when she was 18. Now in the hospital in critical condition, she is the first person to ever survive lethal injection in the United States.


“I have seen five executions in Tennessee,” says Steven Hale, a criminal justice reporter for the

Nashville Banner

, who witnessed Christa Pike’s botched execution. “And I’ve never seen anything like what we saw Wednesday night.”


Christa Pike “has just experienced the most agonizing attempt at lethal injection in the country’s history,” says Sandra Babcock, director of the Cornell Center on the Death Penalty Worldwide. Babcock says Pike should have never been sentenced to death, because she was an “immature 18-year-old” with a history of severe childhood and sexual trauma who “was not receiving medication for post-traumatic stress disorder and bipolar disorder at the time of [the murder], which she committed with her abusive boyfriend at the time.”

content:
Di seguito l’indizione del dibattito organizzato dai comitati e dai cittadini che si stanno attivando a Torino sul tema dei data center insieme all’

Assemblea Universitaria di Scienze di UniTo

.


DIBATTITO


MERCOLEDì 21 OTTOBRE ORE 17.30

–

DIPARTIMENTO DI FISICA, AULA C, VIA PIETRO GIURIA 1 – TORINO

.


Riteniamo che l’università possa avere un ruolo centrale in questo dibattito. La

comunità scientifica ha le competenze adatte a valutare da vicino gli aspetti tecnici

, sia della realizzazione dei data center

sia della valutazione del loro impatto sull’ambiente

: servono fisici per l’analisi termica, chimici per l’analisi degli agenti inquinanti, medici per valutarne gli effetti sulla salute e biologi per studiarne l’impatto sul territorio. Questi saperi devono essere messi a disposizione dei territori impattati da questi nuovi progetti.

Ma non solo: è proprio all’interno delle università, e in particolare nei poli STEM, che tecnologie come l’AI vengono sviluppate.

 


I data center assumono un ruolo importante in questa

fase di guerra

: possono essere obiettivo o strumento, così come l’energia

nucleare

 che viene sponsorizzata per risolvere il problema dell’enorme richiesta energetica che queste macchine impongono al territorio. Il governo parla di

“interesse strategico nazionale”

 in merito a queste grandi opere, eppure la proprietà dell’infrastruttura e dei dati è sovranazionale, essendo molto spesso i promotori le

Big Tech americane.

 A seguito di un’estate di

blackout

 e di

ondate di calore

 l’esplosione di progetti di data center anche in Piemonte è un paradosso da fermare immediatamente. 


Questo primo evento pubblico avrà l’obiettivo di

informare sugli impatti ambientali e sociali

 dei data center e di approfondire i

progetti

 che fanno capolino sul nostro territorio: da

Grugliasco

 a

Trino Vercellese

, da

Caselle

 a

Lucento

 fino al progetto hyperscale di

Moncalieri

 in modo da iniziare a creare

rete tra comitati, cittadini, universitari e esperti

 che vogliono opporsi a questi progetti che avranno un costo ingente per la nostra salute e per la nostra vivibilità sia in termini ecologici sia economici.

Enrico Duranti

, portavoce della Rete dei Comitati STOP Data Center Lombardia; 


Francesco Cappello

, fisico, Direttivo COMITATO NO GUERRA NO NATO, Vice presidente Associazione Per un mondo senza guerre;


Sergio Manera

Li gorî çavkaniyan, rêveberiyên Riyad û Dohayê fikar dikin ku di rewşa ji nû ve destpêkirina êrişên berfireh ên DYAyê yên li ser Îranê de, Tehran binesaziya wan a energiyê bike hedef.


Rêveberiya Trump di dawiya Tîrmehê de vebijêrkên êrişên berfireh ên li ser binesaziya enerjiyê ya Îranê nirxandibû. Têkildarî vê yekê, Mîrzayê Erebistana Siûdî Mihemed bin Selman di hevdîtina 1ê Tebaxê ya bi Trump re de fikarên xwe yên li ser zêdebûna rageşiyê aniye ziman û daxwaz kiriye ku ji êrişan dûr bisekine. Welatên herêmê ku Qeter jî di nav de ye di heman serdemê de bang li Washîngton û Tehranê kiribûn ku rageşiyê kêm bikin.


Trump di 2yê Tebaxê de diyar kir ku di muzakereyan de pêşketin çêbûye û êrişa ku dihat plan kirin, betal kir. Rêveberiya DYAyê di hefteyên dawî de zextên aborî û ambargoyên li ser Îranê zêde kirin.


Di şerê DYA-Îranê de rewşa dawî

Dîplomasî berdewam dike:

 Di serî de Qeter û Pakistan navbeynkar, ji bo peymana ku dê şer bi dawî bike û Tengava Hurmuzê ji nû ve veke bi aliyan re hevdîtinan dikin. Rêveberiya Tehranê ragihand ku bersiva fermî ji bo teklîfa wan a dawî ya peymanê hatiye dayîn, lêbelê naveroka bersivê bi raya giştî re parve nekir.


Trump rêya îhtimala êrişên nû vekirî hişt:

 Serokê DYAyê Trump got ku wan teklîfa dawî ya Îranê kêm dîtine û îhtimala zêdekirina bombebaranên li ser Îranê ya piştî hilbijartinên navberê ên 3ê Mijdarê yên DYAyê ji holê ranekir.


Riska li Hurmuzê berdewam dike:

 Şer, trafîka behrê ya di tengava krîtîk a ji bo bazirganiya enerjiyê ya cîhanê de bi awayekî cidî asteng kir. Navenda Operasyonên Bazirganiya Deryayî ya Brîtanyayê di 1ê Cotmehê de ragihand ku tiştekî ku çavkaniya wî nehat diyar kirin li tanker e ku di Tengava Hurmuzê re derbas dibû ketiye û agir bi tankerê ketiye. Zirar negiştiye karmendan û ti aliyekî berpirsiyarî negirt ser xwe.


DYA hebûna xwe ya leşkerî ya li herêmê zêde dike:

 Li gorî nûçeya APê ku navenda wê li DYAyê, rayedarekî DYAyî ê ku navê xwe nedaye, koma keştiya balafiran a Theodore Roosevelt û koma amfîbî ya Makin Island ber bi herêmê ve diçin. Ev tevgerana dikare bibe sedem ku ber bi dawiya Cotmehê ve sê keştiyên balafiran ên DYAyê di heman demê de li herêmê bin.


Bandorên aborî û sivîl girantir dibin:

 DYAyê di 1ê Cotmehê de ambargoyên nû anîn ser beşa otomotîv û rêhesinî ya Îranê. APê her wiha ragihand ku riyalê Îranê di dawiya Îlonê de ketiye asta xwe ya herî jêrîn a nû, bihayên dermanan bi lez zêde bûne û gihîştina hinek dermanan zihmettir bûye.
